question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. unemployment rate for September 2025 be initially reported as 4.4% or higher?
subquestions.background_information: In September 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) lowered the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 4.00%-4.25% (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm). As recent monetary policy decisions have demonstrated, the Fed is closely monitoring downside risks to the labor market; the August 2025 unemployment rate rose to 4.3% alongside significantly slowed job gains, prompting the initial rate cut (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm). Because the Fed's dual mandate requires balancing inflation with maximum employment, a continuing rise in the unemployment rate to 4.4% or higher would signal a deteriorating labor market, increasing the likelihood of aggressive policy actions such as a 50+ basis points rate cut at or before the January 2026 meeting. Tracking the September 2025 unemployment rate, typically released on the first Friday of October, provides a vital early indicator of whether the labor market is stabilizing or worsening. Sources: Federal Reserve Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm | BLS Employment Situation Summary: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm | FOMC Meeting Calendars: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) for September 2025 is initially reported as 4.4% or higher by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). This event must occur between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive). The primary resolution source will be the initial Employment Situation Summary news release for September 2025 published by the BLS (available at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm or the historical archive at https://www.bls.gov/bls/newsrels.htm). Only the headline, seasonally adjusted U-3 rate from the initial release for September 2025 will be used; any subsequent revisions or data updates will not affect the resolution. If the data release is postponed beyond the resolution window and does not occur by 2025-10-18, the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: The recent 25 basis point rate cut by the Federal Reserve in September 2025 was driven heavily by an unexpectedly weak labor market, highlighted by an August unemployment rate of 4.3%. A further increase in the September unemployment rate to 4.4% or above would strongly suggest that the U.S. labor market is continuing to cool, increasing the pressure on the FOMC to act aggressively and making a larger 50+ basis points cut at the January 2026 meeting highly probable. Conversely, if unemployment stabilizes or falls, the Fed will likely maintain a slower pace of rate cuts.

question: Trump declassifies UFO files in 2025?
description:

Announcements of declassifications that are not implemented within this market's timeframe will not count.

The primary resolution source for declassification will be official information from the government of the United States, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a US congressional committee or task force hold a public hearing primarily focused on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs) or UFO declassification between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
In August 2025, Representative Anna Paulina Luna, chair of the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, reiterated claims about 'interdimensional beings' and expressed her intent to secure public access to previously classified UAP information (https://www.hindustantimes.com). There is growing momentum for UAP transparency in Washington, with the Pentagon's All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) aiming to release more unclassified data (https://abcnews.go.com) and lawmakers floating proposals like the UAP Transparency Act to mandate disclosure (https://medium.com). Congress typically reconvenes in September following its August recess. A public congressional hearing focused on UAPs during this first month back would be a critical leading indicator of sustained legislative momentum. It would demonstrate coordinated pressure on the Trump administration to fulfill its promises of 'radical transparency' and actively declassify UAP files by the end of 2025.

Sources:
Hindustan Times: https://www.hindustantimes.com
ABC News: https://abcnews.go.com
Medium: https://medium.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if any official committee, subcommittee, or task force of the United States Congress (House or Senate) holds a public hearing where the primary stated topic relates to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs), Unidentified Flying Objects (UFOs), extraterrestrial intelligence, or the declassification of government records related to these phenomena, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

To qualify for a 'Yes' resolution:
1. The hearing must physically convene and take place within the specified time window (between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01). Announcements of future hearings do not qualify.
2. The hearing must be public (i.e., at least a portion of it must be accessible to the public and press). Entirely closed-door or classified briefings do not count.
3. The official title of the hearing or the main subject listed on its officially released agenda must explicitly include terms such as 'UAP', 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena', 'UFO', 'extraterrestrial', or 'non-human intelligence'.

Delayed Events: If a qualifying hearing is scheduled but postponed beyond 2025-10-01, it will not count towards resolution, and the question will resolve 'No'.

The primary resolution sources will be the official calendars of the US House of Representatives (https://docs.house.gov/Committee/Calendar/ByWeek.aspx) and the US Senate (https://www.senate.gov/committees/hearings_meetings.htm). Credible news reporting (e.g., from major outlets like AP News, Reuters, or ABC News) verifying that the hearing occurred will also be considered if official calendars are delayed or unavailable.
subquestions.rationale: A formal congressional hearing dedicated to UAPs or their declassification is a strong indicator of mounting legislative and public pressure on the executive branch. If Congress prioritizes this issue immediately after their August recess, it significantly increases the likelihood that the Trump administration will respond by declassifying files by the end of 2025. Conversely, a lack of legislative activity in September may suggest the topic is losing priority among lawmakers.

question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for August 2025 be reported at 4.4% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
The unemployment rate is a critical indicator of economic health and a key metric evaluated by the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) when determining recession timelines. As of earlier in 2025, the U.S. unemployment rate was recorded at 4.2%. Despite a Q1 2025 GDP contraction of 0.5%, Q2 GDP rebounded strongly to an estimated 3.3% growth. However, a significant component of recession forecasting hinges on labor market dynamics. The Sahm Rule, an empirical indicator of recessions, tracks upward momentum in the unemployment rate. A continued rise in unemployment to 4.4% or higher for August 2025 would signal substantial labor market cooling. This would indicate an increased probability of negative GDP growth in Q3 and Q4, or a broad economic decline prompting an NBER recession declaration in 2025.

Sources:
Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) Unemployment Rate: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that the headline, seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (U-3) for August 2025 is 4.4% or higher in its initial Employment Situation news release published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive). The resolution will be based strictly on the headline one-decimal figure (e.g., 4.4%) published in the initial release (typically found in the summary text and 'Table A. Major indicators of labor market activity, seasonally adjusted'). Subsequent revisions to this figure in later months will not affect the resolution. If the August 2025 Employment Situation report is delayed and not published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, this question will resolve as unresolvable. The official BLS Employment Situation release will be the primary source: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm.
subquestions.rationale: The NBER relies heavily on broad employment data to date recessions. Furthermore, a rising unemployment rate triggers the Sahm Rule, which correlates strongly with economic downturns. Identifying whether unemployment reaches 4.4% or higher in August acts as a leading crux for Q3 economic weakness, strongly updating forecasters' probabilities regarding a recession in 2025.

question: Will Max Verstappen be the 2025 Drivers Champion?
description:
This market will resolve according to the driver that finishes 1st in the driver standings for the 2025 F1 season. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

As soon as the results for the final scheduled race of the 2025 F1 season are known this market will resolve.

If at any point it becomes impossible for a listed driver to win the 2025 F1 Drivers Championship based on the rules of F1 (e.g., they are mathematically eliminated from contention), this market will resolve to “No”.

If the F1 season is permanently canceled or has not been completed by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Formula 1.

subquestions.question: Will Max Verstappen win at least one Formula 1 Grand Prix race between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Max Verstappen is the 2024 F1 Drivers' Champion and is currently chasing his fifth consecutive title. However, he has faced steep competition in the 2025 season from McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris. As of late September 2025, Verstappen was reported to be 69 points behind the championship leader, Oscar Piastri, with only seven rounds remaining. Despite this significant deficit, Red Bull has recently found renewed form, with Verstappen winning the late-season races at Monza and Baku (https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/after-baku-brilliance-heres-why-singapore-gp-is-key-for-max-verstappens-f1-title-hopes/10656600/). To close the 69-point gap in the final stages of the season and win the 2025 Drivers' Championship, Verstappen needs to consistently outscore his rivals and secure more race victories. This question focuses on whether his late-season momentum will carry through the critical October stretch of the calendar.

Sources:
Motorsport.com - After Baku brilliance, here's why Singapore GP is key for Max Verstappen's F1 title hopes: https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/after-baku-brilliance-heres-why-singapore-gp-is-key-for-max-verstappens-f1-title-hopes/10656600/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Max Verstappen is officially classified as finishing in 1st place in at least one official Formula 1 Grand Prix race that takes place between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive). The primary resolution source will be the official Formula 1 race results page (https://www.formula1.com/en/results.html). The date of the race will be determined by the local start time of the event. 

Sprint races, qualifying sessions, and any other non-Grand Prix events do not count towards this resolution. A Grand Prix is defined as the main race event typically held on a Sunday. If no Formula 1 Grand Prix races are held during the specified window, or if Verstappen does not win any of the Grand Prix races held, the question resolves No. 

If a race initially scheduled within this window is postponed to a date after 2025-10-31, its results will not count towards this resolution. Post-race penalties applied before the official publication of results by the FIA will count, but subsequent long-term appeals altering the race results after November 7, 2025, will not be considered.
subquestions.rationale: Verstappen faces a steep 69-point deficit to the championship leader with only 7 races remaining. To mount a realistic comeback and secure the ultimate championship, he must maintain his recent winning form (from Monza and Baku) into the October schedule. Securing at least one Grand Prix victory in October would serve as a powerful indicator that Red Bull's recent car upgrades are effective across different track profiles, substantially increasing his probability of winning the overall title.

question: US strikes Iran by June 30, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US Department of Defense confirm the death of at least one US military service member due to hostile action in the CENTCOM area of responsibility between December 23, 2025, and January 22, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between the United States and Iran have remained exceptionally high following a severe military escalation in June 2025, during which the US and Israel conducted airstrikes on Iranian nuclear facilities, and Iran retaliated with strikes against a US base in Qatar. A ceasefire was brokered on June 24, 2025, but the security situation remains volatile. Recent events have underscored this instability, with Iran conducting extensive military drills in the Persian Gulf in December 2025, showcasing its missile and drone capabilities (https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf). Furthermore, Iran's suspension of IAEA cooperation and warnings of radioactive leaks at struck facilities have stalled diplomatic progress (https://en.trend.az/world/other/3345123.html). Throughout the region, Iranian-backed militias frequently target US forces. For example, in January 2024, an Iranian-backed drone strike on the Tower 22 outpost in Jordan killed three US service members, prompting significant US retaliatory strikes (https://zeenews.india.com/world/the-night-american-pilots-became-israels-shield-against-iran-2790312.html). Any new fatal attack on US personnel by Iranian proxies or Iranian forces would dramatically increase the likelihood of direct US military retaliation against Iranian soil. This question asks whether any US service members will be killed by hostile action in the Middle East during the specified period, which would serve as a critical leading indicator for a potential US strike on Iran.

Sources:
The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/iran-holds-drills-in-gulf
Trend News Agency: https://en.trend.az/world/other/3345123.html
Zee News: https://zeenews.india.com/world/the-night-american-pilots-became-israels-shield-against-iran-2790312.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the United States Department of Defense (DoD) officially confirms the death of at least one active-duty US military service member as a direct result of hostile action occurring within the US Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility (AOR) between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22 (inclusive).

The death must be officially attributed to hostile action (e.g., enemy fire, drone strikes, missile attacks, IEDs) by the DoD in a formal press release or casualty report available on the official DoD website (https://www.defense.gov/News/Casualty-Status/ or https://www.defense.gov/News/Releases/). Deaths resulting solely from accidents, illness, self-inflicted injuries, or non-hostile causes will not count toward a Yes resolution.

The hostile event causing the fatality must occur between 2025-12-23 and 2026-01-22, inclusive. If the attack occurs during this window but the service member succumbs to their injuries after 2026-01-22 (but before the resolution of this question on 2026-02-01), it will still count as a Yes, provided the DoD attributes the death to the hostile action that occurred within the specified timeframe.

The CENTCOM AOR includes countries in the Middle East, Central Asia, and parts of South Asia (such as Iraq, Syria, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Yemen, etc., and surrounding waters like the Persian Gulf and Red Sea).

If no such death is confirmed by the DoD by February 1, 2026, the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A fatal attack on US forces by Iran or its proxy groups is one of the clearest tripwires for US military retaliation. In the past, the US has struck proxy targets or engaged in limited direct action when US service members were killed (e.g., following the Tower 22 attack). Given the recent direct exchanges of fire between the US and Iran in June 2025, any further loss of American life in the region would heavily pressure the US government to conduct strikes on Iranian territory to reestablish deterrence, making it a highly informative crux for the ultimate question.

question: Will Trump meet with Xi Jinping by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump meets with Xi Jinping between July 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An exchange of words, handshake, direct conversation, or other clear personal interaction between the named individuals will qualify as a meeting. Merely standing in proximity, making eye contact, or being present in the same room or event without direct interaction will not qualify.

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the US or Chinese government officially announce a planned in-person meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information: US-China trade talks resumed in Stockholm in late July 2025, with negotiators aiming to extend a 90-day tariff truce that was originally set to expire in mid-August (https://www.marketscreener.com). According to analysts, an extension of the truce would prevent new tariffs and pave the way for an in-person meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later in the year, potentially in late October or November (https://www.indiatoday.in). Given the massive logistical and diplomatic preparation required for a bilateral summit between the US and Chinese leaders, such an event is typically announced weeks in advance by either the White House or the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Thus, an official announcement by October 1 would serve as a strong early indicator of whether a meeting will materialize by the end of October. Sources: Market Screener - https://www.marketscreener.com | India Today - https://www.indiatoday.in
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if an official announcement confirming a scheduled in-person meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). To qualify, the announcement must be made by the White House, the US Department of State, or the Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) via an official press release, a formal statement published on their website, or an on-the-record public statement by an official spokesperson or the leaders themselves. The announcement must clearly state that an in-person meeting has been agreed upon. Statements that merely express a desire to meet, indicate that a meeting is being 'explored', or rely solely on anonymous media reports will not count toward resolution. The planned date of the meeting does not need to be before October 31; the question resolves based entirely on whether the confirmation is announced within the specified window. If no such official announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. If an official press conference or scheduled announcement event intended to confirm the meeting is explicitly postponed beyond the resolution window, the question should be considered unresolvable and canceled. Resolution Sources: White House Briefing Room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/ | US Department of State Press Releases: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/ | Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China: https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/
subquestions.rationale: An official announcement of a meeting is a necessary precursor to a highly-choreographed US-China presidential summit. If an announcement occurs before October 1, it significantly increases the likelihood that a meeting will take place by the ultimate question's October 31 deadline. Conversely, the lack of an announcement strongly implies that no meeting is imminent, heavily updating the probability of the ultimate question toward No.

question: Will Artificial Intelligence be TIME's Person of the Year for 2025?
description:
If listed person/thing is named as TIME's Person of the Year for 2025, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve to "Yes" if listed person is named TIME's Person of the Year either alone or in conjunction with any other person or thing which is not named in this market, so long as the term is explicitly named. 

For example, if the Person of the Year is "Donald Trump and the MAGA movement", this would qualify to resolve this market to “Trump”. However if the Person of the Year is "The MAGA movement", this would not qualify to resolve this market to “Trump” regardless of whether Trump is depicted on the cover. 

If two or more people or things which are named in this market are named TIME's Person of the Year, this market will resolve in favor of whichever person or thing is listed first. For example if TIME's Person of the Year is “Joe Biden and Kamala Harris”, the market for Joe Biden would resolve to “Yes” and the market for Kamala Harris would resolve to “No”. 

This market will resolve based on Time's cover. Other Time webpages which differ from the cover will not be considered.

This market can resolve after the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is announced by TIME magazine. If for any reason the 2025 TIME's Person of the Year is not announced by January 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: this event is mutually exclusive.

subquestions.question: Will worldwide search interest for the topic 'Artificial Intelligence' reach a 5-year peak (score of 100) on Google Trends during any week ending between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
TIME's Person of the Year is heavily influenced by the cultural zeitgeist, global public attention, and the sheer magnitude of a subject's impact on the news cycle. In 2025, Artificial Intelligence has remained a central global focus, underscored by the release of the TIME100 AI 2025 list in late August and massive geopolitical developments, such as the US White House's announcement of a $1.4 trillion American AI infrastructure investment. Public search interest serves as a highly reliable, quantitative proxy for this cultural dominance. If global search interest for 'Artificial Intelligence' hits a new 5-year maximum (achieving a score of 100 on Google Trends) during the critical fall period, it will signal unprecedented public engagement. This would strongly elevate AI's status as the most influential entity of the year just as TIME editors are beginning their final deliberations, significantly increasing its chances of being named TIME's Person of the Year over competing high-profile political figures.

Sources:
Google Trends: https://trends.google.com/trends/
TIME100 AI List Coverage: https://time.com/collection/time100-ai/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if the worldwide Google Trends score for the topic 'Artificial Intelligence' reaches exactly 100 for any weekly data point whose date range ends between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

To determine the resolution, the resolver will access Google Trends (https://trends.google.com/trends/) between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-06 to allow all data for September to fully populate. The resolver must apply the following exact parameters:
1. Search term: 'Artificial intelligence' (select the 'Topic' classification, not 'Search term').
2. Location: 'Worldwide'.
3. Time range: 'Past 5 years'.
4. Category: 'All categories'.
5. Search Type: 'Web Search'.

The resolver will then examine the data graph. Google Trends will display weekly data points over the 5-year window. The resolver will check all data points where the end date of the week falls between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. If any of these specific weeks displays a relative score of 100, the question resolves 'Yes'. If all weeks ending within this window show a score strictly less than 100, the question resolves 'No'. If Google Trends data becomes permanently unavailable or the platform undergoes a fundamental change that removes this capability before resolution, the question resolves as 'Unresolvable'.
subquestions.rationale: TIME's Person of the Year selection correlates strongly with what dominates the public consciousness late in the year. Reaching a 5-year peak in global search interest during September would serve as empirical proof that AI is capturing more public attention than at any point during its recent massive booms (including the initial ChatGPT launch), making it a highly informative indicator that AI has the momentum required to secure the title.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will either the United States Armed Forces or the Venezuelan military fire warning shots at the other's vessels or aircraft between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between the United States and Venezuela have sharply escalated following the U.S. deployment of a major naval task force to the Caribbean. The U.S. currently has over 4,500 personnel in the Southern Caribbean, supported by three destroyers, two landing-dock ships, an amphibious assault ship, a littoral combat ship, and the guided-missile cruiser USS Lake Erie. U.S. warships carry Coast Guard detachments tasked with drug interdiction operations and making arrests (https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-crosses-panama-canal-trumps-caribbean-buildup-continues). In response to the U.S. military presence, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro has ordered the deployment of 4.5 million members of the Bolivarian Militia, while Defense Minister Vladimir Padrino announced 'significant' deployments of drones, warships, and larger vessels to patrol territorial waters (https://www.news24.com/news24/world/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-to-confront-us-destroyers-submarines). The close proximity of heavily armed forces performing overlapping patrols and interdiction missions greatly increases the risk of a confrontation. The firing of warning shots is a standard naval de-escalation or signaling tactic used before lethal force is applied, and serves as an excellent early indicator of escalating hostilities.

Sources:
Newsweek - USS Lake Erie crosses Panama Canal as Trump's Caribbean buildup continues: https://www.newsweek.com/uss-lake-erie-crosses-panama-canal-trumps-caribbean-buildup-continues
News24 - Venezuela deploys warships, drones to confront US destroyers, submarines: https://www.news24.com/news24/world/news/venezuela-deploys-warships-drones-to-confront-us-destroyers-submarines
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if there is a consensus of credible reporting or official government confirmation that either the United States Armed Forces (including the U.S. Coast Guard) or the Venezuelan military (including the FANB, Venezuelan Coast Guard, or Bolivarian Militia) fired warning shots at, or in the immediate vicinity of, a vessel or aircraft operated by the other country between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

- 'Warning shots' are defined as the intentional discharge of a weapon (e.g., deck guns, machine guns, artillery, or missiles) intended to signal a warning, demand compliance, or deter an adversary, without the intent to strike, damage, or destroy the target.
- The shots must be directed near a state-operated military, militia, or coast guard vessel/aircraft belonging to the US or Venezuela. Warning shots fired exclusively at civilian smuggling vessels, unidentified narco-submarines, or commercial shipping will not count toward a 'Yes' resolution unless a state-operated vessel is directly involved as the target.
- If a military engagement occurs involving the use of destructive force (which would trigger the ultimate question), this subquestion will still resolve 'Yes' if credible reports indicate that warning shots were fired as a precursor during an incident within the specified time window.

Resolution will be based on official press releases from the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/), U.S. Southern Command (https://www.southcom.mil/), the Venezuelan Ministry of Popular Power for Defense (http://www.mindefensa.gob.ve/), or a consensus of credible mainstream media reporting (such as Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/ or Associated Press: https://apnews.com/). If no such event is reported to have occurred between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question explicitly excludes 'non-violent actions, such as warning shots' from its definition of a military engagement. Consequently, asking whether warning shots will be fired acts as a perfect subquestion: it tracks a measurable, distinct event that falls strictly short of the ultimate resolution criteria, yet acts as a severe escalation and a profound indicator that the two militaries are in direct tactical friction. Forecasters who expect an actual military engagement by late October would likely expect warning shots to occur beforehand, making this a strong crux.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by October 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla officially open its Austin, Texas Robotaxi service to the general public between September 1, 2025 and September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla has been operating a pilot Robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, since June 2025. Currently, this service is restricted to an invite-only group of testers and requires a safety monitor in the vehicle. In August 2025, CEO Elon Musk and Tesla indicated that the Austin Robotaxi service would be rolled out to the general public in September 2025. 

Opening the service to the general public is a critical intermediate milestone for Tesla's autonomous ride-hailing ambitions. For the ultimate question of whether Tesla will launch a fully driverless Robotaxi service by October 31, 2025, observing whether Tesla meets its near-term September rollout goal will provide strong evidence regarding the company's development timeline and operational momentum. If the service opens early in September, it suggests Tesla is executing rapidly; if it is delayed, it casts doubt on the strict October 31 timeline for an even more advanced (fully driverless) launch.

Sources:
GuruFocus - Barclays Expects Long Approval Process for Tesla's (TSLA) Robotaxi: https://www.gurufocus.com
Tesla North - Tesla Hints at Chicago Robotaxi Launch with New Job Listings: https://teslanorth.com
NewsBytes - Musk confirms Tesla robotaxi rollout for the public in September: https://www.newsbytesapp.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive), Tesla officially announces that its Robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, has been opened to the general public, or if the service concretely becomes available to the general public in Austin within this time window. 

"General public" is defined as individuals who are not Tesla employees, contractors, or part of a specifically invited closed-beta/early-access group, meaning any ordinary user in the operational area can download the app (or use the existing Tesla app) and summon a Robotaxi ride. The presence of a safety monitor in the vehicle does not preclude a Yes resolution for this subquestion, as long as the service is openly available to the public. 

The resolution will be based on official communications from Tesla, such as its official press releases (https://ir.tesla.com/#tab-press-releases), the Tesla blog (https://www.tesla.com/blog), or statements from the official Tesla X account (https://x.com/Tesla) / Elon Musk's official X account (https://x.com/elonmusk). Corroboration from credible technology and automotive news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, The Verge, Electrek) reporting that public rides are actively being offered will also suffice for a Yes resolution. 

If no such public rollout occurs or is announced between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 at 11:59 PM ET, the question will resolve No. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Tesla has publicly targeted September 2025 for opening its Austin Robotaxi pilot to the general public. Tracking whether they achieve this in the first week of September serves as a highly informative crux. If they cannot hit this intermediate milestone early in the month, it significantly lowers the probability that they will achieve the much harder milestone of a fully driverless (no safety monitor) service by October 31.

question: OpenAI browser by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if OpenAI publicly releases a standalone web browser that is intended for general web browsing and is available for use by the public in at least one country or region by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes," such a browser must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling free waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by OpenAI as being accessible to the general public.

Browser extensions, plugins, or integrations within third-party browsers do not count; it must be a standalone browser application.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from OpenAI. If there is ambiguity, a consensus of credible reporting will be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce or open a closed beta/waitlist for a standalone web browser between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
OpenAI has been rapidly expanding its product ecosystem, with recent launches including the gpt-realtime speech-to-speech model and Codex IDE integrations (https://www.winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent/). The AI browser space is heating up, with competitors like Anthropic rolling out closed-beta browser extensions for Claude (https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/) and Perplexity launching its 'Comet' browser. Furthermore, Windows Central recently noted 'OpenAI's rumored project' in the context of emerging AI browsers (https://www.windowscentral.com/let-me-scam-that-for-you). For OpenAI to meet the October 31, 2025 deadline of publicly releasing a standalone web browser (general availability or open beta), it is standard industry practice to first announce the project or open a closed beta/waitlist to a limited group of users. This subquestion tracks whether OpenAI takes this preliminary step by October 1, 2025.

Sources:
Winbuzzer: https://www.winbuzzer.com/2025/08/28/openai-supercharges-codex-ai-coding-agent/
ZDNet: https://www.zdnet.com/article/anthropics-claude-chrome-browser-extension-rolls-out-how-to-get-early-access/
Windows Central: https://www.windowscentral.com/let-me-scam-that-for-you
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if OpenAI officially announces the development of a standalone web browser, OR opens a closed beta, private preview, or waitlist for a standalone web browser, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET (inclusive).

To qualify:
1. The announcement or waitlist must be published on an official OpenAI channel, such as the OpenAI News/Blog (https://openai.com/news), the official OpenAI X/Twitter account (https://x.com/OpenAI), or the X/Twitter account of CEO Sam Altman (https://x.com/sama).
2. The product must be explicitly described as a "standalone web browser" (a dedicated desktop or mobile application for general web browsing), not a browser extension, plugin, or an in-app browser within the existing ChatGPT client.
3. If OpenAI bypasses a closed testing phase and directly releases the browser to the public (open beta or general availability) during this timeframe, this question also resolves Yes.

If no such announcement or testing phase is officially initiated by OpenAI between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves No. Any events, announcements, or leaks occurring after 2025-10-01 11:59 PM ET will not count toward a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A standalone web browser is a major product release. Software companies typically announce such products, or open closed betas and waitlists, weeks or months prior to a full public or open-beta launch. If OpenAI officially announces the browser or opens a closed beta by October 1, it significantly increases the probability that a public release or open beta will occur by the October 31 deadline. Conversely, if no announcement or private beta is seen by October 1, the likelihood of a surprise public launch by October 31 drops considerably.

question: Will Iran close the Strait of Hormuz before 2027?
description:
If Iran halts or severely restricts international maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official governmental information, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will UKMTO or US NAVCENT report that Iranian forces have seized or detained at least one commercial vessel in or near the Strait of Hormuz between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06?
subquestions.background_information:
Following US strikes on Iranian nuclear sites, Iran's parliament approved a measure to close the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway that handles approximately 20% of global daily oil consumption. The final decision rests with Iran's Supreme National Security Council. Amid these escalating tensions, former Iranian officials have threatened to restrict traffic, and there are reports of increased Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) naval activity and GPS jamming in the region. Historically, Iran has used the harassment and seizure of commercial vessels as leverage and as a retaliatory measure. An actual seizure of an international commercial vessel by the IRGC or Iranian Navy during this period would serve as a strong leading indicator that Iran is actively escalating towards a de facto or formal closure of the strait.

Sources:
What if Iran tries to close the Strait of Hormuz? - https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/what-if-iran-tries-to-close-the-strait-of-hormuz
Iran approves closure of oil corridor, Strait of Hormuz, after US strikes: Report - https://www.indiatoday.in/world/story/iran-approves-closure-of-oil-corridor-strait-of-hormuz-after-us-strikes-report-2556637-2025-06-22
Strait of Hormuz Disruption Fears Surge After Former Iranian Minister Threatens Transit Restrictions - https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/strait-hormuz-disruption-fears-surge-after-former-iranian-minister-threatens-transit
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-06 and 2025-12-06 (inclusive), the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) or the US Naval Forces Central Command (NAVCENT) / US 5th Fleet officially reports that Iranian forces (such as the IRGC Navy or the Islamic Republic of Iran Navy) have seized, detained, or forcibly diverted at least one international commercial vessel (e.g., oil tanker, container ship, or bulk carrier) in the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf, or the Gulf of Oman.

The incident must occur and be officially reported within the specified time window (2025-11-06 to 2025-12-06).

Resolution will be based on official reports, warnings, or press releases from:
- UKMTO (https://www.ukmto.org/)
- US NAVCENT / 5th Fleet (https://www.cusnc.navy.mil/)

Edge cases:
- Temporary boardings where Iranian forces depart and the vessel is permitted to continue its voyage on the same day without being diverted to Iranian territorial waters for detention do not count.
- 'Commercial vessel' excludes military vessels, state-owned warships, or small local fishing dhows; it must be an internationally recognized cargo, tanker, or merchant vessel.
- If the event is reported by credible news outlets but not confirmed by UKMTO or NAVCENT by the end of the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A vessel seizure by Iranian forces is a distinct, observable tactical event that demonstrates Iran's willingness to use physical force to disrupt maritime traffic. If Iran begins seizing vessels, major shipping and oil companies will likely halt transits, effectively leading to a closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Therefore, this serves as a highly informative, early proxy for the ultimate question.

question: Will Wicked: For Good be the top grossing movie of 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the "Gross" column on https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses shows 'Wicked: For Good' (2025) as the film with the highest 2025 gross once data for December 31 is made available. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: This market is about the movie's domestic calendar gross in 2025 - dates outside of 2025 will not count toward this movie's gross.

In the event of an exact tie the film that comes first alphabetically will be considered the winner.

If there is no final data available by January 7, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, another credible resolution source will be chosen.

subquestions.question: Will any film record a domestic gross of $500 million or more on the Box Office Mojo 2025 calendar grosses chart by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The ultimate question asks whether 'Wicked: For Good', scheduled for release on November 21, 2025, will be the highest-grossing domestic film of 2025. The original 'Wicked' film grossed roughly $756 million worldwide and was pushing toward the $500 million milestone at the domestic box office. For 'Wicked: For Good' to become the top-grossing film of 2025, it will have to out-earn every other movie released during the year. Knowing whether any 2025 release has already crossed the $500 million mark domestically by the beginning of October serves as a critical indicator, as it sets the concrete baseline that 'Wicked: For Good' must surpass. Tracking the top gross of the year leading into Q4 provides an observable hurdle. Sources: [1] Comicbook: Prime Video Just Added One of the Biggest Movies of 2024 (https://comicbook.com), [2] Pinkvilla: Box Office: Wicked returns to theaters for one night (https://www.pinkvilla.com), [3] Box Office Mojo 2025 Calendar Grosses (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the 'Gross' column for any film on the Box Office Mojo 2025 Calendar Grosses page (https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/2025/?grossesOption=calendarGrosses) shows a value of $500,000,000 or greater. The resolution will be based on data available on the page at any time during this window. Snapshots from the Internet Archive (https://web.archive.org) taken between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 may be used to verify the gross if the page changes or is unavailable. If no film reaches or exceeds a gross of $500,000,000 within this timeframe, the question resolves No. If the site alters its formatting, the equivalent domestic cumulative gross metric for the calendar year 2025 will be used.
subquestions.rationale: If an existing 2025 release has already accumulated $500 million at the domestic box office by October 1, 2025, it establishes a substantial financial hurdle that 'Wicked: For Good' must overcome. Given that the first 'Wicked' film maxed out near $500 million domestically, a requirement for the sequel to significantly exceed this figure just to rank first would decrease the likelihood of the ultimate question resolving Yes.

question: Israel and Saudi Arabia normalize relations in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia officially announce the establishment of diplomatic relations between Janaury 26, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Israel and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will an official, publicly acknowledged in-person meeting take place between a cabinet-level or higher official from Israel and a cabinet-level or higher official from Saudi Arabia before October 2, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Saudi Arabia has officially maintained that normalization of relations with Israel is contingent on an end to the war in Gaza and the establishment of a Palestinian state. Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan has publicly stressed that without meaningful progress on a two-state solution, normalization talks cannot proceed. Concurrently, U.S. diplomatic efforts have pushed heavily for an expansion of the Abraham Accords. The UN General Assembly, held every September in New York, traditionally provides a prime venue for high-level diplomatic engagements and backchannel meetings. If Israel and Saudi Arabia are genuinely on track to officially normalize relations by the end of 2025, observable high-level diplomatic steps—such as direct meetings between foreign ministers or state leaders—are highly likely to occur in the preceding months. 

Sources:
Saudi Press Agency: https://www.spa.gov.sa/en
U.S. Department of State - Abraham Accords: https://www.state.gov/the-abraham-accords/
Reuters Middle East: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), a publicly acknowledged in-person meeting takes place between at least one cabinet-level official, head of government, or head of state representing Israel and a counterpart or cabinet-level/higher official representing Saudi Arabia.

- "Cabinet-level or higher" includes roles such as Prime Minister, Crown Prince, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Minister of Defense, etc.
- The meeting must be explicitly scheduled or acknowledged as a bilateral or trilateral (e.g., brokered by the U.S.) meeting. 
- Passing encounters, unacknowledged brief handshakes, or simply being in the same room at a multilateral summit without a dedicated sit-down meeting do not count.
- The occurrence of the meeting must be confirmed by official government sources from Israel (https://www.gov.il/en), Saudi Arabia (https://www.spa.gov.sa/en), or the United States (https://www.state.gov), or by a consensus of credible reporting from major news agencies such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/) or the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/hub/middle-east).
- If a meeting is scheduled but postponed beyond the resolution window, it does not count.
- If no qualifying meeting is confirmed to have occurred during the resolution window of 2025-09-01 through 2025-10-01, the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: For normalization to be formalized in 2025, preliminary high-level meetings are necessary to hammer out complex conditions, such as U.S. security guarantees, Palestinian concessions, and civil nuclear agreements. The September UN General Assembly window is a crucial indicator. If high-ranking officials from both nations are willing to be seen meeting publicly by October 1, it demonstrates substantial momentum toward a deal, strongly updating the ultimate question toward 'Yes'. A lack of such meetings would indicate negotiations remain stalled over red-line issues, significantly dragging down the likelihood of a 2025 normalization.

question: Israel x Hamas ceasefire before 2026?
description:
On March 17, Israel announced extensive strikes on terror targets belonging to the Hamas terrorist organization in the Gaza Strip ending a previous ceasefire agreement which had been agreed on January 15 (See: https://x.com/IDF/status/1901802698237935705).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement, between Israel and Hamas between March 19, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of whether the ceasefire officially starts afterwards.

An announced agreement to reinstate the previous agreed upon January 15th ceasefire deal will qualify.

Any form of informal agreement will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses will not count toward the resolution of this market.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Israel and Hamas, however a wide consensus of credible media reporting stating an official ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas has been reached will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will an official Israeli delegation travel to Doha, Qatar, or Cairo, Egypt, for ceasefire or hostage negotiations between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 18, 2025, Hamas reportedly approved a 60-day temporary ceasefire proposal mediated by Egypt and Qatar, based on a framework previously presented by US mediators (https://egyptianstreets.com). However, as of late August, Israel had not formally responded to this acceptance. Instead, reports indicated that Israel's security cabinet was convening on August 31 to review plans for a major military offensive to seize control of Gaza City, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu deliberately keeping the ceasefire deal off the formal agenda (https://abc17news.com). Furthermore, Israeli officials stated that Israel and the US have shifted toward backing a comprehensive plan to end the war, moving away from partial or temporary deals (https://www.timesofisrael.com). Sending a high-level delegation to Cairo or Doha would signify that Israel is returning to active, mediated negotiations and strongly exploring the proposed frameworks. If Israel continues to boycott such talks to focus on the Gaza City offensive, the prospects of an overarching ceasefire agreement before 2026 will diminish significantly.

Sources:
Egyptian Streets - https://egyptianstreets.com
ABC17NEWS - https://abc17news.com
The Times of Israel - https://www.timesofisrael.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if credible media reporting (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Axios, The Times of Israel) or official government statements confirm that an official Israeli delegation traveled to Doha, Qatar, or Cairo, Egypt, to engage in Gaza ceasefire or hostage release negotiations between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

An 'official Israeli delegation' is defined as a group of authorized government representatives, which must include high-level officials such as the Director of Mossad, the Director of Shin Bet, or formal envoys explicitly appointed by the Prime Minister's Office or the Ministry of Defense for this purpose.

The physical presence of the delegation in Doha or Cairo for the purpose of negotiations must occur at least partially between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). Virtual meetings or phone calls do not count toward resolution; physical travel to either city is strictly required. If a delegation travels but the visit is exclusively unrelated to the Gaza conflict (e.g., routine bilateral economic or security discussions), it will not qualify.

If no such travel is reported to have occurred within the specified window by 2025-10-01 at 23:59 UTC, the question resolves 'No'. Resolvers will primarily consult international news wires such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) and AP News (https://apnews.com) for definitive reports.
subquestions.rationale: Direct, in-person participation by an Israeli delegation in regional talks is a necessary leading indicator of an eventual official ceasefire agreement. Given the reported reluctance of Israel's Prime Minister to prioritize negotiations over a looming Gaza City offensive, the dispatch of a delegation would show renewed commitment to a negotiated track. Conversely, the failure to send a delegation within this critical one-month window would suggest an extended phase of military escalation, substantially reducing the likelihood of a formal ceasefire agreement.

question: Will James Talarico be the Democratic nominee for Senate in Texas?

If no 2026 Texas Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Texas Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

subquestions.question: Will U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett be officially listed as a filed candidate for the 2026 Texas Democratic Senate Primary by December 9, 2025?

However, the field might become more crowded. As of early November 2025, U.S. Rep. Jasmine Crockett is reportedly considering entering the primary, with her decision hinging on polling results. The Dallas Morning News: https://www.dallasnews.com/news/politics/2025/10/28/james-talarico-targets-rival-colin-allreds-home-turf-in-senate-primary-fight/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, at any point between 2025-11-13 and 2025-12-09 (inclusive), U.S. Representative Jasmine Crockett is officially listed as a filed candidate for the United States Senate in the 2026 Texas Democratic Primary. subquestions.rationale: The candidate filing deadline is December 8, 2025. Jasmine Crockett's potential entry into the primary would dramatically change the competitive landscape. As a prominent progressive from Dallas, she would likely draw voters and endorsements that might otherwise go to Talarico or Allred, significantly affecting Talarico's probability of becoming the nominee. Knowing whether she officially files is a critical early indicator of Talarico's path to victory.

question: Will Gemini 3.0 be released by October 31?
description:

subquestions.question: Will Google officially announce or publish a technical report for 'Gemini 3.0' between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information: Google has maintained a rapid pace of AI development, recently releasing models in the Gemini 2.5 series, including Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image, to users in August 2025. Conversely, a lack of any official mention by October 1 would indicate that Google might not be ready for a public rollout within the following 30 days, decreasing the likelihood of a Yes resolution for the ultimate question.

question: Will the U.S. invade Venezuela by December 31, 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the United States commences a military offensive intended to establish control over any portion of Venezuela between September 6 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. military conduct a kinetic strike on the sovereign land territory of Venezuela between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06?
subquestions.background_information:
As of early October 2025, tensions between the United States and Venezuela have sharply escalated. The U.S. administration declared a 'non-international armed conflict' targeting Latin American drug cartels and conducted lethal strikes on suspected narcotrafficking boats in the Caribbean Sea. According to reports, the Pentagon has deployed significant military forces near Venezuela, including F-35 jets and the 22nd Marine Expeditionary Unit, and has even drafted plans that include seizing ports and airfields (https://www.the-sun.com/). In response, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro declared a nationwide 'state of external emergency,' putting the armed forces on a wartime footing and repositioning air defense systems to protect infrastructure (https://www.defenseworld.net/). The U.S. strikes so far have been restricted to maritime targets (https://tass.com/). Expanding military operations from international or territorial waters to direct kinetic strikes on Venezuelan land territory would indicate a profound escalation in the conflict.

Sources:
Defense World: https://www.defenseworld.net/
The US Sun: https://www.the-sun.com/
TASS: https://tass.com/
AP News: https://apnews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/) officially confirms, or if there is a consensus of credible independent reporting from major news agencies such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/) and the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/), that the United States military intentionally conducted a kinetic attack (such as an airstrike, missile strike, artillery fire, or naval bombardment) that physically impacted the sovereign land territory of Venezuela between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06 (inclusive).

The strike must hit a target on land (e.g., a port facility, airfield, military base, or land vehicle). Strikes exclusively targeting maritime vessels at sea, even if within Venezuelan territorial waters, do not qualify for a Yes resolution unless the strike also damages land-based infrastructure. Cyberattacks, electronic warfare, or intercepted projectiles that do not impact the land territory do not count. The action must be intentional and not an accidental misfire. If no such event occurs and is confirmed to have occurred during the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A kinetic strike on Venezuelan land would represent a major escalation from the ongoing maritime counter-narcotics operations. Because the ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will invade to establish control over parts of Venezuela, an invasion would almost certainly be preceded by or begin with strikes on land-based air defenses, ports, and military installations. If the U.S. shows the willingness to strike Venezuelan soil in this timeframe, the probability of a broader invasion before December 31, 2025, increases dramatically.

question: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia in 2025?
description:

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

Only Ukraine’s signature is required; Russia’s signature or ratification is not.

Localized, temporary, or issue-specific arrangements—such as airstrike-limitation or deconfliction protocols, humanitarian pauses, evacuation corridors, prisoner-exchange or trade/export arrangements, border/DMZ adjustments, or ceasefires limited to a particular sector/front/municipality—will not qualify.

The document must bear a wet-ink or officially issued electronic signature of an authorized Ukrainian representative. Unsigned agreements (e.g., the 2023 Ohrid arrangement) will not qualify regardless of if they are otherwise officially enacted. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will a direct call or meeting between the President of Ukraine and the President of Russia take place or be officially announced between October 1, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent diplomatic momentum has increased following a US-Russia summit in Alaska involving US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, where the war in Ukraine was a central topic. According to reports from August 2025, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that President Putin is 'ready to meet' with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, provided that high-level issues are prepared in advance and concerns regarding Zelensky's legal legitimacy (following the expiration of his presidential term in May 2024) are addressed. Additionally, US President Trump has indicated his intention to arrange a meeting between Putin and Zelensky, potentially culminating in a trilateral summit or three-way call involving Washington. Given that the ultimate question asks whether Ukraine and Russia will sign a binding peace deal by the end of 2025, a direct discussion between the two state leaders—either held or officially scheduled during October 2025—would serve as a highly informative leading indicator. If October passes without any direct communication or concrete plans for a summit, the timeline to negotiate, draft, and sign a complex peace agreement before December 31, 2025, becomes exceptionally tight.

WION News: https://www.wionews.com/world/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), a direct communication (either a phone call, video conference, or in-person meeting) involving both the President of Ukraine (currently Volodymyr Zelensky) and the President of Russia (currently Vladimir Putin) takes place, OR if an official announcement is made that such a meeting or call has been firmly scheduled.

- The interaction must involve both heads of state. It can be a bilateral discussion or include other leaders (such as a trilateral format with US President Donald Trump).
- If either leader is replaced as the internationally recognized head of state of their respective country before or during the resolution window, this criteria will apply to their official, recognized successor.
- For a 'scheduled' event to trigger a 'Yes' resolution, an official statement must be released by the Office of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en), the Kremlin (http://en.kremlin.ru/), or the US White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) confirming that a specific date has been agreed upon for the leaders to speak or meet. If one government announces a meeting but another officially and explicitly denies that an agreement to meet was reached, it will not count until confirmed or acknowledged by the counterparties.
- If the meeting or call takes place within the resolution window without prior announcement, it must be confirmed by official government sources or a consensus of credible reporting from major international news agencies (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com, AP: https://apnews.com, or Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com).
- Proposals, suggestions, or rumors reported by anonymous sources without official confirmation from the respective governments do not qualify.
- The event must take place or the announcement must be issued strictly within the resolution window. Events or announcements occurring before 2025-10-01 or after 2025-10-31 will not count toward a 'Yes' resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A peace deal between Ukraine and Russia by the end of 2025 would almost certainly require direct, high-level negotiations between the two nations' top leaders to resolve fundamental differences (e.g., territorial boundaries, security guarantees, sanctions). The occurrence or scheduling of a direct call or meeting in October 2025 acts as a necessary procedural milestone. If no such event is held or announced by October 31, 2025, the remaining two months of the year would likely be insufficient to bridge the substantial gaps in their negotiating positions, making the ultimate outcome highly unlikely.

To address this, independent candidate Jim Walden proposed a pledge wherein candidates would agree to drop out if they are not leading in polls by early September to consolidate the non-socialist vote. Andrew Cuomo agreed to this pledge, stating he would withdraw and back Mayor Adams if it became clear he lacked a path to victory. However, Mayor Adams has thus far declined to join the pledge and has rebuffed Cuomo's calls for him to drop out. With Cuomo's self-imposed deadline of 'early September' arriving, his decision to stay in or drop out will heavily impact the race's dynamics. If Cuomo drops out, Adams's position consolidates, likely reducing the chances that Adams withdraws. If Cuomo remains, Adams faces heightened pressure to exit to prevent a split vote.

Cuomo has publicly pledged to drop his independent bid by early September if he is not leading the polls. If Cuomo drops out, the independent field consolidates significantly, relieving pressure on Adams and reducing the likelihood of Adams dropping out. If Cuomo decides to stay in the race, it signals that he sees a viable path to victory, which would increase the pressure on Adams to withdraw to avoid splitting the vote against Zohran Mamdani. subquestions.resolution_criteria:

- If the album's release is delayed but it is released before October 14, 2025, the evaluation will be based on the chart for its first full calendar day of release. The chart must be published within the resolution window (between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15).

- Changes to the album's title prior to release will not affect resolution, provided it is undeniably her 12th studio album.
subquestions.rationale: A strong debut on the Spotify Daily Top Songs Global chart is a proven leading indicator of long-term streaming success. Because "The Life of a Showgirl" contains only 12 tracks compared to the 31 tracks on Swift's previous album, she needs extraordinarily high per-track engagement to generate enough overall volume to secure the top Spotify artist spot for the year. If all 12 tracks debut in the Top 20 globally, it demonstrates deep, widespread user engagement across the entire tracklist, strongly suggesting she will accumulate enough streams through the remainder of 2025 to outpace competitors like Drake, Bad Bunny, or The Weeknd. Conversely, if lower-tier tracks miss the Top 20, it could signal a top-heavy performance, putting her ultimate 2025 title at risk.
