If the win percentage is strictly less than .500 at the end of the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A major driver for a potential Giannis Antetokounmpo trade is the team's poor performance and inability to contend for a title. If the Bucks can rally to a .500 or better record by early January, it signals a successful team turnaround, likely easing trade pressures and keeping Giannis in Milwaukee through the trade deadline. Conversely, if they fail to reach this benchmark by the end of this critical schedule window, the likelihood of the front office pivoting to a rebuild and trading him increases drastically.

question: Poilievre out as leader of Conservatives in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Pierre Poilievre announces he is resigning as head of the Conservative Party of Canada or otherwise ceases to be head of the Conservative Party of Canada for any length of time between March 23, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET (inclusive). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of Pierre Poilievre's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/removal goes into effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from Pierre Poilievre or the Conservative Party of Canada, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any sitting Conservative Member of Parliament publicly call for Pierre Poilievre to resign as leader of the Conservative Party of Canada between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In the 2025 federal election, the Conservative Party of Canada failed to form the government, and leader Pierre Poilievre lost his seat in the Carleton riding. According to the party's constitution, losing a federal election triggers a mandatory leadership review, which the national council has scheduled for January 2026. While Poilievre has expressed confidence in his position and awaits a by-election in Alberta's Battle River-Crowfoot riding (following the resignation of MP Damien Kurek to open up a seat), his position is vulnerable while he remains outside the House of Commons. Maintaining caucus unity is crucial for his survival until the leadership review. Any public dissent from sitting Conservative MPs would indicate a severe fracture in his support base and serve as a strong early indicator of his potential departure.

Sources:
Parliament of Canada - Members: https://www.ourcommons.ca/members/en
CBC News Politics: https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics
Global News Politics: https://globalnews.ca/politics/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), any sitting Member of Parliament (MP) who is a member of the Conservative Party of Canada caucus makes a public, on-the-record statement explicitly calling for Pierre Poilievre to resign, step down, or be replaced as the leader of the Conservative Party of Canada.

The public statement can be made via official social media channels, press releases, parliamentary proceedings, published opinion pieces, or on-the-record interviews with credible media organizations.

The MP must be publicly identified by name and must be actively listed as a Conservative MP on the official Parliament of Canada website (https://www.ourcommons.ca/members/en) at the exact time the statement is made. Statements attributed to anonymous sources, rumored leaks, or made by former MPs who have already resigned do not count.

Resolution will be based on consensus reporting from major Canadian news outlets such as CBC News (https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics) or Global News (https://globalnews.ca/politics/), as well as direct evidence from the MP's verified communication channels. If no such public call is made by a sitting Conservative MP within the specified time window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Following an election loss and his own seat loss, Poilievre is heavily reliant on caucus unity to survive the interim period before the January 2026 leadership review. A public demand for his resignation by a sitting Conservative MP would signal a critical loss of confidence and organized internal opposition. Tracking this provides a highly informative, early indicator of whether he will be ousted or forced to resign before the ultimate question's deadline.

question: NYSE marketwide circuit breaker in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a marketwide circuit breaker is triggered on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at any time between January 1 and market close on December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A marketwide circuit breaker is defined as a trading halt that is initiated due to significant declines in the S&P 500 Index, specifically a Level 1, Level 2, or Level 3 halt as per NYSE rules.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the NYSE, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) close at or above 45.00 on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question evaluates if a marketwide circuit breaker will be triggered on the NYSE in 2025. Circuit breakers halt trading during rapid market declines and are triggered when the S&P 500 drops by 7% (Level 1), 13% (Level 2), or 20% (Level 3) in a single day. In April 2025, the stock market experienced severe sell-offs due to reciprocal tariffs and inflation concerns, with the S&P 500 falling almost 6% in one session—coming very close to the 7% circuit breaker threshold (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/circuit-breaker-heres-trading-halted-20250410.html).

The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) measures the stock market's expectation of volatility based on S&P 500 index options. High VIX values indicate extreme fear and large expected price swings, which are prerequisites for marketwide circuit breakers. Historically, VIX levels above 40 reflect severe market turmoil. During the March 2020 crash, when the last marketwide circuit breakers were triggered, the VIX closed at a record high of 82.69 (https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/16/wall-street-fear-gauge-hits-highest-level-ever.html). Therefore, monitoring whether the VIX surges above 45.00 in September 2025 acts as a highly informative crux for predicting if the extreme volatility needed to trigger a circuit breaker will persist or escalate before the year ends.

Sources:
Yahoo! Finance: What is a circuit breaker? - https://finance.yahoo.com/news/circuit-breaker-heres-trading-halted-20250410.html
CNBC: Wall Street's 'fear gauge' hits highest level ever - https://www.cnbc.com/2020/03/16/wall-street-fear-gauge-hits-highest-level-ever.html
CBOE VIX Index - https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) official closing price is 45.00 or higher on any trading day between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

The primary resolution source will be historical data from Yahoo Finance for the VIX index (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EVIX/history/). The "Close" column for the specified dates will be used for resolution. Intraday highs that exceed 45.00 but close below 45.00 will not count towards a "Yes" resolution. 

In the event Yahoo Finance data is unavailable, data directly from the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE) (https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/) or another credible financial data provider (such as Bloomberg, MarketWatch, or Reuters) will be used as a fallback. 

If the specified window passes without the VIX closing at or above 45.00, or if all major exchanges are closed for the entirety of this period preventing the index from being calculated, this question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A marketwide circuit breaker requires a sudden and severe 7% drop in the S&P 500. The VIX index directly measures anticipated stock market volatility and fear. A VIX closing value above 45.00 in September is a strong signal of panic and extreme distress in the market. Since circuit breakers correlate strongly with immense VIX spikes (as seen in March 2020), tracking if the VIX surpasses 45.00 in the short term serves as a robust leading indicator for the ultimate question without merely being a restatement of it.

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.0% in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Treasury 10-year yield reaches or is higher than the listed value for any date between April 9 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is the Department of the treasury, specially the data listed under "Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates" for the column "10 Yr" (see: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).

subquestions.question: Will the 12-month percentage change in the US Consumer Price Index (CPI-U) for August 2025 be 2.5% or higher?
subquestions.background_information: The ultimate question asks whether the 10-year Treasury yield will hit 5.0% in 2025. A major driver for long-term Treasury yields is inflation, which dictates the Federal Reserve's monetary policy and influences the term premium demanded by bond investors. In mid-2025, inflation was hovering slightly above the Fed's 2% target, with the year-over-year CPI for May 2025 reported at 2.4% (https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news). If inflation begins to accelerate or remains sticky at elevated levels, it reduces the likelihood of near-term Federal Reserve rate cuts, pushing long-term Treasury yields higher. Therefore, the August 2025 CPI release serves as a critical crux. If the 12-month percentage change climbs back to 2.5% or higher, it indicates re-accelerating or persistent inflation, providing a strong signal that the 10-year yield is on track to approach or reach the 5.0% mark later in the year. Sources: Investing.com Economy News (https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news), US Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index (https://www.bls.gov/cpi/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that the 12-month percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), All items, not seasonally adjusted, is 2.5% or higher for the month of August 2025. The data must be officially published in the BLS 'Consumer Price Index Summary' news release between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The resolution will be determined strictly based on the initial release of the August 2025 data available on the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/cpi/news.htm). Any subsequent revisions to the data will not affect the resolution. If the data for August 2025 is not published during the resolution window between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question will resolve as unresolvable (N/A).
subquestions.rationale: Inflation data is a primary leading indicator for long-term Treasury yields. The August CPI report, which is released in September, will provide crucial insight into the inflation trend entering the final quarter of the year. An inflation reading of 2.5% or higher would signal to markets that inflation remains sticky, forcing the Federal Reserve to maintain higher interest rates and making a 5.0% 10-year Treasury yield significantly more probable.

question: Gaza mass population relocation in 2025?
description:
On February 4, Donald Trump floated a plan for the reconstruction of Gaza including the relocation of Gaza’s population (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/)

This market will resolve to “Yes” if at least 500,000 Gazans leave the Gaza strip between February 6, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This includes the transfer of Gazans to Israel, the West Bank or other countries, as well as the departure of Gazans from the Gaza Strip through visa or refugee programs.

This market refers to the total number of Gazans who leave, regardless of method.  

Announcements of relocation plans will not count, only actual relocation will qualify.

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the government of Israel or the United States officially announce a finalized agreement with a third-party sovereign state to accept the relocation of at least 10,000 Palestinians from the Gaza Strip between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: In February 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump proposed a plan for the reconstruction of Gaza that included the mass relocation of its population (https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/). Subsequent reporting in August 2025 indicated that a detailed prospectus known as the 'GREAT Trust' had been circulating within the U.S. administration, aiming to temporarily or permanently relocate residents into transit areas or third countries (https://www.washingtonpost.com/). Israel has actively sought third-party nations to host relocated Palestinians, with reports highlighting talks with South Sudan to establish mass resettlement camps (https://apnews.com/). Despite Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's endorsement, global human rights groups have strongly opposed the plan, and finding willing host nations remains the primary bottleneck. Securing international bilateral agreements is a necessary precursor to large-scale relocations. Sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/trump-netanyahu-set-pivotal-talks-middle-east-agenda-2025-02-04/) | Washington Post (https://www.washingtonpost.com/) | AP News (https://apnews.com/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), an official representative or an official press release from the government of Israel, the United States, or a receiving third-party country publicly announces that a finalized agreement has been reached for the receiving sovereign nation to host, resettle, or process at least 10,000 Palestinians relocating from the Gaza Strip. The announcement must confirm that the agreement is finalized or signed; announcements of ongoing talks, proposals, or exploratory feasibility studies do not qualify. Transfers strictly to the West Bank do not count, as the destination must be a distinct third-party sovereign nation. If the official government announcement does not explicitly specify a number, credible reporting from major news outlets (such as AP News or Reuters) confirming that the agreement covers 10,000 or more individuals will be sufficient to meet the threshold. Primary resolution sources will include official press statements from the U.S. State Department (https://www.state.gov/press-releases/) or the Israeli Prime Minister's Office (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office/news), corroborated by credible international news sources (https://apnews.com/). If no such formalized agreement is announced between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, or if the event is delayed beyond 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question requires 500,000 Gazans to be relocated by December 31, 2025. Moving half a million people is an immense logistical operation that fundamentally requires large-scale destinations willing to accept them. As of August 2025, no official mass resettlement agreements have been confirmed. For 500,000 people to be successfully moved by year-end, formal bilateral host agreements must be established rapidly. If October 1 arrives without any third-party nation formally agreeing to take a significant cohort (10,000+), the logistical window to hit the 500,000 threshold by December 31 effectively closes, making this a highly informative crux for forecasters.

question: Zelenskyy wears a suit and tie during next Trump meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Volodymyr Zelenskyy is photographed or videotaped wearing a Western-style suit and tie in the physical presence of Trump at any point during their next in-person meeting period between November 24, 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “meeting period” refers to the full continuous span of time associated with their next in-person engagement. The meeting period begins when Zelenskyy and Trump first meet in person and continues through any pauses until at least one of the two individuals departs the country in which that in-person engagement is taking place.

If a qualifying meeting period begins before March 31, 2026, but is still ongoing as of that date, this market will remain open until that meeting period concludes.

A Western-style suit and tie refers to a conventional business suit consisting of a jacket, trousers, dress shirt, and necktie, as commonly understood in Western formal or business attire.

Formal military attire, such as was previously worn by Zelenskyy (https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/00.png), which does not meet the above specifications, will not qualify.

This market will resolve to “No” if the next meeting period concludes without a qualifying photograph or video, or if no qualifying in-person meeting occurs by March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting, including photographs or video from reputable media outlets.

subquestions.question: Will Volodymyr Zelenskyy be photographed or videotaped wearing a necktie during any public appearance or official meeting between November 26, 2025, and December 26, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has recently shifted his public wardrobe from olive military fatigues to more formal, black suit-style jackets and collared shirts. This was prominently noted during his meetings with Donald Trump in August and October 2025, where Trump praised his attire as "stylish" (https://www.livemint.com/). However, a critical missing element from these outfits is the necktie. Observers and netizens have consistently pointed out the absence of a tie (https://indiatimes.com/). According to reporting, Zelenskyy has previously vowed not to wear a traditional suit and tie until the war in Ukraine is over (https://www.sbs.com.au/). Because the ultimate question's resolution specifically hinges on him wearing a "Western-style suit and tie", the necktie is the primary crux. Tracking whether he wears a necktie to any official event or public appearance in the near term serves as a strong leading indicator of whether he has broken his vow or updated his wardrobe policy ahead of his next meeting with Trump.

Sources:
Mint: https://www.livemint.com/
India Times: https://indiatimes.com/
SBS: https://www.sbs.com.au/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Volodymyr Zelenskyy is photographed or videotaped wearing a necktie during any public appearance, press conference, or official meeting that occurs between 2025-11-26 and 2025-12-26 (inclusive). 

To resolve Yes, the necktie must be clearly visible in a photograph or video published by credible media outlets (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP News: https://apnews.com/) or official Ukrainian government channels (e.g., the official website of the President of Ukraine: https://www.president.gov.ua/en, or Zelenskyy's official, verified social media accounts).

The event where he wears the tie must be independently verifiable to have occurred within the specified date window (2025-11-26 to 2025-12-26). Re-publications of archival footage or photos from events that took place before November 26, 2025, do not qualify.

For the purposes of this question, a "necktie" is defined as a traditional long piece of cloth worn for decorative purposes around the neck, resting under the shirt collar and knotted at the throat, consistent with standard Western business attire. Bow ties, cravats, or ascots do not qualify. If the resolution window closes without any credible photographic or video evidence of Zelenskyy wearing a necktie at a qualifying event, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question requires Zelenskyy to wear a full Western-style suit *and tie*. While he has already begun wearing suit jackets and collared shirts, he has intentionally avoided the necktie, reportedly vowing not to wear one until the war ends. Monitoring whether he wears a necktie in any public or official capacity over the next month serves as a crucial leading indicator. If he wears a tie, it signals he has abandoned his vow or changed his sartorial policy, massively increasing the probability he will wear one during his next meeting with Trump.

question: Fed rate cut by October 2025 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is decreased at any point between September 18 and the completion of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for October 2025, currently scheduled for October 28–29. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If no relevant statement is released for this meeting by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, and no qualifying rate cut is announced, this market will resolve to "No". Emergency rate cuts will qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the official U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) for September 2025 be reported at 4.3% or higher in the initial BLS release?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. Federal Reserve considers both labor market conditions and inflation when making its monetary policy decisions, balancing its dual mandate of full employment and price stability. In recent months, Fed officials have signaled increasing attention to downside risks in the labor market. As of mid-2025, the unemployment rate has hovered in a narrow band between 4.0% and 4.2%. A rising unemployment rate, particularly breaking above 4.2%, would indicate further labor market softening, creating stronger pressure for the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to lower the target federal funds rate at its upcoming October 2025 meeting. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) typically releases the Employment Situation summary for September on the first Friday of October, providing a critical data point before the Fed's October meeting.

Sources:
BLS Employment Situation News Release: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) initially reports a seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) of 4.3% or higher for the month of September 2025. This initial publication must occur between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive).

The primary resolution source will be the official BLS Employment Situation news release (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm).
- The resolution will be based strictly on the headline seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for September 2025 as published in the initial release during the specified timeframe.
- If the initially reported value is exactly 4.3% or greater, the question resolves Yes. If it is 4.2% or lower, the question resolves No.
- Any subsequent revisions to the September 2025 unemployment data made after the initial release will not be considered for resolution.
- Delayed events: If the BLS postpones the release of the September 2025 employment data beyond the resolution window (i.e., it is not published between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18), the question should be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: The BLS employment report is a critical macroeconomic indicator used by the Federal Reserve to guide monetary policy. A jump in the unemployment rate to 4.3% or higher would signal a meaningful deterioration in the labor market compared to previous months. This would strongly increase the probability that the Fed acts to cut interest rates at the October 2025 FOMC meeting to fulfill the employment side of its dual mandate, making it an excellent leading indicator for the ultimate question.

question: Will Trump deport 750,000 or more people in 2025?
description:
During the 2024 FY ICE removed 271,484 non citizens (see: https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf).

subquestions.question: Will Mexico's Ministry of the Interior (SEGOB) report 350,000 or more Mexican nationals repatriated from the United States in calendar year 2025, in data published between January 29, 2026, and February 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information: The ultimate question asks whether ICE removed 750,000 or more non-citizens in the 2025 fiscal year. Because official ICE deportation data can be delayed, independent tracking by receiving countries serves as an excellent early indicator. Historically, Mexican nationals make up a large percentage of total U.S. deportations. Mexico's Unidad de Politica Migratoria, Registro e Identidad de Personas (UPMRIP), under the Secretariat of the Interior (SEGOB), independently tracks and publishes the number of Mexican nationals repatriated from the United States ('Eventos de repatriacion de mexicanos desde Estados Unidos'). For context, in 2023, SEGOB reported approximately 214,849 repatriations of Mexicans from the U.S. If U.S. deportations surged to meet or exceed the 750,000 threshold across all nationalities in 2025, it is highly probable that repatriations of Mexican nationals would correspondingly surge to 350,000 or more. Monitoring SEGOB's calendar year 2025 statistics provides a strong, independent early indicator of ICE's overall deportation volume before the ICE Annual Report is fully processed and published. Sources: 1) ICE Annual Report FY 2024 (https://www.ice.gov/doclib/eoy/iceAnnualReportFY2024.pdf) 2) Mexico UPMRIP Boletines (http://portales.segob.gob.mx/es/PoliticaMigratoria/Boletines_Estadisticos).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2026-01-29 and 2026-02-26 (inclusive), Mexico's Unidad de Politica Migratoria, Registro e Identidad de Personas (UPMRIP) or the Secretariat of the Interior (SEGOB) publishes official data indicating that the total number of 'Eventos de repatriacion de mexicanos desde Estados Unidos' (Events of repatriation of Mexicans from the United States) for the full calendar year 2025 was 350,000 or greater. The primary resolution source will be the official UPMRIP statistical bulletins or data tables available at http://portales.segob.gob.mx/es/PoliticaMigratoria/Boletines_Estadisticos. If the reported total for the 2025 calendar year is exactly 350,000 or greater, it resolves Yes. If the reported total is less than 350,000, it resolves No. If the final data for the full calendar year 2025 is not published within this exact resolution window (by 2026-02-26 at 11:59 PM UTC), the question will be considered unresolvable and should resolve as Ambiguous/Unresolved.
subquestions.rationale: Mexico is historically the largest country of origin for deportees from the U.S. Using an independent dataset from the Mexican government tracking incoming deportees provides a highly correlated proxy for U.S. ICE numbers that cannot be obfuscated by U.S. domestic agency delays. Since Mexicans typically comprise 40-50% of U.S. deportations, seeing 350,000 or more Mexican repatriations strongly points toward total ICE removals approaching or exceeding 750,000, providing forecasters with actionable evidence before the ultimate ICE report.

subquestions.question: Will the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), NIH, or CDC publicly release a formal written report or study concerning the causes of autism between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In late August 2025, Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced during a Cabinet meeting that his department had identified "certain interventions" that are "almost certainly causing autism." He pledged that a full public announcement, alongside related research and data, would be released in September 2025. Previously, in May 2025, he had pushed his original September deadline back to March 2026, but his recent August remarks reinstated the September timeline. The NIH has also been directed to conduct studies pinpointing these supposed causes. Tracking whether a formal written report or study is actually published by HHS or NIH in September serves as a concrete, observable indicator of whether RFK Jr. is on track to definitively name a cause of autism before November.

Sources:
Yahoo News - https://www.yahoo.com/news/rfk-jr-made-big-promises-autism-000000000.html
UPI - https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/08/27/rfk-jr-autism-report/
The Independent - https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/rfk-jr-autism-cause-timeline-b2721835.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), the National Institutes of Health (NIH), or the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) officially publishes a formal written report, study, white paper, or official dataset specifically investigating or addressing the causes of autism (including potential "interventions" or "environmental toxins") between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

- The document must be officially published or hosted on an official .gov website associated with HHS (https://www.hhs.gov/), NIH (https://www.nih.gov/), or CDC (https://www.cdc.gov/), or be formally distributed via an official press release from these agencies linking to the written document.
- The document does not need to declare a definitive cause to count, as long as its primary subject matter is the investigation of autism's causes or links to interventions/toxins.
- Verbal statements, interviews, press conferences, or social media posts by RFK Jr. or other officials do not count for this subquestion unless they are accompanied by the public release of a formal written report or study as described above.
- Leaked documents that are not officially released or acknowledged by the agencies do not qualify.
- If the document is delayed and no such qualifying release occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 at 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion tracks an observable administrative milestone—the publication of a formal written report or study by federal health agencies—rather than a verbal claim of finding a 'definitive cause'. Since RFK Jr. explicitly promised to release his research in September 2025, the actual publication of this document is a crucial leading indicator. If the agencies publish the report by October 1, it is highly likely RFK Jr. will use it to formally announce a definitive cause, resolving the ultimate question to 'Yes'. Conversely, if no official document materializes in September, it strongly suggests another delay in his timeline, making a definitive announcement before November unlikely.

question: Han Duck-soo in jail by January 31?
description:

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo spends time in custody in a jail or prison. subquestions.question: Will a South Korean court issue a new arrest warrant or extend the detention of former President Yoon Suk-yeol between December 25, 2025, and January 18, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Former South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol is currently detained while facing trial for his role in the December 2024 martial law declaration and insurrection attempt. According to legal experts and news reports, the legal deadline for his current detention period expires on January 18, 2026 (https://english.hani.co.kr/). Prosecutors are actively seeking a new arrest warrant from the Seoul Central District Court to ensure he remains in custody throughout his trial. Meanwhile, former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo is a co-defendant in the broader insurrection case, charged with aiding the effort, and faces a requested 15-year prison sentence with a verdict expected on January 21, 2026 (https://english.chosun.com/). Because Yoon is considered the primary architect of the insurrection, the court's willingness to keep him detained by issuing a new warrant will serve as a bellwether for the judiciary's overall stance on the insurrection cases. A strict approach toward Yoon increases the likelihood that Han Duck-soo will be convicted and immediately taken into court custody (jail) upon his sentencing.

Sources:
Hankyoreh (English): https://english.hani.co.kr/
The Chosun Ilbo (English): https://english.chosun.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if credible news reports or official South Korean court announcements confirm that a court has issued a new arrest warrant, a new detention warrant, or officially extended the pre-trial detention period for former President Yoon Suk-yeol between 2025-12-25 and 2026-01-18 (inclusive of both dates, based on South Korea Standard Time). 

If Yoon is released, or if January 18, 2026, 11:59 PM KST passes without any new warrant or extension being issued, this question resolves No. 

Official government press releases or reporting from reputable South Korean and international media outlets will be used for resolution. Primary sources include Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr/), KBS World (https://world.kbs.co.kr/english/), and The Korea Herald (https://www.koreaherald.com/). Delayed announcements of an extension that actually occurred within the window will still count toward a Yes resolution, provided the legal decision was finalized before the end of the window. If the court process is postponed beyond the resolution window and no decision is made by the end date, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Han Duck-soo's potential imprisonment hinges largely on his January 21 sentencing for his role in the December 2024 martial law declaration. Yoon Suk-yeol is the central figure in the same overarching insurrection case, and his detention is set to expire on January 18. If the court issues a new warrant to keep Yoon detained, it strongly signals that the judiciary is taking a severe stance on the insurrection defendants, making it significantly more likely that Han will also receive a guilty verdict with immediate prison time. Thus, Yoon's detention status is a highly informative crux for Han's fate.

question: Will the ECB announce no change at the February 2026 meeting?
description:
This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the deposit facility rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the European Central Bank's (ECB) February 2026 meeting.

If the deposit facility rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 basis points and will resolve to the relevant bracket.
For example, if the deposit facility rate is increased or decreased by 12.5 basis points, it will be treated as a 25 basis point change for the purposes of resolution.

The resolution source for this market is information released by the European Central Bank after its February 5, 2026 policy meeting, as listed on the official ECB calendar:
https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html

The level and change of the deposit facility rate is also published at the official ECB interest rates page:
https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/key_ecb_interest_rates/html/index.en.html

This market may resolve as soon as the ECB releases its interest rate decision following the February 5, 2026, meeting.

If no interest rate decision or update is published by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to the “No change” bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the ECB's December 2025 macroeconomic projections forecast euro area annual HICP inflation for 2026 at 1.9% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
The European Central Bank (ECB) targets an inflation rate of 2% over the medium term. At its October 2025 meeting, the ECB maintained the deposit facility rate at 2.00%, noting that actual euro area annual inflation had risen to 2.2% in September 2025. The ECB is scheduled to release its next monetary policy decision alongside updated Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections on December 18, 2025. Previous projections had 2026 inflation at 1.7%, but market analysts anticipate a slight upward revision, though generally expecting it to remain below 2%. If the 2026 inflation forecast is revised to 1.9% or higher, it would signal that inflation expectations are uncomfortably close to the ECB's ceiling. This would directly influence the governing council's assessment, potentially prompting a rate hike or hawkish pivot at the subsequent February 2026 meeting rather than maintaining a 'no change' stance.

Sources:
European Central Bank - Economic Bulletin Issue 7, 2025: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/economic-bulletin/html/index.en.html
European Central Bank - Macroeconomic Projections: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/projections/html/index.en.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections for the euro area, published between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive), forecast the annual Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP) inflation for the year 2026 to be 1.9% or higher.

The resolution will be based on the headline HICP inflation projection for 2026 in the "baseline" or "main" scenario, as found in the official publication on the ECB's macroeconomic projections page (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/pub/projections/html/index.en.html).

If the exact projected value for 2026 is 1.9% or greater, the question resolves "Yes". If the projected value is 1.8% or lower, it resolves "No". If no updated macroeconomic projection for 2026 HICP inflation is published by the ECB between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12, the question will resolve "No".
subquestions.rationale: The ECB's interest rate decisions are strictly data-dependent and heavily influenced by its own staff macroeconomic projections. By capturing whether the 2026 inflation projection is revised to 1.9% or higher, this subquestion isolates a key indicator of underlying inflationary pressures. A higher inflation projection in December 2025 would serve as a strong crux indicating that the ECB may deviate from a 'no change' policy and instead opt for a rate adjustment at the February 2026 meeting to address persistent inflation risks.

question: Israel x Hamas ceasefire cancelled by December 31?
description:
On October 9, Israel and Hamas signed a deal implementing a ceasefire: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-hamas-agree-gaza-ceasefire-return-hostages-2025-10-09/

This market will resolve to "Yes" if a either Israel or Hamas announce the cancellation of the ongoing ceasefire, or if a consensus of credible reporting confirms that the ceasefire is no longer in effect, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

Announcements that one side or another violated the ongoing ceasefire will not be enough to resolve this market to "Yes"; only a definitive announcement by Israel or Hamas, or otherwise a wide consensus of credible reporting that that the ceasefire has been ended, will qualify to resolve this market to "Yes".

The primary solution resolution source will be official information from Hamas or the government of Israel, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Israeli government or IDF officially confirm the release of at least 10 living Israeli hostages from Gaza between October 11, 2025 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 9, 2025, Israel and Hamas signed a ceasefire and hostage-prisoner exchange deal aimed at ending the two-year Gaza conflict. A core component of this first phase of the peace plan is the release of all remaining Israeli hostages held by Hamas. Current estimates indicate there are 48 hostages remaining, with approximately 20 believed to be alive. The agreement reportedly stipulates a 72-hour window following the ceasefire's implementation for Hamas to return the living hostages, a deadline expected to fall early in the week following the October 9 agreement. Reaching this milestone is critical; if Hamas complies and returns the hostages, it demonstrates commitment to the deal, significantly increasing the likelihood that the ceasefire will hold. If Hamas fails to return these hostages, the ceasefire is highly likely to collapse rapidly and be formally cancelled by Israel.

Sources:
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-hamas-agree-gaza-ceasefire-return-hostages-2025-10-09/
Israel Defense Forces (IDF): https://www.idf.il/en/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the Israeli government (e.g., the Prime Minister's Office) or the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) officially announces the release and safe return to Israeli territory of at least 10 living Israeli hostages, who were held in Gaza prior to October 11, 2025, between the start_date of 2025-10-11 and the end_date of 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The official announcement must be made via official government or IDF channels, such as their websites (e.g., https://www.idf.il/en/ or https://www.gov.il/en/departments/prime_ministers_office) or their official, verified social media accounts. A consensus of credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP: https://apnews.com/) quoting Israeli officials confirming the release of at least 10 living hostages during this window will also suffice if an official public statement is temporarily unavailable.

The hostages must be confirmed alive at the time of their return. The release of deceased hostages' remains does not count toward the threshold of 10 living hostages. 

If the threshold of 10 living hostages is not met by 11:59 PM ET on October 31, 2025, this question resolves "No". Delayed events beyond this resolution window will result in a "No" resolution. Announcements of violations or partial returns falling short of the threshold will not be sufficient to resolve "Yes".
subquestions.rationale: The return of the living hostages is the most immediate and critical condition of the ceasefire agreement established on October 9, 2025. If Hamas successfully releases a significant number of living hostages (at least 10), it strongly indicates that the initial phase of the ceasefire is being implemented, building the necessary trust to prevent a cancellation. Conversely, failure to release the hostages would be a major violation of the newly signed terms, making it highly probable that Israel would announce the cancellation of the ongoing ceasefire before December 31. Therefore, this subquestion serves as a powerful, early observable indicator of the ultimate outcome.

question: Pedro Sánchez out as PM of Spain in 2025?
description:

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation, is dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as Prime Minister of Spain within this market's timeframe.

subquestions.question: Will a formal motion of no confidence (moción de censura) against Pedro Sánchez be registered in the Spanish Congress of Deputies between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is facing mounting pressure and calls for resignation due to a series of corruption investigations involving his wife (Begoña Gómez), his brother (David Sánchez), and former key aides such as Santos Cerdán. Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo of the Popular Party (PP) has strongly urged Sánchez to step down, stating that 'survival is no longer an option.' Despite these scandals and leading a fragile minority coalition that has struggled to pass legislation, Sánchez has explicitly ruled out resigning or calling snap elections, declaring instead that he will 'fight to get [a budget] approved.' Under Article 113 of the Spanish Constitution, the Congress of Deputies can challenge the government's political responsibility by adopting a motion of no confidence. Such a motion must be proposed by at least one-tenth of the Deputies (35 members). Given Sánchez's refusal to resign, a motion of no confidence represents the primary institutional mechanism the opposition could use to attempt to force him from power during the critical autumn legislative session.

Sources:
MyJoyOnline: https://www.myjoyonline.com/spanish-pm-sorry-for-corruption-scandal-as-opposition-demands-resignation/
NZ Herald: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/spanish-pm-accuses-judges-of-doing-politics-in-graft-cases/
Congress of Deputies (Motion of no confidence rules): https://www.congreso.es/en/cem/mocion
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if a formal motion of no confidence (moción de censura) against the government of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is officially registered with the Bureau of the Congress of Deputies (Mesa del Congreso de los Diputados) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The registration must be confirmed by the official registry of the Spanish Congress of Deputies or through a consensus of credible reporting from major Spanish or international news outlets. The motion does not need to be debated, voted on, or passed within this timeframe; the singular act of formal registration by at least 35 deputies within the specific resolution window is sufficient for a 'Yes' resolution. 

If Pedro Sánchez resigns or is otherwise removed from office during this window without a motion of no confidence being registered first, this question will resolve 'No'. If no such motion is registered by the end of the day on 2025-10-31, the question resolves 'No'.

Resolution sources:
- Official Congress of Deputies Parliamentary Initiatives Registry: https://www.congreso.es/es/busqueda-de-iniciativas
- El País (English edition): https://english.elpais.com/
- Reuters Europe: https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/
subquestions.rationale: A motion of no confidence is the direct constitutional mechanism for removing a Spanish Prime Minister. Tracking whether the opposition has enough momentum and unity to formally register such a motion during the politically fraught October budget period serves as an excellent early indicator for whether Sánchez will ultimately be ousted by the end of 2025. If a motion is registered, it significantly increases the likelihood of his removal; if the opposition fails to mount this challenge, it indicates he retains enough passive support to survive the year.

question: Will Trump announce Chris Waller as next Fed Chair in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will there be credible media reporting between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025 that Christopher Waller has completed or is scheduled for a second-round interview for the Federal Reserve Chair position?
subquestions.background_information:
In late October 2025, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent identified five finalists to potentially succeed Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve chair: Christopher Waller, Michelle Bowman, Kevin Warsh, Kevin Hassett, and Rick Rieder. Bessent stated that he plans to conduct second-round interviews in the coming weeks and will present President Donald Trump with a 'good slate' of candidates after the Thanksgiving holiday (November 27, 2025). Trump is expected to make his final choice before the end of the year. As of October 31, 2025, Christopher Waller is officially one of the five named finalists. Since the second round of interviews will dictate who advances to the final slate, confirmation that Waller has participated in this round is a crucial near-term indicator of his viability for the ultimate nomination.

Sources:
Anadolu Ajansı (October 28, 2025) - https://www.aa.com.tr/en
LiveMint (October 28, 2025) - https://www.livemint.com
NBC News - https://www.nbcnews.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), an official communication from the Trump administration (such as a press release from the Treasury Department [https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases] or a post from Donald Trump's official Truth Social account [https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump]) OR an original report from a credible major news organization (e.g., Bloomberg [https://www.bloomberg.com], Reuters [https://www.reuters.com], The Wall Street Journal [https://www.wsj.com], Fox Business [https://www.foxbusiness.com], or The New York Times [https://www.nytimes.com]) confirms that Christopher Waller has participated in, or is scheduled to participate in, an interview or direct meeting with Donald Trump or Scott Bessent regarding the Federal Reserve Chair position.

To trigger a Yes resolution, the reporting or official statement must explicitly name Christopher Waller (either individually or by confirming that 'all five' previously named finalists, which includes Waller, were interviewed) and reference an interview or meeting occurring or scheduled to occur after October 28, 2025. 

The publication of this confirming report or statement must happen strictly between the start_date (2025-10-31) and end_date (2025-11-30). If the reporting only emerges after November 30, 2025, or if the event is indefinitely postponed beyond the resolution window with no scheduling updates by November 30, the question will resolve No. If it is officially reported before November 30 that Waller has withdrawn his name from consideration without interviewing, this resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is actively managing the Fed Chair search and explicitly indicated that second-round interviews are taking place in November 2025, before presenting a final slate to Trump shortly after Thanksgiving. If Waller is confirmed to have interviewed or scheduled an interview during this critical window, it validates his status as an active contender, significantly increasing his probability of being the ultimate pick. If he does not interview, is omitted from reports of candidate meetings, or drops out, his chances of being chosen drop to near zero, providing a powerful crux for the ultimate question.

question: Will iPhone 17 cost more than iPhone 16?

question: Will U.S. National debt surpass $38 trillion in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimate the U.S. federal budget deficit for Fiscal Year 2025 to be $1.85 trillion or more in its Monthly Budget Review released between October 1 and October 18, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
According to a September 2025 report by the Congressional Budget Office (CBO), the United States accumulated a $2 trillion federal budget deficit over the first 11 months of Fiscal Year 2025. Because September typically sees a surplus due to quarterly tax receipts, the CBO projected the total deficit for the full fiscal year (ending September 30, 2025) to be $1.8 trillion. Meanwhile, the gross national debt surpassed $37 trillion in mid-August 2025, growing at a historically rapid pace of roughly $1 trillion every five months. The annual budget deficit directly drives the borrowing needs of the Treasury. If the final FY 2025 deficit comes in significantly higher than the $1.8 trillion projection (e.g., $1.85 trillion or more), it would indicate that government spending outpaced revenues by more than expected in the final month. This accelerated pace of deficit spending acts as a critical indicator that the total national debt is accumulating faster than forecasted, thereby increasing the likelihood that it will breach the $38 trillion mark before the end of calendar year 2025.

Sources:
Congressional Budget Office - Monthly Budget Review: https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review
Report: U.S. racked up $2 trillion deficit over past 11 months (KPVI): https://www.kpvi.com/news/national_news/report-u-s-racked-up-2-trillion-deficit-over-past-11-months/article_ed1c23a8-4e8b-59d4-8d48-3a9d4a413d11.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) publishes a Monthly Budget Review (or official equivalent release estimating the full FY 2025 deficit) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-18 (inclusive) stating that the total federal budget deficit for Fiscal Year 2025 (October 2024 through September 2025) was $1.85 trillion or greater (i.e., $1,850 billion or more).

The primary source for this resolution is the official CBO website, specifically the Monthly Budget Review publications page (https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review). 

To resolve the question, the specific numerical value provided in the summary table for the FY 2025 total deficit (typically listed in billions of dollars) will be used. If the text and table differ, the table's exact figure will take precedence. If a range is provided rather than a point estimate, the midpoint of the range will be used. 

If the reported deficit is strictly less than $1,850 billion, the question resolves 'No'. 

If the CBO does not release its FY 2025 full-year deficit estimate between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-18 at 11:59 PM ET, the question will be considered unresolvable and should be canceled.
subquestions.rationale: The U.S. national debt is heavily influenced by the federal budget deficit. By the end of August 2025, the national debt topped $37 trillion, and the CBO projected a full-year FY 2025 deficit of $1.8 trillion. If the final FY 2025 deficit reported in early October exceeds expectations and hits $1.85 trillion or more, it implies that recent borrowing was higher than forecasted. This accelerated pace of debt accumulation serves as a strong leading indicator for whether the national debt will surpass the ultimate threshold of $38 trillion by the end of 2025.

question: GPT ads by March 31?
description:

Limited advertisement releases restricted to a specific region, model, or user group will qualify. The release must be publicly announced as accessible to the relevant users. Closed betas or fully private testing do not count.

Once implemented, the market will resolve to “Yes” immediately, regardless of whether the integration is later removed.

An announcement will not suffice to resolve this market to "Yes"; only the release of the advertisement integration will trigger a "Yes" resolution for this market.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from OpenAI; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce plans to introduce advertisements into ChatGPT or its general-purpose GPT models between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent leaks from the ChatGPT Android app beta (version 1.2025.329) have revealed code referencing an 'ads feature', 'search ad', and 'search ads carousel', heavily suggesting that OpenAI is actively developing ad integrations. Some users on social media have also recently claimed to see experimental ads in the app. Although OpenAI CEO Sam Altman previously called ads a 'last resort' and 'uniquely unsettling', the massive operational costs of supporting an estimated 800 million weekly users may be shifting the company's monetization strategy, especially for the free tier. This question tracks whether OpenAI will formally confirm these plans in the near term, which would serve as a strong leading indicator for a full ad release by March 2026.

Sources:
Engadget: https://www.engadget.com/
Tom's Guide: https://www.tomsguide.com/
Digit: https://www.digit.in/
Fudzilla: https://www.fudzilla.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05 (inclusive), OpenAI makes an official public announcement confirming plans to integrate advertisements into ChatGPT, GPT-4, GPT-5, or any successor general-purpose GPT model. 

An 'official announcement' is defined as a public statement made directly by OpenAI or its executive leadership. Acceptable sources for resolution include:
1. A blog post, press release, or update on OpenAI's official website (https://openai.com).
2. A post from OpenAI's official X/Twitter account (https://x.com/OpenAI) or other official corporate social media channels.
3. An explicit verbal or written statement by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, or another C-level executive at OpenAI, in a publicized interview, keynote, or official podcast, acknowledging that ad integration is planned, being actively tested, or slated for release.

Leaked code, third-party rumors, news reports based on anonymous sources, or unverified user screenshots will not suffice for a 'Yes' resolution unless accompanied or followed by an official confirmation from OpenAI within the resolution window. If no qualifying announcement occurs between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05 at 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question resolves only upon the actual integration and release of advertisements. Given the recent discoveries of ad-related code in beta versions of the app, an official announcement or public confirmation is a highly probable precursor. Tracking whether an announcement is made by early January provides a strong early crux for forecasters: if OpenAI publicly confirms ad testing or plans in this window, the likelihood of a public rollout by March 31 increases dramatically.

subquestions.question: Will US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin hold an in-person meeting in Budapest, Hungary, between November 11, 2025, and December 11, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question concerns whether any major disruptive military or geopolitical events will occur by the end of 2025, including a "US-Russia nuclear deal" or "Ukraine agrees to give up the rest of Donbas." According to reports from mid-October 2025, US President Donald Trump announced plans to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Budapest, Hungary, facilitated by his relationship with Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban. During a meeting at the White House, Trump mentioned that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's attendance at this potential Budapest summit is "to be determined" (https://www.devdiscourse.com/). Furthermore, Russian President Vladimir Putin has publicly praised Trump's peace efforts and expressed a strong desire to extend the 2010 New START nuclear arms treaty, which Trump has reportedly called "a good idea" (https://www.pbs.org/). The New START treaty limits deployed nuclear weapons, and an extension or replacement is a critical component of US-Russia relations. An in-person meeting between Trump and Putin in Budapest would serve as a critical negotiating forum for both a nuclear arms treaty and the ongoing Ukraine war. Therefore, whether this meeting actually takes place in the near term is a strong early indicator of the likelihood of a US-Russia nuclear deal or a major territorial concession by Ukraine before the end of the year.

Sources:
Devdiscourse: https://www.devdiscourse.com/
PBS: https://www.pbs.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-11 (inclusive), US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin hold an in-person meeting in Budapest, Hungary. The meeting can be bilateral or part of a larger summit, provided both leaders are physically present in the same room and engage in a recognized diplomatic discussion or meeting. 

Resolution will be based on official press releases or statements from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or the Kremlin (http://en.kremlin.ru/), or corroborated reporting from at least three major reliable news agencies (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP News: https://apnews.com/). 

If the meeting is canceled, held exclusively in a city other than Budapest, or postponed such that it does not occur before the end of 2025-12-11, this question resolves No. Virtual, telephonic, or video-conference meetings do not qualify for a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: An in-person summit in Budapest between Trump and Putin is the likeliest venue for negotiating a US-Russia nuclear deal or a Ukraine peace agreement (such as one involving the concession of Donbas). If this planned meeting happens by December 11, it strongly increases the probability of one of the ultimate question's resolution conditions being met before December 31, 2025. If it does not occur, time will be running out for such complex geopolitical agreements to be reached before the ultimate question's deadline.

question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will NATO or any NATO member state officially announce a policy to intercept Russian aerial targets over Ukrainian territory between September 24, 2025, and October 24, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 9-10, 2025, a swarm of Russian drones entered Polish airspace during a bombardment of Ukraine, prompting Polish, Dutch, and Italian fighter jets to shoot down multiple drones over Poland (https://apnews.com/). This unprecedented incident marked the first time NATO forces directly engaged Russian munitions within allied airspace. Following the incursion, Poland invoked Article 4 of the NATO treaty, and the incident spurred urgent discussions about NATO's deterrence posture. According to policy experts, there have been growing calls for NATO to consider extending air-defense coverage into western Ukraine to intercept Russian drones and missiles before they breach allied borders (https://ecfr.eu/). Such a policy shift would actively involve NATO forces in the defense of Ukrainian airspace and has been framed as a vital step to enforce deterrence by punishment against Russia (https://cepa.org/).

Sources:
AP News: https://apnews.com/
European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR): https://ecfr.eu/
Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA): https://cepa.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24 (inclusive), NATO as an organization or the national government of any NATO member state officially announces a policy, decision, or agreement to use its military forces to intercept, shoot down, or otherwise neutralize Russian missiles, drones, or aircraft while those targets are in Ukraine's internationally recognized airspace.

The announcement must be made publicly by an official government or military representative (e.g., a head of state, defense minister, or NATO Secretary General) and be available via credible media outlets or official government websites (such as the Polish Ministry of National Defence at https://www.gov.pl/web/national-defence or NATO's official press portal at https://www.nato.int/). Statements from anonymous sources, rumors, or unconfirmed leaks do not qualify.

The interception policy must explicitly authorize the targeting of Russian aerial assets over Ukraine. If the announcement only reaffirms authorizations for intercepts strictly within NATO airspace, or only involves donating air defense equipment to Ukraine without NATO personnel operating it, the question will not resolve Yes.

If no such official announcement is made between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-24 at 11:59 PM ET, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether there will be a direct military clash between NATO and Russia by the end of 2025. Extending NATO air defense to intercept targets over Ukraine would be a significant escalation, placing NATO operators in a direct combat role against Russian strike packages. This policy shift would heavily increase the risk of Russia retaliating against NATO air defense batteries or a NATO jet accidentally engaging a Russian manned aircraft. Therefore, an official announcement of this policy serves as a highly informative early indicator (crux) of an impending clash.

question: Will the EU impose new tariffs on US goods in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the European Union imposes any new or increased tariffs on the United States between July 23, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any tariff which is officially enacted within the market's time frame will qualify, regardless of when the tariff goes into effect.

Only tariffs specifically targeting the U.S. will qualify. For example, a global tariff (tariffs on all imports into the EU) will not count toward this market's resolution.

Tariffs enacted by EU member states will not count. Only Tariffs imposed by the EU will qualify.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission formally propose new tariffs targeting the United States, or will an EU legislative body vote on such a proposal, between October 31 and November 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In August 2025, the U.S. and the EU reached a framework trade agreement wherein the U.S. applied a 15% tariff on most EU goods, and in return, the EU committed to eliminating tariffs on U.S. industrial goods. The U.S. continues to hold a 27.5% tariff on European automobiles as leverage until the EU enacts these legislative cuts. Tensions remain high due to unpredictable U.S. trade policies, including recent 10% global tariffs affecting over 60 countries. Within the European Union, implementing new tariffs requires a distinct, consensus-driven procedure. The European Commission must first formally propose the trade measure, which is then subject to approval by the member states. The EU maintains a policy of strategic autonomy and separates unilateral sanctions from standard tariff procedures. Given this bureaucratic timeline, any retaliatory or new tariffs fully enacted by the EU against the U.S. by the end of December 2025 would almost certainly need to be formally proposed by the European Commission, or actively voted on, weeks in advance. Therefore, tracking whether the Commission officially proposes tariffs targeted at the U.S. in November serves as a highly informative leading indicator for the ultimate outcome.

Sources:
U.S. and EU flesh out trade commitments under new framework deal: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-eu-flesh-out-trade-commitments-2025.html
US keeping lofty EU car tariffs until levies on American goods cut: https://nypost.com/2025/08/21/business/us-keeping-lofty-eu-car-tariffs-until-levies-on-american-goods-cut/
Tariffs not a cure-all: https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202510/16/WStariffs.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29 (inclusive), the European Commission formally adopts and publishes a legislative proposal, draft implementing act, or draft delegated act to impose new or increased tariffs (or customs duties) specifically targeting the United States. If such a proposal was already published prior to 2025-10-31, this question will also resolve Yes if the Council of the European Union or the European Parliament formally votes on or approves the proposal during the resolution window.

To qualify, the proposed measure must explicitly target imports originating from the United States. Proposals for global tariffs or safeguard measures applied to imports from all countries (such as the recently proposed EU global steel quotas) do not count.

The official action must be publicly announced via an official press release on the European Commission's Press Corner (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en), the Council of the EU's press page (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/), or published in the Official Journal of the European Union (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/oj/direct-access.html) during the resolution window.

The proposed tariffs do not need to be enacted or enter into force during the resolution window; the formal proposal or vote is sufficient to trigger a Yes resolution. If the proposal is delayed or postponed beyond the resolution window, it does not count.

If no qualifying proposal or vote occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-29, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Because the European Union requires consensus among member states and a formal process to enact new tariffs, the European Commission must first issue a formal proposal, followed by legislative voting. If a proposal is made or voted on by late November, it strongly indicates that the EU is on track to officially impose retaliatory tariffs by December 2025. Conversely, the absence of a proposal or vote makes it logistically difficult and politically unlikely for new tariffs to be fully enacted by the December 31 ultimate deadline.

subquestions.question: Will a Notice of Intention to Circulate a Recall Petition against Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass be officially filed with the Los Angeles City Clerk between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass is facing unprecedented political pressure in late 2025. Her administration is grappling with a nearly $1 billion city budget deficit that has led to proposals for 1,600 city employee layoffs and deep agency cuts (https://news.yahoo.com/). Simultaneously, she is managing a high-profile crisis involving immigration protests and the presence of National Guard troops deployed by the federal government, a situation that has intensely tested her leadership (https://thehill.com/). According to a UCLA Luskin School Quality of Life Index survey, her net favorability rating recently dropped to a negative 12 (https://luskin.ucla.edu/). In California, the formal recall process against a local official begins with the filing of a 'Notice of Intention to Circulate a Recall Petition' with the local City Clerk. Given the severity of her compounding crises, public dissatisfaction could easily materialize into an organized recall campaign. A formal recall filing would serve as a powerful indicator of organized opposition, significantly increasing the probability that Bass could be forced out or choose to resign in 2025.

Sources:
- LA City Clerk Recall Process: https://clerk.lacity.gov/clerk-divisions/elections/petition-process
- Yahoo News: https://news.yahoo.com/
- The Hill: https://thehill.com/
- UCLA Luskin School: https://luskin.ucla.edu/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a 'Notice of Intention to Circulate a Recall Petition' explicitly targeting Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass is officially filed with or formally accepted by the Los Angeles City Clerk between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

The filing must be verifiable via the official Los Angeles City Clerk's website (https://clerk.lacity.gov/) or confirmed by reporting from at least two credible news organizations, such as the Los Angeles Times (https://www.latimes.com/) or CBS Los Angeles (https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/).

If multiple notices are filed, at least one must be submitted within this specified date window. If a notice of intention was filed prior to 2025-09-01 and remains active, but no new notice is filed between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, this question resolves No. If no such notice is filed during the resolution window, the question resolves No. Any petition that is delayed or submitted after 2025-10-01 will not count toward a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A formal recall effort is a severe threat to a sitting mayor. If a Notice of Intention is filed during this one-month window, it signifies that public dissatisfaction has escalated into an organized, legal mechanism for her removal. Even if a potential recall election would not occur until after 2025, the presence of a formal recall campaign drastically increases political pressure, making an early resignation or political collapse much more likely. Conversely, the absence of a recall filing suggests that despite low approval ratings, opposition remains disorganized, thereby increasing the likelihood she finishes out the year.

question: Will US or Israel strike Iran by December 31, 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US or Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on Iranian soil or any official Iranian embassy or consulate between the time of this market's creation and the listed date (ET). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US or Israeli military forces that impact Iranian ground territory or any official Iranian embassy or consulate (e.g., if a weapons depot on Iranian soil is hit by an US or Israeli missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones which are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether they land on Iranian territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US or Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. government explicitly confirm or condemn the execution of any Iranian protesters between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19?

By mid-January 2026, reports indicated nearly 2,600 deaths associated with the unrest. Amidst these tensions, U.S. President Donald Trump voiced support for the Iranian demonstrators, explicitly warning Tehran that the U.S. would take 'very strong action' if protesters are executed. Concurrently, the U.S. has advised some personnel at the Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar to evacuate or reposition, citing threats from Iranian forces. Because the U.S. administration has drawn a clear red line regarding the execution of protesters, official confirmation or condemnation of such executions by the U.S. government would serve as a strong leading indicator of impending military action or strikes against Iran.

Sources:
