News18: Missiles That Think, Bombs That Dig - https://www.news18.com/world/
U.S. Department of State Press Releases - https://www.state.gov/press-releases/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if the White House, the U.S. Department of State, or the President of the United States explicitly confirms or condemns the execution of one or more protesters by the Iranian government between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19 (inclusive).

To satisfy this condition, an official statement, press release, or briefing transcript must be published on whitehouse.gov or state.gov, or a public statement must be posted on the official X (formerly Twitter) accounts of the President (@POTUS or @realDonaldTrump) or the Secretary of State between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19.

The statement must explicitly acknowledge that the Iranian government has 'executed', 'hanged', or 'put to death' individuals in connection with the recent or ongoing nationwide protests. The statement must refer to the actual carrying out of the execution, not merely the handing down of a death sentence.

If no such qualifying statement or post is issued between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-19, the question will resolve 'No'. If a scheduled official press briefing or announcement regarding this specific matter is officially postponed beyond the resolution window, the question should be considered unresolvable. Delayed confirmations published after the resolution window will not count toward a 'Yes' resolution. In the event that the primary websites are down, official archives or widely reported video evidence of such press briefings (e.g., C-SPAN) may be used as fallback criteria.

Resolution Sources:
The White House Briefing Room: https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/
U.S. Department of State Press Releases: https://www.state.gov/press-releases/
President's Official X Account: https://x.com/POTUS
Secretary of State's Official X Account: https://x.com/SecState
subquestions.rationale: U.S. President Donald Trump has publicly drawn a red line, warning of 'very strong action' if Iranian protesters are executed. If the U.S. government officially confirms that such executions have taken place, it dramatically increases the political pressure and likelihood of the U.S. launching a retaliatory or preemptive strike on Iran before the end of 2026. Conversely, if no executions are confirmed during this period, it suggests Iran may be exercising restraint, thereby lowering the immediate probability of a U.S. or Israeli strike.

question: California redistricting referendum passes?
description:
Proposition 50 is a 2025 legislatively referred constitutional amendment on congressional redistricting, proposed for the statewide special election in California currently set for November 4, 2025.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Proposition 50 or any other legislatively referred statewide measure that authorizes or implements congressional redistricting is approved by a majority of voters at the California statewide special election currently set for November 4, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

If by the last legally operative deadline for placing measures on the November 4, 2025 statewide ballot—including any deadline set or modified by the statute calling that special election—no qualifying legislatively referred measure has been approved for submission to voters, and there is no enacted statute or pending court order that could still place such a measure on that ballot, the market will resolve “No”.

If the election is officially rescheduled, the same rule applies to the new ballot and its corresponding deadlines.

The resolution source will be based on the official certified results of the vote as published by  State of California. Subsequent litigation, administrative challenges, or failure of any post-approval triggers will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will a poll published by the Public Policy Institute of California (PPIC) or UC Berkeley IGS between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 show support for California Proposition 50 at 50% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
California's Proposition 50 is a legislatively referred constitutional amendment on the November 4, 2025 ballot. The measure would allow the state legislature to temporarily replace the state's independent redistricting commission and redraw congressional maps for the 2026, 2028, and 2030 elections (Los Angeles Magazine, https://lamag.com). A Berkeley IGS poll conducted August 11-17, 2025, found that 48% of registered voters supported the measure, 32% opposed it, and 20% were undecided (Medium, https://medium.com). Whether the "Yes" campaign can cross the majority threshold in leading independent state polls leading up to the election is a crucial early indicator of its ultimate passage. The Public Policy Institute of California (PPIC) and UC Berkeley's Institute of Governmental Studies (IGS) are California's premier nonpartisan polling organizations.

Sources:
Los Angeles Magazine: https://lamag.com
Medium: https://medium.com
PPIC Polling: https://www.ppic.org/polling/
Berkeley IGS: https://igs.berkeley.edu/igs-poll/current-and-past-polls
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the Public Policy Institute of California (PPIC) or the UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies (IGS) officially publishes a statewide poll regarding the November 2025 special election, and the topline result for Proposition 50 (or the referenced 'redistricting constitutional amendment') shows 50.0% or higher support (e.g., 'Yes', 'Favor', or 'Support').

Specific conditions:
- The support level will be evaluated based on the primary sample reported in the poll's headline, press release, or executive summary (e.g., Likely Voters if reported; if not, Registered Voters).
- The required threshold is 50.0%. If the poll reports integer percentages, 50% counts as Yes. If decimals are provided, it must be 50.0% or higher (e.g., 49.8% resolves No).
- If multiple qualifying polls are published by these organizations within the timeframe, the question resolves Yes if AT LEAST ONE poll meets or exceeds the 50.0% threshold.
- If neither organization publishes a poll explicitly asking about Proposition 50 within the resolution window, or if no such poll reaches the 50.0% threshold, the question resolves No.
- Delayed events: If a poll is announced or conducted in the timeframe, but the results are published after 2025-10-01, it will not count towards resolution.

Data sources to be used for resolution:
- Official releases on PPIC's website (https://www.ppic.org/polling/)
- Official releases on Berkeley IGS's website (https://igs.berkeley.edu/igs-poll/current-and-past-polls)
subquestions.rationale: Polling is the most direct indicator of voter sentiment for state ballot measures. A mid-August Berkeley IGS poll showed support at 48%, slightly below the majority needed for passage but with 20% undecided. If a highly-rated California pollster demonstrates that support has crossed the critical 50% threshold by October, it would serve as a robust crux indicating that the "Yes" campaign is capturing sufficient undecided voters, heavily increasing the probability that the referendum ultimately passes on November 4.

question: Will Ukraine agree to give up Russian territory in Kursk?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede territory under its control in Russia’s Kursk Oblast is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. If Russia regains territory in the Kursk Oblast through military action, or if Ukraine unilaterally cedes Russian territory absent of a diplomatic process or agreement, this will not qualify for a “Yes” resolution. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will a fourth round of direct peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine be officially announced or commence before the end of November 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Direct peace negotiations between Russia and Ukraine have seen intermittent progress throughout 2025. Following a highly publicized summit between U.S. and Russian leaders in Alaska, a third round of direct talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations was held in Istanbul on July 23, 2025. These talks addressed political, military, and humanitarian issues, including the transfer of deceased soldiers' bodies and prisoner exchanges. Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky stated that the occurrence of a fourth round of negotiations would depend on the implementation of these agreements. However, as of October 2025, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Galuzin claimed the positive momentum was fading and that Ukraine was not serious about making a deal, although communication lines remain open. At the same time, diplomatic pressure regarding territorial swaps has intensified; Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the Donetsk region, while Ukraine continues to hold a pocket of territory in Russia's Kursk Oblast. For any diplomatic agreement to be reached where Ukraine cedes the Russian territory it controls by the end of December 2025, formal negotiations must resume.

Sources:
TASS (Russian News Agency): https://tass.com/politics
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com
Euractiv: https://www.euractiv.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a fourth round of direct peace negotiations (or an equivalent formal bilateral peace summit) between official delegations of the Russian Federation and Ukraine is officially announced OR officially commences between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

- The negotiations must involve official government delegations from both Russia and Ukraine meeting either in-person or in a formally organized, officially recognized online session aimed at a peace settlement or territorial agreement.
- Routine low-level communications, prisoner exchanges, or working groups strictly limited to humanitarian issues (such as body transfers) do not qualify, unless they are explicitly designated by both parties as part of a formal resumption of peace negotiations or a comprehensive peace negotiation framework.
- If the talks are announced before 2025-10-31, the question will only resolve Yes if the talks actually commence between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30.
- If the talks are announced between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 but are scheduled for a date after 2025-11-30, the question will still resolve Yes, as the milestone of an official announcement within the window was met.
- Official confirmation must come from the Ukrainian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mfa.gov.ua/en), the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mid.ru/en/), or an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP News: https://apnews.com/).
subquestions.rationale: For Ukraine to officially agree to cede Russian territory in Kursk as part of a diplomatic agreement by December 31, 2025, formal diplomatic negotiations between Russia and Ukraine must take place. Following the third round of direct talks in July 2025, negotiations stalled. The announcement or commencement of a fourth round of talks in November 2025 would serve as a critical leading indicator that a comprehensive peace or territorial deal is actively being negotiated, significantly increasing the probability of a 'Yes' resolution on the ultimate question. Conversely, if no formal negotiations are announced or held by November 30, the timeline for reaching a finalized agreement by the end of December becomes highly improbable.

question: Will Polymarket mindshare hit 80%?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Polymarket has at least the specified daily mindshare, as shown on the Kaito Information Markets Arena page (https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets) at any point between November 20, 2025, and March 31, 2026 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only finalized daily results from the Polymarket mindshare percentage shown on the Kaito Info Markets page at https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets, specifically the daily values for Polymarket under 'Historical Data', will be used to resolve this market. Values will be considered final once the value for the subsequent day has been released.

The resolution source for this market is the Kaito Info Markets page found at https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets. If this resolution source is unavailable at check time, this market will remain open until the Kaito Info Markets page comes back online and resolve based on the first check after it becomes available. If it becomes permanently unavailable, this market will resolve based on the latest available data.

Note: the resolution source for this market will be the Kaito Info Markets page (https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets), which reports the platform’s mindshare as a percentage to two decimal places (e.g., 66.56%). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

subquestions.question: Will Polymarket's U.S. platform launch at least one non-sports prediction market by January 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Polymarket recently re-entered the U.S. market in December 2025 by launching a waitlist-based mobile app, initially offering only sports betting markets (such as NFL and NBA games). While the platform built its reputation and massive 2024 volume on political and current event markets, its current U.S. offering is delayed on these fronts. Competitors like Kalshi already offer political and economic markets to U.S. users. If Polymarket successfully expands its U.S. platform to include non-sports markets (such as elections, economic data, or crypto events) in the near term, it would likely trigger a massive surge in trading volume and social media engagement. This expansion is a key catalyst that could propel Polymarket's mindshare on Kaito above the 80% threshold.

Sources:
Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/polymarket-starts-reopening-us-site-2025-12-03.html
Cryptopolitan: https://www.cryptopolitan.com/polymarket-launches-waitlist-app-in-u-s/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-21 and 2026-01-20 (inclusive), Polymarket officially enables U.S. users (even if restricted to waitlist members) to trade on at least one market that is NOT related to sports on its U.S. platform (such as via the Polymarket U.S. app or polymarket.us). 

A 'non-sports market' is defined as any prediction market that is not related to the outcomes, statistics, or events within an athletic or sporting competition (e.g., NFL, NBA, NHL, UFC). Examples of qualifying non-sports markets include political elections, economic data releases, cryptocurrency prices, or entertainment awards.

Verification will be based on official announcements from Polymarket's official X account (https://x.com/Polymarket), its official blog (https://polymarket.com/blog), or credible major media reporting confirming that U.S. users are able to place trades on non-sports events. If U.S. users remain restricted exclusively to sports markets by 23:59 UTC on January 20, 2026, or if the platform suspends U.S. access entirely, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Polymarket's dominance in mindshare historically stems from its political and current events markets. With its U.S. platform currently limited to sports betting, adding non-sports markets is a critical milestone. If they achieve this by January 20, 2026, it will significantly boost their U.S. user engagement and social media mentions, acting as a strong leading indicator for reaching the 80% mindshare target against competitors.

question: Will Trump try to fire Powell in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing Jerome Powell as Chair of the Federal Reserve before his term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a federal lawsuit be filed by Lisa Cook, the Federal Reserve, or the Trump administration regarding Cook's removal from the Federal Reserve Board before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 26, 2025, President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that he had fired Federal Reserve Board member Lisa Cook, citing "gross negligence" and "potentially criminal" actions related to alleged mortgage fraud. Cook and her legal team stated she will not resign and that Trump lacks the authority to remove her, as Federal Reserve governors can only be removed "for cause" under the Federal Reserve Act. The Fed indicated it might pursue legal action to prevent the president's "attempted illegal action" (The Independent, https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/trump-lisa-cook-federal-reserve-b2601718.html). Because Trump has also heavily criticized Fed Chair Jerome Powell, the legal and political fallout from his attempt to fire Cook serves as a direct precedent. The outcome of this standoff—specifically whether it escalates into a formal court battle—will act as a strong indicator of Trump's willingness and legal capability to challenge the Fed's independence and potentially target Powell next.

Sources:
CBS News - https://www.cbsnews.com/
The Independent - https://www.independent.co.uk/
Mediaite - https://www.mediaite.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), a lawsuit or formal legal complaint is filed in a United States federal court by Lisa Cook, the Federal Reserve (or its representatives), Donald Trump, or the US federal government (e.g., the Department of Justice) that explicitly seeks to enforce, block, or clarify the legal status of Lisa Cook's removal from the Federal Reserve Board of Governors. The filing must be docketed within this exact time window. Resolution will be determined by reviewing official federal court dockets via the Public Access to Court Electronic Records (PACER) system (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) or through a consensus of credible reporting from major financial and political news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, https://www.bloomberg.com/; Reuters, https://www.reuters.com/). If no such lawsuit is docketed between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 at 11:59 PM ET, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The unprecedented attempt to remove Governor Lisa Cook is a clear test of the president's power to fire independent Fed officials "for cause." If the dispute escalates into a formal lawsuit within the next month, it demonstrates that Trump's administration is actively litigating the boundaries of Fed independence, increasing the probability he will formally move against Jerome Powell. Conversely, if no legal action is taken and the firing remains a social media statement without legal enforcement, it signals a lower probability that Trump will take formal, legally binding action to fire Powell.

question: Will Donald Trump visit Germany in 2025?
description:
If U.S. President Donald Trump visits a listed country between January 15 and December 31, 2025 11:59 PM ET, the relevant market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the White House officially announce a planned trip by President Donald Trump to Germany for 2025, between October 1, 2025 and October 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
U.S. President Donald Trump has historically had a complex relationship with Germany. During his first term, he only visited Germany once for the 2017 G20 summit and has yet to make a formal bilateral visit to the country (Statista, 2025-09-16). In June 2025, Germany's new leader, Chancellor Friedrich Merz, visited the Oval Office to discuss trade, Ukraine, and Trump's threats of 50% tariffs on EU goods (CFR, 2025-06-05). For a presidential state or working visit to occur before the end of 2025, advance planning and an official announcement would be expected weeks in advance to allow for security and diplomatic preparations. Tracking whether a formal announcement is made in October acts as a strong leading indicator of whether the ultimate visit will materialize before the year concludes.

Sources:
Council on Foreign Relations - https://www.cfr.org/
Statista - https://www.statista.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-22 (inclusive), the White House issues an official statement, press release, public schedule, or briefing transcript confirming that President Donald Trump will travel to Germany before December 31, 2025. The announcement must be published on the official White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or through the President's verified social media accounts (e.g., https://twitter.com/POTUS) within the resolution window. The announcement must explicitly name Germany as a destination for an upcoming trip in 2025. Announcements stating the trip will occur in 2026 or later, or announcements that solely involve German officials visiting the U.S. or meeting Trump in a third country, do not qualify for a Yes resolution. If no such qualifying announcement is made by the end of the resolution window on 2025-10-22 at 23:59 UTC, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Presidential international travel requires immense logistical and security preparation, meaning trips are nearly always publicly announced weeks before the actual visit. If Trump is to physically visit Germany before the end of 2025, an official announcement during early-to-mid October serves as a highly reliable crux for the ultimate question.

question: Will NVIDIA be the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31, 2025, as of market close.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the daily closing market capitalization of either Apple (AAPL) or Microsoft (MSFT) exceed that of Nvidia (NVDA) on any trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13?
subquestions.background_information:
Nvidia has seen unprecedented growth due to its dominance in AI hardware. As of September 30, 2025, Nvidia reached a record market capitalization of $4.53 trillion, securing its position as the world's most valuable company, ahead of Apple and Microsoft. For Nvidia to finish the year as the second-largest company by market cap, it would need to be surpassed by at least one of its major rivals (most likely Apple or Microsoft). The tech sector often experiences significant volatility around quarterly earnings reports, and both Apple and Microsoft typically report earnings in late October. Tracking whether either company can temporarily or permanently overtake Nvidia in market cap during the mid-October to mid-November window provides a clear indicator of the competitive dynamics and Nvidia's likelihood of dropping to the number two spot by the end of December.

Sources:
Yahoo Finance NVDA: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA
Yahoo Finance AAPL: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL
Yahoo Finance MSFT: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MSFT
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the daily closing market capitalization of either Apple Inc. (AAPL) or Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) is strictly greater than the daily closing market capitalization of Nvidia Corporation (NVDA) on any regular U.S. stock market trading day between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 (inclusive). 

The resolution will be based on the official daily closing market capitalization data provided by Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MSFT) as of the close of regular trading (4:00 PM ET). Intraday market cap fluctuations do not count; only the final closing value for the day is considered. In the event of data discrepancies or if Yahoo Finance is unavailable, alternative credible financial data providers such as YCharts (https://ycharts.com) or standard Bloomberg terminal data will be used as a fallback. If neither Apple nor Microsoft closes with a higher market cap than Nvidia during the defined period, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: For Nvidia to resolve as the 'second-largest' company at the end of the year, it must relinquish its current position as the largest company. If Apple or Microsoft overtakes Nvidia in market cap between mid-October and mid-November (a period often catalyzed by Q3 earnings reports), it proves Nvidia's lead is vulnerable, significantly increasing the probability that Nvidia might finish the year in the number two spot. Conversely, if Nvidia maintains its lead through its rivals' earnings season, its chances of remaining the largest company through year-end are much higher.

question: GOP uses 'Nuclear Option' to break filibuster by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Senate passes a motion to invoke cloture and end debate on any part of the legislative process, with such a cloture motion receiving Yea votes from fewer than three-fifths of the Senators by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve "No".

Confirmations are considered part of the Senate’s “advice and consent” function, not part of the Senate’s “legislative process,” and will therefore not count towards this market's resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. government.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate successfully invoke cloture on a government funding bill with 60 or more Yea votes between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal government is currently in a shutdown that has lasted at least 21 days as of late October 2025, tying it for the second-longest in history (https://baynews9.com). In response to the legislative deadlock, several House Republicans, such as Rep. Chip Roy and Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, have called for the Senate to invoke the "nuclear option"—changing Senate rules to bypass the 60-vote filibuster threshold and pass a Continuing Resolution (CR) with a simple majority (https://thehill.com, https://easternprogress.com). While Senate Republicans recently used the nuclear option in September 2025 to streamline the confirmation of Trump administration executive nominees (https://washingtontimes.com), Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Speaker Mike Johnson have thus far opposed using it for legislation, with Thune warning that the legislative filibuster "makes the Senate the Senate" (https://baynews9.com).

The ultimate question is whether the GOP will eliminate the legislative filibuster by December 31, 2025. If the Senate is able to reach a bipartisan agreement and invoke cloture on a funding bill with the standard 60 votes by November 30, the immediate shutdown crisis will be resolved conventionally, significantly lowering the odds of the nuclear option being deployed for legislation this year. Conversely, if no such 60-vote threshold is met, the continuing shutdown will maximize pressure on GOP leadership to change the rules.

Sources:
Spectrum News Bay News 9: https://baynews9.com
The Hill: https://thehill.com
Washington Times: https://washingtontimes.com
Eastern Progress: https://easternprogress.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the U.S. Senate holds a successful roll call vote to invoke cloture on a bill, joint resolution, or continuing resolution that provides appropriations for the federal government, and the cloture motion receives 60 or more "Yea" votes, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

The primary resolution source will be the official U.S. Senate roll call vote tracker (https://www.senate.gov/legislative/votes_new.htm). 

The legislative item in question must provide continuing or regular appropriations to fund federal government operations (e.g., a Continuing Resolution or a regular appropriations bill). Cloture votes on other unrelated legislation do not count towards resolution.

If no such successful cloture vote with 60 or more Yea votes occurs on a funding bill between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the question resolves "No". Furthermore, if the funding dispute is resolved via unanimous consent, a voice vote, or by the Senate invoking the nuclear option (which would allow cloture to be invoked with fewer than 60 votes), this question will also resolve "No".
subquestions.rationale: The primary catalyst right now for potentially using the legislative nuclear option is the ongoing government shutdown. If the Senate successfully invokes cloture on a funding bill with the standard 60 votes, it demonstrates that a bipartisan consensus was reached, removing the immediate crisis pushing the GOP to change the legislative filibuster rules. This event would heavily update forecasters toward a 'No' on the ultimate question. Alternatively, a failure to reach 60 votes implies either a prolonged shutdown or a procedural rule change, increasing the probability of a 'Yes' outcome.

question: Will the federal government be shut down for 10–29 days in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

Days are counted based on notices checked at 10:00 AM ET each day. If the Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown, this will count; however, announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather will not qualify. 

If there are multiple government shutdowns during the relevant period, this market only applies to the first shutdown, as the market will resolve after the end of the first shutdown. Notices of emergency furloughs or impacted government operations count toward the shutdown days.  

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

The resolution source for this market will be the website of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. President sign a Continuing Resolution (CR) or other appropriations legislation into law between September 17, 2025 and September 30, 2025, to avert an October 1 government shutdown?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. fiscal year ends on September 30, 2025. Congress must pass new appropriations to fund the federal government for Fiscal Year 2026. According to the National Law Review, as of early September 2025, lawmakers are behind schedule: the Senate has passed only three of twelve appropriations bills, and the House only two. If a Continuing Resolution (CR) or other comprehensive funding legislation is not signed into law by midnight on September 30, 2025, a partial federal government shutdown will occur starting October 1, 2025. A shutdown would furlough hundreds of thousands of non-essential federal employees and suspend non-essential operations. Prediction markets have recently shown a 43% chance of a government shutdown by the end of 2025, highlighting the severe risk of political gridlock. This subquestion focuses on whether Congress and the President can successfully enact a stopgap or permanent funding measure before the deadline.

Sources:
Over 43% chance of U.S. government shutdown in 2025: Polymarket (TheStreet) - https://www.thestreet.com/
When could a government shutdown occur? How would it affect you? (Aol) - https://www.aol.com/
Potential Outcomes If Congress Misses the Federal Funding Deadline (The National Law Review) - https://www.natlawreview.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a Continuing Resolution (CR) or any other comprehensive appropriations legislation that provides funding for the federal government past October 1, 2025, is signed into law by the President of the United States on or before 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2025. 

The legislation must prevent a lapse in appropriations for all regular federal agencies on October 1, 2025. The overall resolution window during which qualifying events and confirmation can occur is between the subquestion start date of 2025-09-17 and the end date of 2025-10-02.

The primary resolution sources will be the official legislation tracker on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/) and official statements from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/legislation/).

If the President signs qualifying legislation funding the government past October 1, 2025 within the specified window, the question resolves Yes. If the deadline of 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2025 passes without such legislation being signed, triggering a lapse in appropriations for the start of the fiscal year, the question resolves No. If legislation is passed by Congress but not signed by the President by the 11:59 PM ET September 30 deadline, it does not count and the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The failure to pass a funding bill by September 30 is the direct trigger for an October 1 shutdown. If a bill is signed into law, an October 1 shutdown is averted, which significantly reduces the probability of a 10-29 day shutdown occurring in 2025 (though a shutdown could theoretically happen later if a CR expires in late 2025). Conversely, if no bill is signed, a shutdown begins immediately, drastically increasing the likelihood that the ultimate 10-29 day shutdown threshold will be met.

question: Taylor Swift holds top ten spots on the Billboard Hot 100 for the week of October 18th?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Taylor Swift holds the top 10 spots (1-10) on the Billboard Hot 100 chart for the week titled “week of October 18, 2025”. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The resolution source will be Billboard.com

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift occupy all 10 of the top 10 positions on the Spotify Daily Top Songs USA chart for any single day between October 3, 2025 and October 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Taylor Swift is set to release her 12th studio album, 'The Life of a Showgirl', on October 3, 2025. The album has already broken the Spotify record for the most pre-saved album Countdown Page, setting expectations for a massive streaming debut (https://www.euronews.com). Swift previously set records with her 2024 album 'The Tortured Poets Department', becoming the first artist to occupy the top 14 positions on the Billboard Hot 100 (https://www.forbes.com). The Billboard Hot 100 ranking formula relies heavily on U.S. streaming data, making Spotify's Daily Top Songs USA chart a vital leading indicator for Billboard chart performance. If Swift manages to sweep the top 10 on the Spotify USA daily chart in the days immediately following her album release, it will serve as a highly informative crux for her likelihood of sweeping the top 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 for the week of October 18, 2025.

Sources:
Euronews: https://www.euronews.com
Forbes: https://www.forbes.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if Taylor Swift is credited as an artist (primary, co-lead, or featured) on all of the top 10 songs (positions 1 through 10, inclusive) on the Spotify Daily Top Songs USA chart for any single daily tracking period between October 3, 2025, and October 8, 2025 (inclusive). 

The resolution window for this subquestion is between the start date of 2025-10-01 and the end date of 2025-10-10. This means the qualifying event must occur and be verifiable via published chart data between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10.

The primary resolution source will be the official Spotify Charts (https://charts.spotify.com/charts/view/regional-us-daily/latest). Third-party data trackers such as Kworb (https://kworb.net/spotify/country/us_daily.html) may be used as a fallback if the official Spotify charts site is unavailable or if historical daily data for the dates in question is needed to verify the outcome. If Swift does not occupy all 10 of the top 10 spots on any single daily chart in this timeframe, or if such an event is not recorded and verifiable before the end of the resolution window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The Billboard Hot 100 calculation heavily weights U.S. streaming metrics alongside radio airplay and sales. A dominant streaming performance—specifically sweeping the top 10 of the U.S. daily Spotify chart during the new album's debut week—is a crucial leading indicator. If she achieves this on Spotify, forecasters will have strong observable evidence to update their probabilities toward a 'Yes' on the ultimate Billboard Hot 100 question.

question: Will Michael Jackson be named in newly released Epstein files?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump Administration (including any federal court) publicly releases previously unreleased files pertaining to the illegal activities of Jeffrey Epstein which contain any mention of the listed individual between July 16 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only previously unreleased files which contain novel material not previously available to the public will qualify. Documents that are merely re-released, have had redactions removed, repackaged, or newly publicized versions of already available information do not qualify.

Any mention of the listed individual in connection with Jeffrey Epstein will qualify, regardless of if connected to nefarious or illegal activities.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) publicly announce it is withholding or delaying the release of any Epstein-related documents citing an ongoing investigation between November 30, 2025, and December 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Donald Trump signed the Epstein Files Transparency Act into law on November 20, 2025, which legally obligates the Department of Justice to release all unclassified investigative materials related to Jeffrey Epstein by December 19, 2025 (https://www.chicagotribune.com). This release is expected to include FBI reports, witness transcripts, flight logs, and internal communications. Although the law forbids redactions intended solely to protect the reputations of public figures, the DOJ retains the authority to withhold files if their release would jeopardize an active investigation (https://globalnews.ca). Attorney General Pam Bondi recently launched a new investigation into Epstein's associates and political adversaries, which could serve as a justification for the DOJ to temporarily delay or withhold significant portions of the files (https://www.pbs.org). Prediction markets and the public are heavily speculating on which high-profile names, including Michael Jackson, will appear in the new documents, though Jackson was previously named in earlier releases without allegations of wrongdoing (https://www.financialexpress.com). The completeness of the December document dump is central to whether novel information about Jackson will be published.

Sources:
Global News - The Epstein files: What to know ahead of their release (https://globalnews.ca)
PBS - 7 things to know about the Justice Department's Epstein files (https://www.pbs.org)
Chicago Tribune - What to know about the Justice Department's Jeffrey Epstein files (https://www.chicagotribune.com)
The Financial Express - Epstein Files: From Elon Musk to Leonardo DiCaprio (https://www.financialexpress.com)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), the Attorney General, or an official spokesperson for the DOJ publicly announces or confirms in a legal filing, press release, or public statement that it is withholding or delaying the release of one or more documents related to Jeffrey Epstein, specifically citing an ongoing or active investigation as the reason, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-15 (inclusive). The announcement must occur within this specified time window. A general statement that the DOJ 'might' withhold documents does not count; the DOJ must affirmatively state that they are withholding or delaying specific documents, a category of documents, or the entire release due to an ongoing investigation (such as the newly launched probe by Attorney General Pam Bondi). If the release is delayed or withheld for other reasons (e.g., technical difficulties, privacy redactions of victims) without citing an ongoing investigation, this question resolves No. If the deadline passes without any such announcement, it resolves No. Delayed events: if the DOJ makes this announcement after 2025-12-15, it will not count toward resolution and the question resolves No. Authoritative sources for resolution include official DOJ press releases (https://www.justice.gov/news/press-releases) and court filings via PACER (https://pacer.uscourts.gov/), supplemented by credible reporting from major news outlets such as the Associated Press (https://apnews.com/).
subquestions.rationale: The Epstein Files Transparency Act mandates the release of all unclassified Epstein files by December 19, 2025. The ultimate question resolves Yes if Michael Jackson is named in newly released files by December 31, 2025. A major crux for this outcome is whether the DOJ will fully comply with the December 19 deadline or use exceptions to withhold documents. The recently announced investigation by AG Pam Bondi provides a legal mechanism for the DOJ to withhold materials. If the DOJ announces it will withhold documents due to this active investigation before December 15, the scope of the new document release will be significantly reduced or delayed, heavily decreasing the likelihood that novel documents naming Michael Jackson will be released by the end of the year. Conversely, no such announcement strongly implies the impending release of the full corpus of documents.

question: U.S. Government funding lapse on October 1?
description:

A funding lapse is defined as the President failing to sign the relevant bill(s) extending government funding by September 30, 11:59 PM ET. If a bill extending the funding of the U.S. government is passed and signed by the acting President before October 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes" any funding lapse will count. If only a portion of the US government is covered by any signed bill(s) extending funding of the US government, and a portion of the US government goes unfunded, this market will still resolve to "Yes".

The primary resolution for this source will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass a continuing resolution (CR) or any bill extending federal government funding beyond September 30, 2025, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26?
subquestions.background_information: Congress faces a September 30 deadline to pass funding legislation for the new fiscal year beginning October 1, 2025, or face a partial government shutdown. As of late August 2025, the House has passed only a few appropriations bills, and a stopgap continuing resolution (CR) is expected to be necessary to avoid a lapse in funding (https://thehill.com). Democratic leaders Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries recently sent a letter to GOP leaders urging immediate 'four corners' negotiations for a stop-gap measure. Furthermore, Representative Steve Womack noted that the chances for a shutdown are very high given the few session days remaining (https://talkbusiness.net). Passing a CR or a funding package in the House is a crucial step; if the House has not passed any funding extension by September 26, the timeline to get a bill through the Senate and signed by the President before October 1 becomes extremely tight, significantly increasing the probability of a shutdown. Sources: The Hill (https://thehill.com), Talk Business & Politics (https://talkbusiness.net), Military Times (https://www.militarytimes.com).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes a bill that extends funding for the federal government (such as a Continuing Resolution or an omnibus appropriations package covering the majority of federal agencies) for the fiscal year beginning October 1, 2025, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26 (inclusive). Passage must occur before 11:59 PM ET on September 26, 2025. Resolution will be determined by official roll call vote or voice vote records from the Office of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives (https://clerk.house.gov/Votes) or Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov). To qualify, the bill must be specifically intended to prevent a lapse in appropriations on October 1, 2025 (e.g., providing funding past September 30, 2025). If no such bill is passed by the House between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-26, the question resolves No. If passage is delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A funding bill must be passed by both chambers of Congress before being signed by the President. If the House passes a funding extension by September 26, the chances of avoiding a shutdown increase substantially because the legislative process is moving forward. If they fail to do so, the timeline to avert an October 1 shutdown becomes extremely compressed, making this a strong early indicator.

question: 5kt meteor strike in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a natural meteoroid (bolide) explodes in Earth's atmosphere with a total impact energy greater or equal to 5 kilotons of TNT equivalent between May 28, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The object must be classified as a natural meteoroid; events involving artificial objects or reentry vehicles do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/. The relevant field for determining impact energy is the “Impact Energy (kt)” column. If this dataset has not been updated to include all relevant dates by February 28, 2026, or if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository becomes permanently unavailable, this market may resolve based on a consensus of credible sources including the European Space Agency (ESA), the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN), the U.S. Department of Defense, or credible reporting of a scientific consensus, such as a NASA press release.

subquestions.question: Will the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository record at least 3 distinct fireball events occurring between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Fireballs and bolides are exceptionally bright meteors resulting from meteoroids entering Earth's atmosphere. NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) maintains a public repository of these events (https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/), documenting their date, time, and calculated impact energy. The frequency of smaller, detectable meteor events acts as a proxy for the baseline influx of meteoroids and the current sensitivity of Earth's detection networks. On average, the CNEOS database logs approximately 30 to 40 fireball events annually, which equates to roughly 2 to 4 events per month. For example, recent news highlighted a 1.6 kiloton fireball over southern Japan on August 19, 2025, demonstrating ongoing active detections (https://watchers.news). Because meteoroid sizes roughly follow a power-law distribution, an increased or average baseline count of smaller fireballs can indicate whether Earth is passing through higher-density debris fields, which provides context for the likelihood of a much larger (≥5 kt) meteor impact later in the year.

Sources:
NASA JPL Fireball Database: https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/
Watchers News (August 2025 Event): https://watchers.news
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the NASA JPL Fireball and Bolide Data repository (https://cneos.jpl.nasa.gov/fireballs/) records at least 3 distinct fireball events with a 'Date/Time (UT)' occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive of both dates). The events must be officially listed in the 'Date/Time (UT)' column of the database. The resolution will be based on the data available on the CNEOS repository as of the end of the resolution window. If the NASA JPL repository is permanently unavailable or not updated by the end date, the question may resolve based on a consensus of credible alternatives tracking the same metrics, such as the European Space Agency (ESA) or the International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN). Events involving artificial objects or space debris do not count toward this total.
subquestions.rationale: Forecasting the ultimate outcome of a 5 kt impact depends heavily on understanding the current rate of meteoroid influx and the operational reliability of atmospheric detection networks. Tracking the general count of smaller fireball events over a one-month window serves as an observable, near-term metric for baseline meteoroid activity without simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline or tighter energy constraint. A healthy detection rate indicates that sensor systems are online and functioning normally, while a potential spike could indicate a dense debris stream.

subquestions.question: Will the COMEX Gold Continuous Contract (GCW00) close below $4,000 per troy ounce on any trading day between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?

By late August, COMEX Gold had rebounded, settling at $3,431.80 (https://www.morningstar.com), and by late September, the front-month contract reached $3,736.90 (https://www.morningstar.com). In mid-October 2025, gold decisively broke through the $4,000 per ounce psychological and technical resistance level, with market analysts projecting $4,000 to act as a new support floor (https://talkmarkets.com). Given that the ultimate question asks if gold will close the year between $3,900 and $4,000, it is crucial to monitor whether this new $4,000 support level holds or if prices pull back below it. This subquestion focuses on whether COMEX Gold will close below $4,000 at any point during November 2025, which would serve as a strong indicator that the price might end the year within the $3,900-$4,000 bracket rather than staying in 'blue sky territory' above $4,000.

Morningstar: https://www.morningstar.com

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce definitive agreements to restructure away from its non-profit board control by October 31, 2025?

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

subquestions.rationale: Sam Altman currently does not hold equity, and reports indicate that he will only receive an equity grant after OpenAI restructures its non-profit governance model into a for-profit framework. Because completing a corporate restructuring takes time, achieving definitive agreements in October 2025 is a critical milestone if Altman is to receive his equity by December 31, 2025. question: Will Kim Keon Hee be sentenced to prison by March 31?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the prosecution formally demand a prison sentence of 5 years or more for Kim Keon Hee in her corruption trial by January 2, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Former South Korean First Lady Kim Keon Hee was arrested and indicted in August 2025 on multiple charges, including bribery, stock-price manipulation, and election interference (https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/east-asia/south-korea-kim-keon-hee-arrest-b2713890.html). She was detained, and her trial began on September 24, 2025, at the Seoul Central District Court (https://www.koreaherald.com/). Under South Korean criminal procedure, a trial concludes with a final hearing where the prosecution summarizes its case and officially requests a specific sentence (a procedure known as 'guyhyeong'). Given the severity of the charges, which include violating the Capital Markets Act and the Political Funds Act, she faces potentially lengthy prison time, with reports indicating she could face sentences of 5 years or longer (https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/). 

A sentencing demand of 5 years or more by the prosecution would signal a strong case for significant prison time, increasing the likelihood of a guilty verdict and a prison sentence. Because a judge's verdict typically follows the prosecution's demand by two to four weeks, a final hearing held by early January 2026 is a crucial milestone for ensuring the actual sentencing occurs well before the ultimate March 31, 2026 deadline.

Sources:
- The Independent: South Korea's former first lady Kim Keon Hee arrested on corruption charges (https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/east-asia/south-korea-kim-keon-hee-arrest-b2713890.html)
- The Korea Herald: Kim Keon Hee trial begins (https://www.koreaherald.com/)
- Korea JoongAng Daily: Kim Keon Hee's Downfall (https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-12-03 and 2026-01-02 (inclusive in South Korea Standard Time), the South Korean prosecution formally requests (demands) a prison sentence of 5 years or more for Kim Keon Hee during a court hearing in her ongoing corruption trial. This official sentence recommendation is known as 'guyhyeong' in the South Korean legal system.

- If the prosecution requests a prison sentence of less than 5 years, the question resolves 'No'.
- If the final hearing and sentencing demand do not occur between 2025-12-03 and 2026-01-02, the question resolves 'No'.
- If the prosecution requests a sentence range, the minimum of that range must be 5 years or more to resolve 'Yes'.
- A demand of life imprisonment or the death penalty resolves 'Yes'.
- 'Corruption trial' refers to the trial that began on September 24, 2025, covering charges of stock manipulation, bribery, and election interference, or any subsequent consolidated trials encompassing these charges.
- Resolution will be based on official announcements from the South Korean prosecutors' office or the Seoul Central District Court, or a consensus of credible news reporting from reliable outlets such as Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr/), The Korea Herald (https://www.koreaherald.com/), or Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/).
subquestions.rationale: In South Korea, the prosecution's sentencing demand at the final hearing is a critical milestone in a criminal trial, typically occurring two to four weeks before the judge delivers the verdict and sentence. If the prosecution requests a severe penalty of 5 years or more by January 2, 2026, it strongly indicates that the trial is concluding swiftly and that the prosecution has built a robust case for significant prison time. This makes a guilty verdict and a prison sentence highly likely to happen well before the ultimate question's March 31, 2026 deadline. Conversely, a delayed final hearing or a lenient sentencing demand would lower the probability of her receiving a prison sentence by the target date.

question: Pepe ETF in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will a registration statement (e.g., Form S-1) for a spot Pepe ETF be filed with the SEC between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
In September 2025, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) adopted generic listing standards that significantly streamline the approval process for new spot cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs). By eliminating the need for individual 19b-4 filings for qualifying assets, the SEC shifted the requirement to merely filing an S-1 registration statement, reducing approval timelines from nine months to as little as 75 days. Several spot ETF proposals are currently pending for altcoins like Solana, XRP, and Dogecoin, but as of late September 2025, no asset manager has formally filed an S-1 for a spot Pepe ETF.

Because the ultimate question asks whether a spot Pepe ETF will be approved by December 31, 2025, the 75-day accelerated timeline implies that an S-1 filing would need to occur by mid-to-late October 2025 to have a realistic chance of approval before the end of the year. If no issuer files an S-1 by October 31, 2025, the prospect of an approval in 2025 becomes practically impossible, making this a pivotal early indicator.

Sources:
Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/
CoinDesk: https://www.coindesk.com/
SEC EDGAR: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if a Form S-1 (or equivalent initial registration statement, such as Form S-3 or Form F-1) for a spot Pepe ETF is filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and becomes publicly available on the SEC's EDGAR database (https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

To qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, the filed registration statement must explicitly state the intention to issue an exchange-traded product (ETP) or exchange-traded fund (ETF) that holds spot Pepe cryptocurrency (PEPE) as its sole or primary underlying asset. 

Filings for diversified crypto index funds where Pepe is only a partial component, or filings for funds primarily holding Pepe derivatives (e.g., futures contracts), will not trigger a 'Yes' resolution. If the SEC EDGAR database goes offline or becomes unavailable, credible reporting from at least three major financial news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, CoinDesk, Yahoo Finance) confirming the filing will be used as a fallback resolution source. If no such filing occurs and is made public between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: To secure SEC approval for a spot Pepe ETF by December 31, 2025, an issuer must first file an initial registration statement (like an S-1). Under the SEC's new generic listing standards, the approval timeline has been reduced to approximately 75 days. Consequently, an S-1 filing in October 2025 is a critical prerequisite for a 2025 approval. Resolving whether this filing happens by October 31 serves as a highly informative crux: a 'No' would almost certainly preclude a 2025 approval, while a 'Yes' would indicate active pursuit of the ETF within the required timeframe.

question: Will Michael Anton be next National Security Advisor?

Articles published prior to 2025-11-30 do not count. The reporting must occur and be published between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-25. If none of these three outlets report that he is under consideration or appointed by the end of the day on 2025-12-25 (11:59 PM ET), the question resolves "No".
subquestions.rationale: In the modern political landscape, major administration appointments are almost always preceded by leaks and shortlist reporting by top political news organizations. If Michael Anton is truly a leading candidate or among the top contenders for the permanent National Security Advisor role, it is highly probable that reporters at Politico, Axios, or The New York Times will uncover and publish this information before the end of the year. Conversely, if no such reporting emerges by December 25, 2025, it strongly implies that he is not in serious contention, providing a highly informative, early update for forecasters predicting whether he will be the ultimate appointee.

question: U.S. forces in Gaza in 2025?

subquestions.question: Will the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) adopt a resolution authorizing or establishing a multinational stabilization force for the Gaza Strip before November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 10, 2025, a ceasefire brokered by the Trump administration took effect in Gaza. To monitor the implementation of the agreement, the U.S. deployed roughly 200 military personnel to Israel to form a Civil-Military Coordination Center. Concurrently, discussions are actively underway to deploy an international stabilization force into Gaza. U.S. and European officials have advanced a UN Security Council draft resolution to establish this international stabilization force under Egyptian leadership, while Arab nations are pushing for a UN mandate to define the legal authority of the broader mission. Although the U.S. currently maintains that American troops will not physically enter Gaza, the establishment of an official UN-mandated force architecture—co-managed by U.S. coordination cells in Israel—would dramatically alter the military landscape. Monitoring whether the UNSC successfully passes such a resolution provides critical insight into how quickly the international military framework in Gaza will be established, which is a necessary precursor for any potential U.S. military entry (e.g., for oversight, emergency response, or engineering support) before the end of 2025.

ynetnews: https://www.ynetnews.com/
News18: https://www.news18.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

To resolve Yes, the adoption of the resolution must occur within the specified time window (between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30) and be officially documented on the UN Security Council's Resolutions page (https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/resolutions-0) or confirmed by an official UN press release (https://press.un.org/en/content/security-council).

The text of the adopted resolution must explicitly mention Gaza or the Gaza Strip and the establishment, authorization, or endorsement of a multinational or international military/stabilization force. It is not required that the United States directly contributes troops to this specific force under the resolution.

If a draft resolution is proposed but vetoed, or otherwise fails to be adopted by the UNSC within the resolution window, it will not count towards a Yes resolution. If no qualifying resolution is adopted by 11:59 PM UTC on November 30, 2025, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A UN Security Council resolution authorizing an international force in Gaza is a critical precursor to the deployment of foreign militaries into the territory. While current diplomatic plans exclude U.S. troops from entering Gaza directly, the formal establishment of a multinational force—especially one coordinated by the newly deployed U.S. military personnel in Israel—increases the likelihood of U.S. regular forces eventually crossing into Gaza for logistical, engineering, or emergency support. Conversely, if no such UN mandate is passed by the end of November, the stabilization effort may stall, severely reducing the conditions under which U.S. forces would enter Gaza by the end of 2025.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. government publish a formal proposal, Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, or Notice of Inquiry in the Federal Register regarding semiconductor tariffs or domestic-to-import chip ratios between October 24, 2025, and November 23, 2025?

General tariffs (e.g., across-the-board tariffs on all goods from a country) do not count; the notice must specifically highlight semiconductors or related integrated circuits. subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks if tariffs will be enacted by the end of 2025. Progress on establishing the Board is heavily dependent on the operationalization of the ISF, which relies on international troop and financial contributions. Since negotiations for these contributions have been ongoing since November 2025, an official, quantified commitment by a sovereign nation acts as a highly costly, observable signal that the administrative and logistical hurdles of the plan are being successfully navigated. Positive movement on the ISF strongly indicates that the Board of Peace itself is likely to be officially established by the ultimate March 2026 deadline.

subquestions.background_information:

In August 2025, reports indicated that the Department of Justice (DOJ) planned to send a partial release from an estimated 100,000 pages of Epstein files to the U.S. House Oversight Committee, a move that reportedly made the Trump administration nervous (https://www.alternet.org/). In September 2025, U.S. Democrats released a new batch of documents from Epstein's estate that included mentions of Elon Musk, adding to earlier releases and fueling further speculation regarding other high-profile associates (https://www.thestar.com/). Concurrently, former President Donald Trump faced renewed public scrutiny regarding his connections to Epstein. Trump repeatedly denied visiting Epstein's private island, Little Saint James, claiming he turned down the invitation, though flight logs verify he flew on Epstein's plane (https://people.com/). Because the potential discovery of new evidence largely hinges on forthcoming document releases, tracking whether the House Oversight Committee publicly releases further batches of these files—from the massive 100,000-page repository—is a strong early indicator of whether new, definitive evidence about Trump's whereabouts will emerge before the end of 2025.

Sources:
Alternet: https://www.alternet.org/
The Star: https://www.thestar.com/
PEOPLE: https://people.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Accountability (or any of its official subcommittees) officially and publicly releases at least 50 pages of previously unreleased documents related to Jeffrey Epstein between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive).

To qualify, the release must be made publicly available via the Committee's official website (https://oversight.house.gov/), linked directly through an official Committee press release, or officially entered into the public congressional record by the Committee during the specified time window. 

Documents leaked to the press but not officially published or acknowledged by the Committee do not count toward the threshold. The 50-page requirement can be met by a single document release or a cumulative total of multiple official releases during the resolution window. If no such release occurs, or the total number of pages officially released is fewer than 50 between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, this question resolves "No".
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether definitive evidence of Trump visiting Epstein's island will be made public by the end of 2025. Given that the DOJ is in the process of transmitting up to 100,000 pages of Epstein-related documents to the House Oversight Committee, the committee is the most likely conduit for new evidence. If the committee actively releases a substantive batch of documents (50+ pages) in November, it signals an ongoing pipeline of transparency that increases the probability of Trump-related evidence emerging. Conversely, a lack of releases suggests stalled momentum, reducing the likelihood of a 'Yes' on the ultimate question.

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the December meeting by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the median projection for the federal funds rate at the end of 2025 be 4.1% in the FOMC's September 2025 Summary of Economic Projections?
subquestions.background_information:
As of July 2025, the target range for the federal funds rate is 4.25% to 4.50%, with a midpoint of 4.375% (typically represented as 4.4% in Federal Reserve projection tables). The ultimate question asks whether the Fed will execute a "cut-pause-pause" sequence across its final three meetings of 2025 (September, October, and December). At the September 16-17, 2025 meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will release its Summary of Economic Projections (SEP), which includes the "dot plot" detailing policymakers' expectations for the federal funds rate at year-end.

If the Fed expects to execute exactly one 25-basis-point cut for the remainder of 2025 (matching the "cut-pause-pause" sequence), the projected end-of-2025 target range would be 4.00% to 4.25%. The midpoint of this range is 4.125%, which is conventionally rounded and displayed as 4.1% in the SEP tables. Therefore, a median projection of 4.1% for 2025 in the September SEP is a direct, observable leading indicator that the FOMC plans exactly one more cut for the year, perfectly aligning with the ultimate question's required trajectory.

Sources:
1. Federal Reserve Open Market Operations: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm
2. FOMC Calendars & Statements: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the "Summary of Economic Projections" (SEP) released by the FOMC shows a "Median" value of exactly 4.1% (or exactly 4.125% if unrounded) for the "Federal funds rate" for the year 2025 in Table 1 (or the equivalent main projections table) between 2025-09-05 and 2025-10-05 inclusive.

This question resolves No if the median projection for 2025 is any other value (e.g., 3.9%, 4.4%), or if no SEP is published within the resolution window.

The official resolution source is the Projection Materials PDF provided for the September 16-17, 2025 FOMC meeting on the Federal Reserve website: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

To resolve, resolvers should navigate to the specific FOMC meeting on the calendar, open the "Projection Materials" PDF, locate "Table 1. Economic projections of Federal Reserve Board members and Federal Reserve Bank presidents" (or equivalent table), and find the intersection of the "Federal funds rate" row and the "2025" column under the "Median" heading. If the publication format changes but an equivalent median projection for the year-end 2025 federal funds rate is released in official Fed materials within the timeframe, that figure will be used.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question depends on the Fed delivering exactly one rate cut over the final three meetings of 2025 (cutting in September, then pausing in October and December). The September SEP 'dot plot' directly reveals the committee's median expectation for the end-of-year rate. A median of 4.1% explicitly signals a consensus for exactly one 25 bps cut from the current 4.25-4.50% range. If the Fed cuts in September and concurrently projects a 4.1% year-end rate, it essentially confirms their intention to pause at the subsequent two meetings, making this projection a highly informative crux for forecasters.

question: Will Russia capture Myrnohrad by September 30?

Once Russia captures the intersection, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

subquestions.question: Will Russia capture the entirety of the settlement of Novoekonomichne by September 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Russian forces have been advancing towards the city of Myrnohrad in the Donetsk Oblast. During late August 2025, Russian units expanded their area of control east of Myrnohrad. Reports indicated heavy fighting in and around nearby settlements, including Novoekonomichne. Ukrainian units were reportedly attempting to hold the southern part of Novoekonomichne while retreating westward under drone and artillery fire. Because Novoekonomichne sits strategically on the eastern approach to Myrnohrad, its complete capture by Russian forces would serve as a key leading indicator of Russian momentum. If Russian forces cannot fully clear Novoekonomichne, their chances of advancing deep enough into Myrnohrad to capture the target intersection by September 30 are significantly reduced.

Sources:

ISW Interactive Map: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the settlement of Novoekonomichne, Donetsk Oblast, is assessed as fully captured or fully under Russian control by the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) or DeepStateMap between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-25 11:59 PM ET.

Specifically, the question resolves Yes if, at any point during the resolution window (between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-25 inclusive), either of the following conditions is met:
1. DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) updates its map to show the entire territorial limits of the Novoekonomichne settlement as under Russian control (marked as occupied).
