subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve announce a reduction in the target range for the federal funds rate at or before the conclusion of its October 2025 FOMC meeting?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question resolves to "No" if any of four conditions are met, one of which is that the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates twice between September 23, 2025, and December 31, 2025. The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) has a scheduled policy meeting on October 28-29, 2025. Because there is only one other scheduled meeting in 2025 (in December), a rate cut at the October meeting is a critical stepping stone for the "Fed cuts twice" condition to be fulfilled. If the Fed does not cut rates in October, fulfilling the condition would require an emergency inter-meeting cut or multiple cuts at a single meeting in December. Market expectations leading up to the meeting point to a 0.25-percentage-point cut in the fed funds rate, though recent data and potential disruptions such as a government shutdown add uncertainty to the Fed's decision-making process.

Sources:
Investopedia: Next Fed Meeting: When It Is In October And What To Expect - https://www.investopedia.com/
Federal Reserve FOMC Calendar - https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announces a reduction in the target range for the federal funds rate between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-05 (inclusive).

The primary source for resolution will be the official press releases issued by the Federal Reserve, available on their official website (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm and https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm). 

If the stated target range (or single target rate, in the event the Fed modifies its targeting framework) for the federal funds rate announced at the conclusion of the October 2025 FOMC meeting (or an emergency announcement prior to the end date) is lower than the target range in effect immediately prior to 2025-10-27, the question resolves Yes.

If the FOMC announces no change, an increase, or does not issue any decision to lower the target range between 2025-10-27 and 2025-11-05, the question resolves No. If the scheduled October meeting is delayed beyond the end date of 2025-11-05 without any rate cut announcement occurring within the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A rate cut at the October 2025 FOMC meeting serves as an important crux for the ultimate question. Since the ultimate question looks for two rate cuts between September 23 and December 31, an October rate cut is practically necessary for this condition to be met. Establishing whether this first cut happens provides strong early evidence of whether the 'Nothing Ever Happens' outcome will be invalidated by the Fed's monetary policy path.

question: Will there be at least 500 measles cases in the U.S. in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there have been the specified amount or more confirmed cases of Measles (Rubeola) in humans in the territory of the United States of America in 2026 according to the CDC case counter between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. subquestions.question: Will the CDC report a cumulative total of 50 or more distinct measles outbreaks in the U.S. for the year 2025 by January 1, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The United States is currently experiencing its worst measles year in decades, with over 1,700 confirmed cases reported by November 2025. While the overall number of cases is an important metric, the geographic dispersion and number of distinct transmission chains are crucial indicators of the virus's momentum. The CDC reported 45 distinct measles outbreaks as of November 13, 2025, which is a massive increase compared to the 16 outbreaks recorded in all of 2024. The CDC typically defines a measles outbreak as a cluster of 3 or more related cases. 

A continuously rising number of outbreaks indicates that the virus is establishing new transmission chains in different communities rather than remaining confined to localized events (such as the massive Texas outbreak earlier in 2025). Tracking whether the U.S. reaches 50 or more outbreaks before the end of 2025 serves as an early indicator of how widely dispersed the virus will be heading into 2026. This metric is especially relevant given declining national MMR vaccination rates (currently around 92.5%, below the 95% herd immunity threshold) and warnings from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) regarding the potential loss of the U.S. measles elimination status in early 2026.

Sources:
CDC Measles Data - https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html
The Boston Globe - https://www.bostonglobe.com
SheKnows - https://www.sheknows.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports a cumulative total of 50 or more measles outbreaks in the United States for the year 2025, in any official data update or press release published between 2025-12-02 and 2026-01-01 (inclusive). 

The primary resolution source will be the official CDC Measles (Rubeola) Data and Statistics page (https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html). Official CDC press releases, health advisories, or Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Reports (MMWR) published within the resolution window will also qualify. 

If the CDC ceases to publish or update the national count of outbreaks during this window due to budget cuts or other disruptions, the question will resolve No unless the threshold of 50 was explicitly met and published by the CDC prior to the stoppage but within the resolution window. An 'outbreak' is defined by the CDC parameters (typically 3 or more related cases); however, for resolution, whatever number of distinct outbreaks the CDC officially states as the cumulative total for 2025 will be taken as authoritative regardless of their internal classification changes. Delayed reports published after 2026-01-01 will not be considered.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. will see 500+ cases in 2026. The number of active or total outbreaks at the end of 2025 is a powerful leading indicator for 2026 case volume. More distinct outbreaks mean the virus is geographically dispersed and actively circulating in multiple independent communities. If the U.S. crosses the 50-outbreak threshold by the end of December 2025, it signals that public health interventions are failing to contain geographic spread, strongly predicting multiple uncontained seed points heading into 2026.

question: Next BLS jobs report during government shutdown?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down following the shutdown that began on October 1, 2025. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

Partial shutdowns are considered shutdowns, whereas announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as shutdowns.

Both a full release of the monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate) and an official release of the underlying data by the Bureau of Labor Statistics will count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the Bureau of Labor Statistics cancels the release or is otherwise rendered incapable of releasing it by that time, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the Bureau of Labor Statistics official release as well as the OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/); however, a consensus of credible sources will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announce that the U.S. federal government is no longer shut down between October 8, 2025 and November 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. federal government entered a shutdown on October 1, 2025. Due to the lapse in appropriations, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) suspended normal operations, meaning critical economic data like the September jobs report—originally scheduled for October 3, 2025—was delayed. The ultimate question asks whether the BLS will release the Employment Situation report before the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces that the government is no longer shut down. Given that the BLS is closed during the shutdown, if the shutdown ends and the OPM announces it, the BLS will likely reopen and release the report shortly after, resulting in a 'No' for the ultimate question. However, if the shutdown drags on significantly, there may be increasing pressure from financial markets and policymakers to grant the BLS a special exemption or targeted funding to release the data during the shutdown. This subquestion asks whether the shutdown will end, as announced by the OPM, by November 1, 2025.

Sources:
OPM Current Status: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/
OPM News Releases: https://www.opm.gov/news/releases/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) officially announces that the federal government is no longer shut down, or that normal operations have resumed following the lapse in appropriations, between 2025-10-08 and 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z. The primary resolution source will be the OPM's Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/) and official OPM press releases (https://www.opm.gov/news/releases/). A change in the operating status indicating that the government is 'Open' and that the shutdown has ended will suffice. If no such announcement is made by 2025-11-01T00:00:00Z, this question resolves 'No'. Announcements of office closures due to holidays, weather, or isolated incidents do not count as the end of the shutdown. If the event is postponed or delayed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: If the government shutdown ends by November 1, 2025, the BLS will reopen and release the jobs report after the OPM's announcement. This timeline would naturally trigger a 'No' resolution for the ultimate question. Conversely, if the shutdown continues into November, the likelihood of an emergency data release of the jobs report during the shutdown (a 'Yes' resolution for the ultimate question) increases significantly due to the prolonged absence of critical economic data and mounting pressure from the Federal Reserve and markets.

question: Will Italy win the second most medals in the 2026 Winter Olympics?
description:

In the case of ties, the ordered list for most medals won will use most gold medals won as a tiebreaker (e.g. If Norway and China tie for most medals won, and Norway wins more gold medals than China, Norway will be ranked first and China will be second). If this also results in a tie, the country whose name comes first in alphabetical order, as listed in this market group, will be ranked higher.

This market will resolve based on the medal figures as they stand after medals are awarded for the final event in the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics. Later changes to medal counts will not be considered toward the resolution of this market.

If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are partially completed and then cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve based on the medals awarded in the completed events. If the 2026 Milano-Cortina Winter Olympics are entirely cancelled or postponed after December 31, 2026, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The resolution source will be official information from the International Olympic Committee (https://www.olympics.com/).

subquestions.question: Will Italy win at least 12 medals at the 2026 Winter Olympics between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-16?
subquestions.background_information:

To finish with the second most medals overall at the 2026 games, Italy would likely need to surpass powerhouses like the United States and Germany, both of which are traditionally projected to win upwards of 25-30 medals. According to recent prediction markets and analyses, Norway is the favorite to win the most total and gold medals, with the USA and Germany also serving as strong contenders. For Italy to secure the second most medals overall, a highly productive performance in the middle days of the Games is crucial. Winning at least 12 medals over this 9-day stretch (February 8 to February 16) would pace Italy to a total medal count in the high 20s or low 30s, acting as a strong indicator of whether they are on track for a top-two finish in the total medal count.

Sources:
Milano Cortina 2026 Official Site: https://milanocortina2026.olympics.com/en/
International Olympic Committee: https://olympics.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Italy is officially awarded 12 or more total medals (gold, silver, or bronze combined) in the 2026 Winter Olympics between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-16.

To determine resolution, the official International Olympic Committee (IOC) medal records (https://olympics.com/en/olympic-games/milano-cortina-2026/medals) will be used. The count will include all medals won by Italy in events that conclude between 2026-02-08 at 00:00 UTC and 2026-02-16 at 23:59 UTC, inclusive.

Any subsequent disqualifications, medal strippings, or reallocations announced after 2026-02-16 will not be taken into account for the resolution of this market. If the Olympics are postponed, paused, or cancelled, and fewer than 12 medals are awarded to Italy strictly within this time window, the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: To achieve the second most medals overall, a nation typically needs 25-30 medals. Italy's baseline from 2022 is 17 medals. Tracking their medal haul over an 9-day mid-Games window (February 8 to February 16) provides a high-value early indicator of their overall trajectory. If they win 12 or more medals in this span, they are significantly outperforming their 2022 pace and demonstrating the host-nation bump required to challenge the US and Germany for second place.

question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch Tool indicate a probability of 50.0% or higher for a December 2025 rate pause (375-400 bps) as of December 5, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
At the October 2025 FOMC meeting, the Federal Reserve lowered the federal funds target rate to a range of 3.75%-4.00% (or 375-400 bps). The decision revealed growing internal divisions, with the 10-2 vote featuring one dissent for a 50 bps cut and another for a pause. Chair Jerome Powell subsequently emphasized that a December cut is "far from it" (not a foregone conclusion) and acknowledged a "growing chorus" supporting a pause. Additionally, a U.S. government shutdown has hindered the release of key economic data, complicating the Fed's outlook (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/powells-december-warning-exposes-hardening-divisions-at-fed-20251030/). For the ultimate question's "Pause-Pause-Pause" scenario to resolve 'Yes', the Fed must first choose to pause at its December 9-10, 2025 meeting. The CME FedWatch Tool is widely used to gauge market expectations of FOMC policy changes by calculating probabilities based on 30-Day Fed Funds futures pricing data. If market sentiment solidifies around a pause ahead of the December meeting, it serves as a highly informative crux for the ultimate outcome.

Sources:
CME FedWatch Tool: https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html
Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/powells-december-warning-exposes-hardening-divisions-at-fed-20251030/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the CME FedWatch Tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html) reports a probability of 50.0% or strictly greater for the Federal Funds Target Range to be 375-400 bps for the December 10, 2025 meeting, as of 5:00 PM ET on December 5, 2025. The condition must be satisfied within the resolution window that begins on the start_date of 2025-11-05 and ends on the end_date of 2025-12-05 (inclusive). The resolver must check the "Probabilities" tab for the "10 Dec 2025" meeting date on the CME FedWatch Tool at or shortly after 5:00 PM ET on December 5, 2025. If the probability shown in the 375-400 bps column is 50.0% or higher, the question resolves Yes. If the probability is strictly less than 50.0%, it resolves No. In the event that the CME FedWatch Tool is permanently unavailable on December 5, the question will resolve based on the last available daily settlement probability published by the CME Group for the 375-400 bps range between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05.
subquestions.rationale: For the Fed to execute a 'Pause-Pause-Pause' sequence over its next three decisions, a pause in December is the mandatory first step. Tracking the CME FedWatch Tool probability leading up to the December meeting captures the culmination of all macroeconomic data (and lack thereof due to the shutdown) and Fed official remarks. If the market assigns a >50% probability to a pause just days before the December meeting, forecasters can significantly update their models toward a 'Yes' on the first leg of the ultimate question.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

question: Will Trump act to ban mail-in voting or voting machines in 2025?
description:
On August 18, 2025, President Donald J. Trump announced his commitment to eliminate mail-in voting and voting machines in U.S. elections, ahead of the 2026 midterms.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that inhibits mail-in voting or voting machines from use for the 2026 midterm election by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any executive action or legislation that restricts, limits, or prohibits the use of mail-in voting or voting machines in any way will qualify, even if the action is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Trump administration officially establish a new federal commission, task force, or advisory board focused on "election integrity," mail-in voting, or voting machines between November 30, 2025, and December 29, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In August 2025, President Donald Trump repeatedly announced his intent to sign an executive order to ban mail-in voting and voting machines before the 2026 midterms, claiming the order was 'being written right now by the best lawyers in the country.' However, legal experts and election administrators note that Article I, Section 4 of the U.S. Constitution grants states the authority to administer elections, meaning a direct federal ban by the president would face severe legal hurdles. Earlier in April 2025, a federal judge blocked a similar Trump executive order requiring proof of citizenship for federal elections, citing that election regulation is a state and congressional power. 

Given these constitutional constraints, an outright ban via executive order may be legally unworkable in the short term. The administration might instead opt to establish a federal commission, task force, or advisory board to investigate mail-in voting and voting machines as a precursor to future action—similar to the Presidential Advisory Commission on Election Integrity established during Trump's first term in 2017. Tracking whether such a commission is established provides a strong indicator of the administration's approach: forming a study commission suggests a delay in immediate restrictive actions, whereas skipping this step might indicate an imminent, direct executive order is still planned for 2025.

Sources:
Al Jazeera Online: 'Trump to order voter ID for every vote, no exceptions' - https://www.aljazeera.com
KOMO: 'Election officials speak out as Trump pushes to eliminate mail-in voting' - https://komonews.com
USA Today: 'Trump says he will issue executive order mandating voter ID requirement' - https://www.usatoday.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), the White House, the Department of Justice (DOJ), or another U.S. federal agency officially establishes a new commission, task force, advisory board, or specialized unit whose stated mandate includes investigating, reviewing, or reforming 'election integrity,' mail-in voting, or electronic voting machines.

- 'Officially establishes' means the action is formalized via a signed executive order, presidential memorandum, or official agency directive. 
- The action must be published or officially announced on an authoritative U.S. government website, such as the White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov), the DOJ website (https://www.justice.gov), or the Federal Register (https://www.federalregister.gov).
- Mere verbal promises or statements of intent during speeches or interviews without an accompanying signed directive or official press release announcing the formal creation of the body do not qualify.
- The mandate of the body must explicitly relate to election administration, voter fraud, mail-in ballots, or voting machines.
- If an executive order is signed that directly restricts or bans mail-in voting/voting machines AND ALSO creates a task force within the same document, this question resolves Yes. If it solely restricts/bans without creating such a body, it resolves No.
- Any action taken before 2025-11-30 or after 2025-12-29 will not count toward a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: A direct federal ban on mail-in voting via executive order is legally complex and likely to face immediate injunctions, as states possess constitutional authority over election administration. If the Trump administration recognizes an immediate ban is unfeasible by the end of 2025, they may pivot to establishing a federal commission or task force to 'investigate' mail-in voting and voting machines as an interim step. If such a commission is formed in December, it indicates a longer-term strategy, reducing the likelihood that Trump will issue a direct, inhibiting executive action before December 31, 2025. Conversely, the absence of a commission may indicate that the administration intends to proceed directly with a blunt executive order to fulfill Trump's August 2025 promises before the end of the year.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q3 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's GDPNow model estimate for Q3 2025 real GDP growth be 2.5% or higher in its final update of September 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's GDPNow model provides a running, real-time estimate of real gross domestic product (GDP) growth based on the latest available economic data for the current measured quarter. As the ultimate question asks whether Q3 2025 GDP will land exactly between 2.0% and 2.5%, tracking the GDPNow estimate at the end of September (the close of the third quarter) is highly informative. According to recent news reports, the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) revised Q2 2025 GDP growth up to 3.3%, up from the advance estimate of 3.0%. This growth was driven largely by strong AI-related investments and a sharp drop in imports ahead of tariff hikes. However, economists caution that tariff-induced drags could slow future growth down closer to 1.5%. By late September, the GDPNow model will have incorporated roughly two months of Q3 data, including July and August figures for retail sales, industrial production, and trade balances. A GDPNow reading of 2.5% or higher at the end of September would indicate that the economy maintained strong momentum through Q3, making a final BEA print inside the narrow 2.0-2.5% range less likely by suggesting a potential overshoot.

Sources:
Atlanta Fed GDPNow: https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow
BEA GDP Data: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta's GDPNow model estimate for Q3 2025 real seasonally adjusted annual rate GDP growth is 2.5% or higher, according to the final update published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive). 

Resolution will be based on the official 'Latest estimate' figure posted on the Atlanta Fed GDPNow website (https://www.atlantafed.org/cqer/research/gdpnow). The resolver will check the headline number provided in the final model update released on or before 2025-09-30. If the value is 2.5% or greater (e.g., 2.5%, 2.6%), the question resolves Yes. If the value is 2.4% or lower, it resolves No. 

If the GDPNow model is discontinued or no updates are published between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question will resolve based on the last available estimate published prior to 2025-10-01. Any updates or revisions made to the GDPNow model on or after 2025-10-01 will not be considered for the resolution of this subquestion.
subquestions.rationale: The Atlanta Fed GDPNow is a premier real-time tracking model for US GDP. Its final update in September will incorporate the majority of the quarter's actual data. If this estimate is 2.5% or above, it acts as a strong crux indicating Q3 momentum is too hot to safely land in the 2.0% - 2.5% target bracket, heavily updating forecasts for the ultimate BEA release in October.

question: Will US GDP growth in 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted real GDP growth rate for the United States in 2025, as reported in the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) "Advance Estimate" release for Q4 of 2025, scheduled for January 29, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: The relevant data will be the full-year real GDP growth rate as stated in the advance estimate, typically expressed as the percentage change from the annual level in 2024 to the annual level in 2025. Any revisions to this figure made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the final estimate of U.S. real GDP growth for the third quarter of 2025 be 4.2% or lower?
subquestions.background_information:
According to recent reports, the U.S. economy grew at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter of 2025 based on the initial estimate from the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) (https://www.hindustantimes.com/). This followed a 3.8% growth rate in Q2 and a contraction in Q1, resulting in a 2.5% annualized growth rate for the first three quarters of 2025 combined (https://www.foxbusiness.com/). Due to a government shutdown, the BEA delayed its releases and the final estimate for Q3 2025 is scheduled for release on January 22, 2026 (https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product). For the full-year 2025 GDP growth to land between 2.0% and 2.5%, the Q4 figure will need to be relatively low, or prior quarters will need to see downward revisions. Therefore, a downward revision to the Q3 GDP growth estimate (to 4.2% or lower) would mathematically increase the likelihood that the full-year 2025 GDP growth remains within the 2.0%-2.5% range.

Sources:
BEA GDP Data: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
Hindustan Times: https://www.hindustantimes.com/
Fox Business: https://www.foxbusiness.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reports a final estimate of real Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth for the third quarter (Q3) of 2025 that is 4.2% or lower (e.g., 4.2%, 4.1%, etc.). The resolution window for this question is between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-29 (inclusive).

The value used for resolution will be the "seasonally adjusted at annual rates" percent change from the preceding quarter for Real Gross Domestic Product, specifically for Q3 2025, as published in the BEA's final GDP release for that quarter (scheduled for January 22, 2026). The official release will be accessed at the BEA's website: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product.

If the reported value is 4.3% or higher, the question resolves No. If the final estimate for Q3 2025 is not published by the BEA on or before January 29, 2026, the question resolves as unresolvable. Any subsequent revisions to the Q3 2025 GDP data made after January 29, 2026, will not be considered for resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The full-year 2025 GDP growth outcome depends on the growth rates of all four quarters. Currently, the first three quarters suggest a running average of 2.5%. For the ultimate question (full-year GDP between 2.0% and 2.5%) to resolve Yes, the average must not exceed 2.5%. A downward revision of the Q3 GDP growth from its initial estimate of 4.3% to 4.2% or lower would reduce the running average, giving more room for Q4 growth before exceeding the 2.5% upper bound, making a full-year result of 2.0% to 2.5% more likely. It is therefore a strong early indicator.

question: Will Tulsi Gabbard be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
description:

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem announce her departure or be removed from her Cabinet position before February 1, 2026?

If no such announcement occurs between 2026-01-05 and 2026-02-01, the question resolves 'No'. subquestions.rationale: Kristi Noem is currently considered one of the most likely Trump Cabinet members to be ousted first, given multiple reports of her precarious standing in late 2025. If Noem leaves the Cabinet before Tulsi Gabbard, Gabbard cannot be the first to leave, which would essentially resolve the ultimate question to 'No'.

question: Will the US capture Khamenei before 2027?

subquestions.question: Will the US government publicly confirm conducting kinetic military strikes on Iranian sovereign territory between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-25?
subquestions.background_information: Since late December 2025, Iran has been engulfed in massive anti-government protests, leading to thousands of deaths and a severe regime crackdown. 'Kinetic military strikes' includes the use of explosive munitions, missiles, drone strikes, or direct ground fire. Cyberattacks, electronic warfare, or psychological operations do not count. The strikes must be officially acknowledged by the US government on the record (e.g., via a press release on https://www.defense.gov/News/Press-Releases/ or an official statement on https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/). Anonymous leaks or unconfirmed reports do not qualify. Strikes on Iranian proxies (e.g., in Iraq, Syria, or Yemen) or on Iranian naval vessels in international waters do not count. The target must be within Iran's terrestrial borders or its territorial waters. If the US government announces a strike that occurred within the date range, but the announcement is delayed until after February 25, the question will still resolve 'Yes' so long as the actual strike occurred between 2026-02-08 and 2026-02-25 and is confirmed by the resolution date.
subquestions.rationale: An operation to capture the Supreme Leader of Iran on Iranian soil would represent an unprecedented escalation and would almost certainly be accompanied or preceded by broader US military action against Iran's air defenses, IRGC bases, and military infrastructure. If the US initiates direct kinetic strikes on Iranian territory in February 2026, it signals a collapse of de-escalation efforts by Gulf allies and a willingness by the US administration to execute extreme military options. If no strikes occur, it suggests diplomacy or deterrence is holding, drastically lowering the probability of an eventual capture raid.

subquestions.question: Will Israeli military aircraft or drones conduct at least one kinetic strike within Syria's Suwayda Governorate between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since the fall of the Bashar al-Assad regime in December 2023, Israel has escalated military operations in southern Syria. Following severe sectarian clashes in July 2025 between Druze militias and Bedouin tribes in the Suwayda Governorate, Israel launched airstrikes targeting Syrian government forces in the region and positioned itself as a protector of the Druze minority (https://reliefweb.int/report/syrian-arab-republic/expert-comment-israels-campaign-syria-enters-new-phase-amid-al-suwayda-escalation). Throughout August and September 2025, Israeli ground troops made progressive incursions into the Quneitra and Daraa provinces, conducting surveys and raiding civilian homes (https://english.enabbaladi.net/archives/2025/09/quneitra-israel-conducts-survey-in-sida-golan). Reports in late September indicate that security negotiations between the Syrian transitional government and Israel have stalled due to Israel's demand to establish a 'humanitarian corridor' directly to Suwayda. Given that Israeli ground forces have not yet reached Suwayda, continued or renewed Israeli airstrikes in the governorate would serve as a strong indicator that Israel is maintaining an active military campaign in Suwayda, potentially shaping the environment for a future ground incursion.

The strike must occur strictly within this timeframe. If a strike occurs within the window but is reported shortly after, it still counts toward a 'Yes' resolution. Airstrikes strictly outside Suwayda (e.g., in neighboring Daraa or Quneitra governorates) do not count. Non-kinetic operations (such as reconnaissance flights, sonic booms, dropping leaflets, or airdropping supplies) will not trigger a 'Yes' resolution.

If no qualifying strike is reported to have occurred between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 by November 7, 2025 (accounting for a 7-day reporting grace period), the question resolves to 'No'. In the event of conflicting reports about the origin or location of the strike, consensus from at least two major international news organizations or explicit confirmation by the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR, https://www.syriahr.com/en/) will be required to resolve the question as 'Yes'.

Kinetic airstrikes in Suwayda would indicate that Israel is actively engaged in shaping the security environment in the province, either to support allied Druze factions, target hostile forces, or prepare for a ground corridor. question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.question: Will the initial seasonally adjusted US unemployment rate for September 2025 be reported at 4.4% or higher?
subquestions.background_information:
In September 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) lowered its benchmark federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 4.00% to 4.25%, marking the first rate cut of the year. The decision was driven largely by concerns over a cooling labor market, with the August 2025 unemployment rate having reached 4.3%—the highest level since October 2021. Fed Chair Jerome Powell described the move as a 'risk management cut' aimed at preventing further softening in employment. The FOMC's updated Summary of Economic Projections (SEP) suggested two more rate cuts could happen by the end of 2025.

Forecasting whether the Fed will follow a specific sequence of 'Cut-Pause-Pause' for the upcoming October, December, and January meetings depends heavily on labor market trajectory. If the unemployment rate continues to rise to 4.4% or higher in September, the Fed may be compelled to cut rates at both the October and December meetings, which would invalidate the 'Cut-Pause-Pause' sequence. Conversely, if the unemployment rate stabilizes or drops, the Fed might cut in October and pause in December and January as they observe the effects of previous cuts.

Sources:
BLS Employment Situation Summary: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
CNBC - Fed approves quarter-point interest rate cut and sees two more coming this year: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/17/fed-approves-quarter-point-interest-rate-cut.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports an initial seasonally adjusted national unemployment rate (U-3) of 4.4% or higher for September 2025. The qualifying event must occur between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The resolution will be based strictly on the headline "Unemployment rate" figure for September 2025 in the "Employment Situation" news release published by the BLS in October 2025 (typically on the first Friday of the month). The official data source for resolution is the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm or the accompanying Table A-1 at https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.t01.htm).

The headline rate reported to one decimal place will be used. If the reported figure is 4.4% or greater (e.g., 4.4%, 4.5%), the question resolves Yes. If the figure is 4.3% or lower (e.g., 4.3%, 4.2%), the question resolves No.

Only the initial release of the September 2025 data will be used; subsequent revisions to the data in later months will not affect the resolution. If the September 2025 Employment Situation report is delayed and not published by the BLS between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, this question will resolve as No.
subquestions.rationale: The Federal Reserve's recent rate cuts are highly sensitive to labor market weakness. For the Fed to execute a 'Cut-Pause-Pause' sequence, the labor market likely needs to stabilize so they feel comfortable pausing after a cut. A higher unemployment rate (4.4%+) would increase pressure for consecutive cuts in both October and December, serving as a strong early indicator that the 'Cut-Pause-Pause' sequence will fail.

If job growth remains sluggish (under 100,000), economic anxiety is highly likely to drag his overall approval down below 44.0%, signaling a probable 'No' on the ultimate question. subquestions.question: Will the BLS report the unadjusted civilian noninstitutional population of women aged 16 to 44 years to be 64.0 million or greater for August 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The ultimate question asks whether the U.S. general fertility rate (births per 1,000 women aged 15-44) will rise above 54.5 in Q2 2025. According to CDC data for 2024, the general fertility rate fell to an all-time low even though the absolute number of births actually increased by 1%. Experts note that this discrepancy is driven by high immigration and adjustments to U.S. Census population estimates, which significantly increased the total population of women of childbearing age (the denominator in the fertility rate calculation). Therefore, the size of this demographic group is a critical crux. If the population of women of childbearing age continues to grow rapidly, it applies strong downward pressure on the fertility rate, making a rate increase mathematically less likely. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) tracks a closely related demographic, the civilian noninstitutional population of women aged 16 to 44 (Series ID: LNU00000026). The August 2025 estimate for this group will be released on September 5, 2025, in the monthly Employment Situation report. Sources: Newsweek (https://www.newsweek.com/us-birth-rate-plunges-new-low-cdc-1930000), FRED LNU00000026 Series (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LNU00000026), BLS Schedule (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the unadjusted civilian noninstitutional population of women aged 16 to 44 years in the United States (Series ID: LNU00000026) is reported to be 64,000,000 (or 64,000 in thousands) or greater for August 2025. The qualifying publication must occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-16 (inclusive). Resolution will be based on the first published estimate for August 2025 released by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) or the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) during this window. The official data can be found at FRED: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/LNU00000026 or the BLS data portal: https://data.bls.gov/timeseries/LNU00000026. If the data for August 2025 is not published by either source between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-16, this question will resolve as No. Revisions made after the initial release during this window will not be considered.
subquestions.rationale: The general fertility rate is calculated as total births divided by the population of women of childbearing age. Demographic analyses for 2024 revealed that the U.S. saw an absolute increase in births, but the fertility rate still fell because the population of women in this age bracket grew even faster, largely due to immigration. Therefore, the size of this female cohort acts as a crucial denominator. If the BLS reports that the population of women aged 16-44 continues to swell, exceeding 64 million, it will be mathematically much harder for the Q2 2025 general fertility rate to increase, since the denominator would be applying strong downward pressure. This provides a highly informative, early indicator before the actual Q2 2025 CDC birth rate data is finalized.

If the original model is removed, it strongly implies the AirTag 2 is a direct replacement that will inherit the $29 price point. question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) publish the September 2025 Employment Situation report between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?

Whether the BLS manages to release this critical September report by the end of October serves as a highly informative early indicator of the severity of the agency's operational crisis.

Sources:
- BLS Release Schedule: https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm
- BLS Employment Situation News Releases: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm

The official source for resolving this question is the Bureau of Labor Statistics website, specifically the Employment Situation releases page (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.toc.htm) or the BLS release calendar (https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm).

To qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, the publication must be the primary, full national employment report containing September 2025 nonfarm payrolls and the national unemployment rate. Publishing only preliminary data, partial estimates, or notices of delay does not qualify.

If the BLS website is offline due to a government shutdown, but the official September 2025 Employment Situation data is distributed by the BLS, the Department of Labor (https://www.dol.gov), or the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov) via alternative official channels within the resolution window, it will count as a 'Yes'.

If the September 2025 Employment Situation report is not published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 at 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks if the BLS will permanently cease regular publication of major reports, stipulating that missing three consecutive scheduled releases by more than 30 days counts as cessation. The September jobs report is scheduled for October 3, 2025. A failure to publish this report by October 31 (a 28-day delay) would be a severe early indicator of systemic dysfunction, an extended government shutdown, or drastic workforce cuts. A 'No' resolution on this subquestion strongly updates the probability of a 'Yes' on the ultimate question, as the agency would be on the brink of triggering the 30-day delay threshold for the first of three consecutive reports. Conversely, a 'Yes' resolution demonstrates agency resilience and its ability to resume operations, supporting a 'No' on the ultimate question.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of Brazil, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the President of the Brazilian Federal Senate officially accept and read an impeachment request against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes in the plenary by September 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes has faced intense criticism and numerous impeachment requests from right-wing lawmakers, citing his actions during investigations into former President Jair Bolsonaro and decisions regarding social media [1, 2]. Recently, the U.S. government imposed sanctions on Moraes, further fueling the push for his removal [3]. Despite over 30 impeachment requests having been filed, the President of the Federal Senate has previously declined to advance them [1, 2]. However, mass protests are planned for September 7, 2025, to explicitly demand his impeachment, which could increase political pressure on the Senate leadership [2]. In Brazil, the impeachment of a Supreme Court Minister begins in the Federal Senate. The President of the Senate has the sole authority to accept an impeachment petition. Once accepted, it is formally read in the plenary, which initiates the process before it goes to a special committee. Tracking whether the Senate President accepts and reads a petition is a direct and necessary precursor to any floor vote on proceeding with an impeachment.

Sources:
[1] Breitbart: https://www.breitbart.com/
[2] NZ Herald: https://www.nzherald.co.nz/
[3] Sahara Reporters: https://saharareporters.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the President of the Brazilian Federal Senate (or an acting President) officially accepts and formally reads (or orders the reading of) an impeachment request against Supreme Federal Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes in the Senate plenary between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive).

The reading must be a formal step to initiate the impeachment procedure according to Senate rules (leitura do pedido de impeachment) and must be recorded in the official journal of the Senate (Diário do Senado Federal) or officially announced via the official Senate news portal (Agência Senado). 

If such a reading takes place within the specified timeframe, the question resolves Yes, regardless of whether a special committee is subsequently formed or if the ultimate impeachment vote succeeds or fails.

If no such reading takes place between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, the question resolves No. If Alexandre de Moraes resigns or otherwise leaves his post before any request is read, this question will resolve No.

The primary data sources will be the official records of the Federal Senate of Brazil (https://www25.senado.leg.br/web/senado/diarios) and Agência Senado (https://www12.senado.leg.br/noticias). A consensus of credible media reporting (e.g., Reuters, Folha de S.Paulo, O Globo) may also be used to confirm the event.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the Senate will vote to proceed with the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes by the end of 2025. According to Brazilian law, before the Senate can vote to proceed, the President of the Senate must first accept an impeachment petition and read it in the plenary. This subquestion tracks this crucial initial bottleneck. With mass protests demanding his impeachment scheduled for September 7, 2025, observing whether the Senate leadership yields to this pressure and officially initiates the process in September will be a highly informative indicator for the ultimate outcome.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by US ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United States military initiate a drone, missile, or air strike that impacts the territory of Yemen between January 13, 2026, and February 12, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
To answer whether the US will strike three different countries in 2026, it is critical to track ongoing US military engagements. As of early January 2026, the US has already initiated qualifying strikes on two countries: Syria, where strikes targeted Islamic State infrastructure on January 10 (https://www.opindia.com/), and Venezuela, where Operation Absolute Resolve utilized bombers and drones on January 3 (https://theintercept.com/). With two countries already struck, a strike on a third country would effectively guarantee a 'Yes' resolution for the ultimate question. Yemen is a prime candidate for the third country, as US Central Command (CENTCOM) forces have frequently targeted Houthi rebel launch sites, radar installations, and weapons caches in Yemen over recent years to protect Red Sea shipping. Observing whether the US strikes Yemen in the coming month serves as a highly informative crux for the ultimate outcome.

Sources:
OpIndia - https://www.opindia.com/
The Intercept - https://theintercept.com/
US Central Command Press Releases - https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/
AP News Yemen Coverage - https://apnews.com/hub/yemen
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if official US government statements (such as from the Department of Defense or US Central Command) or a consensus of credible reporting confirms that US military forces initiated a drone, missile, or air strike that impacted the ground territory of Yemen between January 13, 2026, and February 12, 2026 (inclusive).

A qualifying strike is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact Yemeni ground territory. Strikes on embassies or consulates in Yemen count as striking Yemeni territory.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards resolution, regardless of whether they land on Yemeni territory or cause damage. Actions such as naval shelling, artillery fire, small arms fire, cyberattacks, or ground incursions do not qualify.

The primary resolution sources will be the US Central Command press releases (https://www.centcom.mil/MEDIA/PRESS-RELEASES/) and credible major news reporting (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/, AP News: https://apnews.com/). If a strike occurs within the window but is not officially acknowledged or reported by major outlets by February 19, 2026 (allowing a 7-day delay for information to emerge), the question will resolve 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: The US has already reportedly conducted strikes in Syria and Venezuela in early 2026. Because the ultimate question resolves affirmatively if the US strikes three countries, a strike on Yemen (a highly probable target given ongoing Red Sea security operations) would serve as the decisive third country. Confirming a strike on Yemen within this one-month window would confidently update forecasters' probabilities on the ultimate question towards 100%.

question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?
description:

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announce a reduction of the federal funds target range by 50 basis points or more between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Donald Trump has escalated his pressure on the Federal Reserve to rapidly lower interest rates, taking the unprecedented step of attempting to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook on August 28, 2025 (https://edition.cnn.com). Trump's administration stated it aims to secure a 4-3 majority on the Fed Board to heavily influence the upcoming FOMC policy meeting scheduled for mid-September (https://finance.yahoo.com). Throughout the year, the Fed has held the federal funds target range steady at 4.25-4.50% (https://www.inquirer.net). Because Trump's core motivation for altering the Fed Board's composition is to force faster and deeper interest rate cuts, the Fed's actions at the September FOMC meeting serve as a crucial crux. If the Fed capitulates or independently agrees with the need for a deep cut (50 basis points or more), Trump may view his pressure campaign as successful and back off from attempting to fire another governor by his October 31 deadline. Conversely, if the Fed only cuts by 25 basis points or holds rates steady, Trump is highly likely to continue his aggressive overhaul and target another governor, such as Chair Jerome Powell.

Sources:
CNN International: https://edition.cnn.com
Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com
Inquirer: https://www.inquirer.net
Federal Reserve Open Market Committee: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) publicly announces a cumulative reduction in the target range for the federal funds rate of 50 basis points (0.50 percentage points) or more between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The baseline target range for this reduction is 4.25-4.50%, meaning the new upper limit of the target range must be lowered to 4.00% or lower within the resolution window. Resolution will be based on the official FOMC post-meeting statements or implementation notes published on the Federal Reserve's official website (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm). If the FOMC cuts rates by less than 50 basis points (e.g., a 25 basis point cut), holds rates steady, or raises rates during the period between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves 'No'. If no FOMC statement regarding the target federal funds rate is released during this window, or if the meeting is delayed past 2025-10-01, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Trump's unprecedented attempt to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook is explicitly tied to his desire to force the central bank to lower interest rates more aggressively. The outcome of the September FOMC meeting serves as a primary crux for whether Trump will attempt to fire another governor by October 31. If the FOMC delivers a substantial rate cut of 50 basis points or more, it would align with Trump's demands, likely reducing his immediate hostility toward the board and mitigating the risk of another firing. If the FOMC refuses to cut rates deeply, Trump's frustration is highly likely to trigger further executive action against the Fed's remaining governors to forcibly secure a compliant majority.

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. officially announce a formal trade negotiation period or trade talks with Canada regarding tariffs between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In July and August 2025, the Trump administration enacted significant trade policy changes, including the removal of the de minimis exemption for imports under $800, which has heavily impacted Canadian businesses (https://globalnews.ca/). On August 1, 2025, President Trump signed an executive order raising tariffs on Canadian goods not covered by the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (CUSMA) from 25% to 35% (https://www.wtae.com/). At the same time, Trump agreed to enter a 90-day negotiating period with Mexico, maintaining their existing 25% tariff rate. For Trump to lower, pause, or delay tariffs on Canada by the end of 2025, it is highly probable that a similar negotiation period, bilateral trade talks, or a formal review process would be initiated and announced beforehand. This subquestion tracks whether the U.S. will announce such trade talks with Canada by the end of November, acting as a crucial leading indicator for the ultimate outcome.

Sources:
Global News - https://globalnews.ca/
Pittsburgh's Action News 4 - https://www.wtae.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the White House, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR), or President Donald Trump officially announces the initiation of formal trade negotiations, trade talks, or a designated negotiation period with Canada regarding tariffs or trade between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). The announcement must explicitly mention negotiations, talks, or a review period involving Canada and related to trade or tariffs. General comments about having a good relationship or speaking soon, without explicit reference to trade or tariff negotiations, will not suffice. If the announcement is made between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the question resolves Yes, regardless of when the talks are scheduled to actually begin. If no such announcement is made within this time window, the question resolves No. The primary sources for resolution will be official press releases from the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/) or the USTR (https://ustr.gov/about-us/policy-offices/press-office/press-releases), as well as official statements from Donald Trump's verified social media accounts.
subquestions.rationale: Before tariffs can be formally lowered or paused, diplomatic and trade negotiations are almost always a prerequisite, as demonstrated by the administration's 90-day negotiating period with Mexico. Tracking whether the U.S. announces trade talks with Canada by November 30 provides a strong, early signal of whether a tariff reduction or pause is realistically on the table for December 31.

subquestions.question: Will Sardar Biglari or his affiliated entities file a Schedule 13D amendment or proxy materials regarding Cracker Barrel (CBRL) with the SEC between October 31, 2025 and November 30, 2025?

subquestions.question: Will MicroStrategy's (MSTR) stock officially close at or below $280.00 on any regular trading day between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
MicroStrategy's (MSTR) premium to its Bitcoin holdings, measured by the market-to-net asset value (mNAV), has been steadily shrinking. In late 2024, the mNAV ratio was above 3.6x, but it fell to approximately 1.5x by September 2025 (https://www.coindesk.com/). This decline reflects MSTR's share price dropping roughly 26% since July 2025 to around $335. The stock's underperformance relative to its historical premium has been driven by concerns of shareholder dilution following the company's decision to scrap its pledge not to issue new shares when the mNAV is below 2.5x (https://cryptoslate.com/). 

Some analysts warn this policy shift could trigger a "spiral of doom" where the company repeatedly sells shares to service dividend obligations on preferred shares and debt, further diluting common equity and eroding the premium (https://thecryptobasic.com/). A significant decline in MSTR's share price, such as falling to or below $280, would strongly indicate a further loss of confidence from investors or a sharp drop in Bitcoin's price, both of which are direct precursors to the mNAV ratio falling to 1.00 by December.

Sources:
CoinDesk: https://www.coindesk.com/
CryptoSlate: https://cryptoslate.com/
The Crypto Basic: https://thecryptobasic.com/
Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MSTR/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the official closing price of MicroStrategy Inc. (NASDAQ: MSTR) is less than or equal to $280.00 on any regular trading day between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

Resolution will be determined by historical daily closing price data published by Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MSTR/history). Intraday lows do not count; only the official end-of-day closing price is considered. 

If a stock split, reverse stock split, or similar corporate action occurs during the resolution window, the $280.00 threshold will be adjusted proportionally to reflect the equivalent valuation. If Yahoo Finance data is unavailable or disputed, alternative authoritative financial data providers such as NASDAQ's official historical data (https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/mstr/historical) or Google Finance (https://www.google.com/finance/quote/MSTR:NASDAQ) will be used as fall-back sources. If trading of MSTR is halted and does not resume before the end of the resolution window, only the trading days that actually occurred will be evaluated.
subquestions.rationale: MSTR's mNAV is highly correlated with its share price because the metric is a ratio of the company's market capitalization to its net asset value (primarily Bitcoin). A continued drop in MSTR's stock price, particularly breaking below the $280 level, would signal an accelerating loss of its historical premium over Bitcoin. Tracking this threshold in October serves as a highly informative, observable proxy for the trajectory of the mNAV leading up to December.

question: Will Trump publicly disparage Netanyahu by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will the Israeli Knesset hold a plenum vote on any bill applying sovereignty or civilian law to the West Bank between October 25, 2025, and November 24, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
President Donald Trump recently asserted that his intervention was the primary reason the Gaza war ended, stating on October 24, 2025, 'I stopped Netanyahu.' Concurrently, the Trump administration has strongly opposed Israeli legislative efforts to annex parts of the West Bank. Vice President JD Vance condemned a far-right Israeli bill proposing annexation as a 'very stupid political stunt,' and Trump warned that such a move would cost Israel U.S. support because he 'had given his word to Arab nations against annexation.' (Source: https://www.timesofisrael.com/)

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government relies heavily on far-right coalition partners, such as Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben-Gvir, who strongly advocate for West Bank annexation. If Netanyahu yields to his coalition and allows an annexation bill to advance to a vote in the Knesset, it would constitute a direct defiance of Trump's explicit red lines. Trump frequently views policy defiance as a personal slight, especially when it threatens his diplomatic achievements. Therefore, the advancement of this bill serves as a strong early indicator of future conflict between the two leaders.

Sources:
The Times of Israel: https://www.timesofisrael.com/
The Jerusalem Post: https://www.jpost.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Israeli Knesset holds any official plenum vote (including a preliminary reading, first reading, second reading, or third reading) on any bill or resolution that explicitly proposes the annexation of, the application of Israeli sovereignty over, or the application of Israeli civilian law to any territory or Israeli settlements in the West Bank (Judea and Samaria) between October 25, 2025, and November 24, 2025 (inclusive).

The vote must take place within the resolution window from the start_date (2025-10-25) to the end_date (2025-11-24).

Committee-level votes or cabinet approvals do not count toward a Yes resolution; the vote must be held in the full Knesset plenum.
If a bill is introduced but no plenum vote occurs by 11:59 PM Israel Standard Time on November 24, 2025, the question resolves No.
If the Knesset goes on recess, is dissolved, or otherwise fails to hold such a vote within the specified window, the question resolves No.

Resolution will be based on official records from the Knesset website (https://main.knesset.gov.il/EN/Pages/default.aspx) or consensus reporting from at least two credible news sources, such as The Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com) or Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/).
subquestions.rationale: Trump has explicitly drawn a red line against West Bank annexation, warning it would cost Israel U.S. support. JD Vance recently lambasted a proposed annexation bill as an 'insult'. Netanyahu is caught between appeasing the Trump administration and satisfying his far-right coalition. If Netanyahu allows the Knesset to hold a plenum vote on the annexation bill, it would directly defy Trump. Given Trump's history of publicly attacking allies who defy him or undermine his deals, a Knesset vote on this issue is a strong crux that would highly increase the probability of Trump disparaging Netanyahu by December 31.

question: Will Russia enter Toretske by December 31?
description:

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

subquestions.question: Will the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) confirm a Russian advance near or within Toretsk between November 28, 2025, and December 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Toretsk (also known as Toretske) is a strategically significant mining city in Donetsk Oblast, Ukraine. Russian forces have conducted sustained offensive operations in the Toretsk direction throughout 2024 and 2025, aiming to exploit vulnerabilities and pressure the Ukrainian defensive lines connecting the broader Donetsk front. Forecasters attempting to predict whether Russian forces will officially enter the administrative boundaries of Toretske by December 31, 2025, can monitor the ongoing momentum of the Russian advance in the immediate vicinity. The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) routinely publishes daily 'Russian Offensive Campaign Assessments' tracking localized advances. If ISW confirms a new tactical advance in the Toretsk sector in the weeks leading up to the end of December, it serves as a strong indicator that Russian forces have the initiative and operational capability to potentially breach the city limits by the end of the year. Conversely, a lack of confirmed advances in this period would suggest a stabilized frontline or culminated offensive, significantly decreasing the likelihood of an entry into Toretsk by December 31.

Sources:
Institute for the Study of War: https://www.understandingwar.org/
DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/en
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
