The primary source will be the daily assessment reports published on the ISW website (https://www.understandingwar.org/). The text must clearly indicate a recent or newly confirmed Russian advance, typically found under the "Donetsk Oblast" or "Russian Operations" sections (e.g., using ISW's standard language such as "Geolocated footage published on [Date] indicates that Russian forces recently advanced near Toretsk"). 

Mere claims by Russian sources (e.g., "Russian milbloggers claimed...") that are not assessed as confirmed, verified, or supported by geolocated footage by ISW do not count towards a Yes resolution. 

If ISW stops publishing daily assessments or their website becomes permanently unavailable, the question will resolve Yes if the DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/en) records a confirmed update showing new Russian territorial gains within a 5-kilometer radius of Toretsk's city limits between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-20. If no such advance is confirmed by either source within the designated resolution window, the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: To breach the borders of Toretsk by December 31, Russian forces likely need to maintain offensive momentum and secure tactical gains on the approaches to the city in late November and early December. Confirmed advances by ISW during this time window act as a reliable, observable proxy for Russian momentum in the Toretsk sector.

question: Will Elon and DOGE cut 100-150k employees in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve based on the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees, as reported by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) under the "All Employees, Federal" series (CES9091000001), displayed here (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001)

This market will resolve according to the decrease in the seasonally adjusted number of federal employees between the December 2024 report and the December 2025 report.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The difference will be calculated as the December 2024 value minus the December 2025 value.

The December 2024 figure will be based on the initial December 2024 BLS Employment Situation report scheduled for release on January 3, 2025, and the initial December 2025 figure will be based on the report scheduled for release on January 9, 2026. Revisions made to these figures will not be considered, only the values reported in the initial reports will be used.

The resolution source will be the BLS Employment Situation data, specifically the series CES9091000001, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 or the official BLS website.

subquestions.question: Will the BLS report a month-over-month decrease of at least 15,000 seasonally adjusted federal employees for November 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question seeks to determine if a total of 100,000 to 150,000 federal employee jobs will be cut in 2025 under the leadership of Elon Musk and the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE). Achieving this annual target requires an average reduction of roughly 8,300 to 12,500 jobs per month. Recently, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) canceled the October 2025 jobs report due to incomplete data collection amidst a government shutdown, and the November 2025 report has been rescheduled to December 16, 2025. However, alternative employment data providers have already observed sharp public sector job losses; Revelio Labs reported a net reduction of 22,200 government employees in October 2025 alone. When the BLS releases its delayed November data, the month-over-month rate of job cuts will be a highly informative indicator. A reduction of 15,000 or more in a single month would demonstrate that DOGE is executing cuts at an aggressive pace that makes reaching the 100k-150k target highly probable. Sources: 
BLS Employment Situation: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm 
FRED Federal Employees Data: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001 
TalkMarkets October Nonfarm Employment: https://talkmarkets.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports a month-over-month decrease of 15,000 or more in the seasonally adjusted 'All Employees, Federal' series (CES9091000001) for November 2025. 

The resolution window is between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30 (inclusive). Qualifying data must be published in a BLS Employment Situation report within this timeframe. 

The change will be calculated by subtracting the preliminary November 2025 figure from the October 2025 figure, exactly as reported in the same BLS release (expected December 16, 2025). If the difference (October value - November value) is 15,000 or greater, it resolves Yes. 

Fallback for missing October data: If the BLS does not publish an October 2025 figure due to the canceled October report, the average monthly decrease from the last reported month will be used to resolve the market. For example, ((September 2025 value - November 2025 value) / 2). If this average monthly decrease is 15,000 or greater, the question resolves Yes. 

If the decrease is less than 15,000, or if employment increases, it resolves No. 
If the BLS does not release a November 2025 figure for this series between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-30, the question resolves as Unresolvable. 

The official resolution sources are the BLS Employment Situation release (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm) and the FRED database (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CES9091000001).
subquestions.rationale: Rather than simply restating the ultimate question with an earlier deadline, this subquestion focuses on the velocity of job cuts (month-over-month change). A decrease of 15,000 jobs in November signals that the ongoing workforce reductions are exceeding the average monthly pace needed to hit the 100k-150k annual target, providing a strong near-term signal of the ultimate outcome.

question: Pakistan strike on India by December 31?

Missiles or drones that are intercepted before reaching Indian territory, as well as surface-to-air missile strikes, will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution regardless of whether debris lands on Indian soil or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or any operation conducted by Pakistani ground forces will not qualify as a strike under this market.

subquestions.question: Will a militant or terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir result in the deaths of at least 5 Indian security personnel or civilians between October 15, 2025 and November 14, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In May 2025, India and Pakistan engaged in a major military escalation involving cross-border drone, missile, and air strikes. This conflict, marked by India's 'Operation Sindoor' and Pakistan's 'Operation Bunyan Ul Marsoos', was precipitated by the April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam, which killed 26 civilians. India's retaliatory kinetic actions against terror infrastructure and Pakistani military installations prompted Pakistan to launch its own guided rockets and drones at Indian cities and military sites. Because major militant attacks in Jammu and Kashmir have historically triggered escalatory cycles of cross-border military strikes between the two nuclear-armed neighbors, monitoring the region for mass-casualty terror events provides a critical early warning indicator for potential Pakistani strikes on India. A highly lethal attack would likely force Indian retaliation, significantly raising the probability of a subsequent Pakistani counter-strike.

Sources:
NDTV - 'Less Than 50 Weapons Fired By IAF To End Conflict': https://www.ndtv.com/
India Today - 'Pak's Fatah-1 rocket debris fished out of Srinagar's Dal Lake': https://www.indiatoday.in/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

- The deaths must be a direct result of the attack. Deaths of the militants/terrorists themselves do not count towards the 5-person threshold.
- Cross-border artillery shelling, small arms fire, or missile strikes officially attributed exclusively to the regular Pakistani armed forces do not count as a 'militant or terrorist attack' for the purposes of this question, unless the incident specifically involves an infiltration or attack by non-state militant actors.
- The deaths must occur and be publicly reported by the end of the resolution window (2025-11-14).

The resolution will be based on official statements or press releases from the Jammu and Kashmir Police (https://jkpolice.gov.in/), the Indian Ministry of Home Affairs (https://mha.gov.in/), or a consensus of credible reporting from major Indian news outlets such as NDTV (https://www.ndtv.com/), India Today (https://www.indiatoday.in/), or The Hindu (https://www.thehindu.com/). If no such attack occurs, or if the confirmed death toll of civilians and security personnel is less than 5 by the end of the resolution window, the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: The recent May 2025 missile and drone exchanges between India and Pakistan were directly triggered by the deadly April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam. Because significant terrorist attacks in J&K are the primary catalyst for Indian cross-border retaliatory strikes (which then trigger Pakistani military responses), tracking mass-casualty terror events acts as a robust early indicator for whether the escalation ladder will be climbed again prior to December 31.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs favorably report or advance the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (H.R. 3633 or a Senate companion bill) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:

It successfully passed the U.S. House of Representatives on July 17, 2025, with a bipartisan 294-134 vote. For the bill to become law in 2025, it must navigate the U.S. Senate, which involves passing through the relevant committees before a floor vote. In August 2025, Senator Cynthia Lummis stated that the legislative goal is to move the bill through the Senate Banking Committee in September, followed by the Senate Agriculture Committee in October, aiming to reach the President's desk by the end of the year. Tracking the Senate Banking Committee's action during September provides a critical early indicator of the legislation's momentum and its real chances of meeting the year-end deadline.

Sources:
Congress.gov H.R.3633 - https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633
CryptoNews - https://cryptonews.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs officially advances, favorably reports, or 'orders to be reported' the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act of 2025 (H.R. 3633) or a formally designated Senate companion bill. The primary resolution source will be the official legislative action tracker on Congress.gov for H.R. 3633 (https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/3633/all-actions) or its direct Senate equivalent. A qualifying event must be recorded in the official actions list indicating that the committee has approved or ordered the measure reported out of committee. If no such action occurs by 11:59 PM ET on 2025-10-01, the question resolves 'No'. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: For the CLARITY Act to be signed into law by the end of 2025, it must swiftly advance through the Senate. Proponents of the bill have explicitly outlined a timeline that requires the Senate Banking Committee to advance the legislation in September. If this specific milestone is missed or delayed, the likelihood of completing all remaining legislative steps—including the Senate Agriculture Committee, a full Senate vote, and reconciliation with the House—before year-end drops substantially, making this an ideal crux for forecasting the ultimate outcome.

question: Will Kamala Harris endorse Mamdani?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Kamala Harris announces that she will vote for Zohran Mamdani or endorses Mamdani for the 2025 NYC Mayor election between June 26, and November 3, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

If Kamala Harris announces that she will vote for another candidate or endorses another candidate for NYC Mayor, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be official information from Kamala Harris or one of her representatives, or a consensus of credible reporting of Kamala Harris's endorsement.

subquestions.question: Will House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries publicly endorse Zohran Mamdani for NYC Mayor before September 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Zohran Mamdani, a self-identified socialist, won the Democratic primary for the 2025 New York City mayoral race. While he has secured endorsements from prominent progressives like Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, mainstream Democratic leaders have thus far hesitated to back him. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, a leading New York Democrat, met with Mamdani in July 2025 but has not yet offered an endorsement. Some political commentators, such as former Congressman Anthony Weiner, predict that establishment leaders like Jeffries and Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer will inevitably endorse the Democratic nominee to project party unity ahead of the 2026 midterms, despite concerns about alienating moderate voters.

Sources:
Bernie Sanders Endorsement: https://nystateofpolitics.com
Hakeem Jeffries Meeting: https://www.yahoo.com
Anthony Weiner Prediction: https://dailycaller.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries publicly endorses Zohran Mamdani for the 2025 New York City mayoral election, or explicitly announces that he will vote for him, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-20 (inclusive). 

An endorsement or voting intention must be publicly stated by Jeffries himself, released through his official congressional or campaign channels, or widely reported by a consensus of credible news organizations. If Jeffries explicitly declines to endorse, endorses a different candidate, or if the end date (2025-09-20 at 11:59 PM ET) passes without an endorsement, this question resolves 'No'.

Resolution sources will include Hakeem Jeffries's official website (https://jeffries.house.gov/), his official social media accounts (e.g., https://x.com/RepJeffries), or major credible news outlets such as The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com) and Politico (https://www.politico.com).
subquestions.rationale: Kamala Harris, as a national Democratic leader, typically aligns her down-ballot endorsements with the consensus of local and national party establishments. Because Mamdani represents the far-left wing of the party, mainstream leaders have been cautious. If Hakeem Jeffries—the highest-ranking Democrat in the House and a prominent New Yorker—endorses Mamdani, it signals that the Democratic establishment has decided to unify behind him. This dramatically increases the likelihood that Kamala Harris will also offer her endorsement. Conversely, if Jeffries holds out, it is highly unlikely Harris would step in.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 12 launch by November 30?
description:
If the 12th SpaceX Starship successfully launches from its launch pad by November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Yes”. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The outcome of any launch will be corroborated by examining official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

Any subsequent anomaly (e.g., an explosion) after the launch will have no bearing on the outcome. Any name change of the Starship with another vehicle will have no bearing on the outcome of the market.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX fully stack the Starship Flight 12 vehicle (Ship on Super Heavy) at a launch pad between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-15?
subquestions.background_information:
SpaceX successfully launched Starship Flight 11 on October 13, 2025 (https://www.spacex.com/launches/). With a stated goal by CEO Elon Musk to increase the launch cadence to one flight every 3-4 weeks, Flight 12 is expected to follow shortly. Before any Starship test flight, the upper stage (Starship) must be lifted and placed on top of the Super Heavy booster at an orbital launch mount (a process known as "stacking"). This allows the company to perform fully integrated testing, such as a Wet Dress Rehearsal (WDR), which is required before a launch license can be utilized and the vehicle can be cleared for flight. Tracking when the vehicle is fully stacked is a crucial early indicator of the launch timeline. If the vehicle is stacked by mid-November, a launch by November 30 is highly plausible. If it is not, the timeline makes a November launch very difficult.

Sources:
SpaceX Launches: https://www.spacex.com/launches/
SpaceX Official X (Twitter): https://twitter.com/SpaceX
NASA Spaceflight YouTube Channel: https://www.youtube.com/c/NASASpaceflight
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Starship upper stage assigned to Flight Test 12 is fully stacked (lifted and placed) onto its Super Heavy booster at any orbital launch mount at Starbase, Texas, between the start date of 2025-10-18 and the end date of 2025-11-15 23:59:59 UTC, inclusive.

The stacking event must be confirmed by official SpaceX communications (e.g., website updates at https://www.spacex.com/launches/ or posts from their official X account https://twitter.com/SpaceX) OR via clear visual confirmation from credible third-party spaceflight observers with live feeds of the pad, such as NASA Spaceflight (https://www.youtube.com/c/NASASpaceflight).

If the vehicle was already fully stacked before 2025-10-18, or if it is not stacked by 2025-11-15 23:59:59 UTC, this question resolves No. If the vehicle is stacked within the resolution window and subsequently de-stacked, the question will still resolve Yes. The specific vehicle designations (e.g., Ship and Booster numbers) do not matter as long as they are assigned to the Flight 12 mission.
subquestions.rationale: Stacking the Starship vehicle on the orbital launch mount is a necessary physical milestone that precedes integrated testing (like wet dress rehearsals) and the launch itself. Because it typically takes days to weeks to perform necessary checks and tests after stacking, if SpaceX has not stacked the vehicle by November 15, the chances of launching by November 30 drop significantly. Thus, it acts as a strong, verifiable crux for the ultimate question.

question: Will Khamenei visit Russia by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ali Khamenei visits Russia by June 30, 2026, 11:59PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "visit" is defined as Ali Khamenei physically entering the terrestrial territory of Russia in a voluntary capacity. Whether or not Ali Khamenei enters Russian airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

Entering Russia requires physically entering sovereign Russian territory, including all Russian federal subjects and territories. Areas under Russian control but not under Russian sovereignty (e.g., Crimea) do not count. Russian airspace, Russian embassies/consulates abroad, and international zones do not constitute Russian sovereign territory.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Ayatollah Ali Khamenei be officially confirmed to be outside the territory of Iran at any point between January 10, 2026, and February 9, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Iran is currently experiencing its largest wave of protests to date following a 12-day war with Israel in June 2025 and a severe economic crisis. Demonstrations have reportedly spread across over 200 locations (India Today, 2026-01-09). Amid this crisis, intelligence reports and widespread speculation indicate that Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has prepared an evacuation plan for himself and his inner circle, with Moscow as the highly probable destination. Recent reports suggest that Russian military transport planes, operating under civilian disguises, have conducted multiple flights between Mineralnye Vody and Tehran. These flights are suspected of moving gold and assets out of Iran in preparation for this evacuation (Хартия 97, 2026-01-09). Prediction markets, such as Be In Crypto, indicate high odds of Khamenei being ousted in early 2026. Because Khamenei's reported evacuation plan designates Russia as his destination, any official confirmation that he has fled or left Iranian territory would serve as a critical leading indicator for his eventual arrival in Russia.

Sources:
India Today: https://www.indiatoday.in/
Хартия 97: https://charter97.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if it is confirmed by official statements from the United States government (e.g., the White House, the Department of State), the government of the United Kingdom, the government of Iran, or a consensus of credible international reporting (such as Reuters, Associated Press, or BBC) that Ayatollah Ali Khamenei is physically located outside the sovereign territory of Iran at any point between 2026-01-10 and 2026-02-09 (inclusive).

'Outside the sovereign territory' means he is not physically present within Iran's terrestrial borders, territorial waters, or airspace. The confirmation does not need to specify his exact location, only that he is no longer within Iranian territory. If he is confirmed to have departed Iran prior to 2026-01-10 but remains outside Iran during the specified window, this question resolves Yes. If his location cannot be confirmed to be outside Iran by the end of the day on 2026-02-09, or if reports remain unverified rumors without official corroboration or credible consensus reporting, the question resolves No.

Relevant official US Department of State press releases can be monitored at https://www.state.gov/press-releases/ and Reuters world news at https://www.reuters.com/world/.
subquestions.rationale: Khamenei is currently facing massive protests, and intelligence suggests he has an evacuation plan to flee to Russia. A confirmation that he has physically left Iran during this early window is a necessary first step to him enacting this plan. If he is confirmed to be outside Iran during this period, it becomes highly probable that he will visit Russia by the June deadline, making this an excellent crux to track progress toward the ultimate question.

question: Will Han Duck-soo be sentenced to prison before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Han Duck-soo is sentenced to any time in jail/prison for charges related to the 2024 South Korean political crisis, including but not limited to allegations of failure to promulgate legislation, obstruction of constitutional processes, or other criminal acts stemming from his actions as Acting President and Prime Minister by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will remain open through 2026 regardless of whether Han Duck-soo's initial sentencing includes prison.  Any sentencing will qualify, regardless of subsequent appeals or changes to the sentence.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the South Korean government and law enforcement; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will South Korean prosecutors formally announce their sentence demand (guhyeong) for Han Duck-soo in his first-instance trial between November 25, 2025, and December 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Former South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo was indicted on August 29, 2025, on charges including abetting insurrection, perjury, and falsifying official documents related to former President Yoon Suk-yeol's failed martial law declaration in December 2024 (https://en.yna.co.kr/). His trial began on September 30, 2025, at the Seoul Central District Court (https://www.straitstimes.com/). In South Korean criminal trials, the prosecution concludes its case at the final hearing by formally stating its sentencing demand (guhyeong) to the judges, after which the defense makes its closing arguments and the court sets a date for the verdict. Due to the severe charges, prosecutors previously sought an arrest warrant for Han, which was denied by the court due to a low risk of flight or evidence destruction (https://www.koreaherald.com/). Monitoring when the prosecution makes its final sentencing demand will provide strong evidence regarding the pace of the trial. If the sentencing demand occurs before late December 2025, it strongly indicates that a verdict will be reached in early 2026, long before the 2027 deadline of the ultimate question.

Sources:
Yonhap News Agency: https://en.yna.co.kr/
The Straits Times: https://www.straitstimes.com/
The Korea Herald: https://www.koreaherald.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves "Yes" if credible news reports or official South Korean court records confirm that the prosecution has formally made its sentencing demand (guhyeong) for Han Duck-soo in his first-instance trial between 2025-11-25 and 2025-12-25 (inclusive). The sentencing demand refers to the formal request by the prosecutors at the final hearing of the trial, stating the specific punishment (e.g., number of years in prison) they are asking the court to impose. If the prosecution's sentencing demand is not made, or is made before 2025-11-25 or after 2025-12-25, this question resolves "No". If the trial is suspended, postponed, or delayed such that the final hearing does not occur within this resolution window, the question resolves "No". Resolution will be based on reporting from major South Korean and international news outlets, such as Yonhap News Agency (https://en.yna.co.kr/) and The Korea Herald (https://www.koreaherald.com/), or official announcements from the Supreme Court of Korea (https://eng.scourt.go.kr/eng/main/Main.work).
subquestions.rationale: The timing of the prosecution's sentencing demand is a key milestone in South Korean criminal proceedings, marking the end of the trial phase and preceding the final verdict. By predicting whether this milestone occurs by late December 2025, forecasters can accurately gauge the pace of the trial. A fast trial makes a conviction and sentence before 2027 highly likely, while a delayed trial might push the timeline closer to the ultimate question's deadline or indicate complex legal disputes that could affect the final outcome.

question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

subquestions.question: Will the EIA report U.S. commercial crude oil inventories (excluding SPR) below 420 million barrels in any Weekly Petroleum Status Report released between December 27, 2025, and January 26, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The ultimate question asks if Crude Oil (CL) futures will hit $70 by the end of June 2026. According to recent market data, light sweet crude oil (WTI) futures for near-term 2026 delivery were trading between $58.00 and $60.50 per barrel in late 2025 (Source: https://apnews.com/hub/oil-prices). For crude oil to rally roughly $10-$12 and reach the $70 mark, a strong bullish catalyst—such as tightening physical supply—is required. The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) Weekly Petroleum Status Report is one of the most closely watched gauges of physical market conditions. A scenario where U.S. commercial crude inventories (excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve) drop or remain strictly below 420 million barrels signals a tight domestic supply, which typically provides upward fundamental pressure on WTI futures prices.

Sources:
AP News Oil Prices Hub: https://apnews.com/hub/oil-prices
EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report: https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) reports a figure of strictly less than 420,000 thousand barrels (i.e., less than 420.0 million barrels) for "U.S. commercial crude oil inventories (excluding those in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve)" in any Weekly Petroleum Status Report (WPSR) officially published between December 27, 2025, and January 26, 2026 (inclusive).

The primary resolution source will be the official EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report (https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly/), specifically checking the headline U.S. commercial crude oil inventory figure for the reporting weeks released within the resolution window.

Only the initially reported headline figures in the weekly releases published within the specified timeframe (2025-12-27 to 2026-01-26) are considered. Any subsequent retroactive revisions to this data published after January 26, 2026, will not affect the resolution. If the EIA fails to publish any WPSR during this exact period, or permanently alters its reporting methodology such that a directly comparable commercial crude inventory metric (excluding SPR) is no longer available, the question will resolve as "No".
subquestions.rationale: U.S. commercial crude oil inventory is a crucial early indicator of physical market tightness. If inventories are constrained (falling below 420 million barrels) in early 2026, it indicates that physical supply is struggling to keep up with demand. This fundamental tightness acts as a strong upward driver for crude oil prices, heavily increasing the likelihood that the CL futures will bridge the gap from $58 to the $70 target by June.

question: David Baszucki out as Roblox CEO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if David Baszucki ceases to be CEO of Roblox for any length of time between August 14, and December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An announcement of David Baszucki's resignation/firing before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the announced resignation/firing goes into effect.

This market's primary resolution source will be official information from Roblox and/or David Baszucki, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will a major brand or publicly traded company publicly suspend or terminate its partnership or advertising with Roblox over safety concerns between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Roblox Corporation is currently embroiled in a significant public relations crisis regarding child safety on its platform. CEO David Baszucki is facing intense backlash, including a viral petition with over 250,000 signatures demanding his resignation and a lawsuit from the Louisiana Attorney General alleging the platform fails to protect minors. Historically, executive turnover during tech and social media scandals is often accelerated when controversies threaten core revenue streams—most notably through advertiser boycotts (as seen in past crises on platforms like YouTube and X/Twitter). Roblox partners with numerous major brands (e.g., Nike, Walmart, Gucci) to create in-game branded "experiences." If the ongoing scandal causes these corporate partners to withdraw, the financial and reputational damage would severely increase pressure on the Roblox Board of Directors to replace Baszucki.

Sources:
MediaPost: https://www.mediapost.com/
The Times of India: https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/
Gameranx: https://gameranx.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), at least one publicly traded company or a company listed on the most recent Fortune 500 or Fortune Global 500 list publicly announces that it is pausing, suspending, or terminating its advertising spend, branded experiences, or formal partnership with Roblox Corporation.

To qualify for a Yes resolution:
1. The stated or widely reported reason for the suspension/termination must explicitly relate to child safety, content moderation, or the ongoing controversies surrounding Roblox's environment for minors.
2. The action must be confirmed via an official statement/press release from the brand OR verified reporting from at least two of the following credible news organizations: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com), CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com), The Wall Street Journal (https://www.wsj.com), or The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com).

If the suspension or termination occurs but the company attributes it solely to routine business decisions (e.g., campaign end dates) without mentioning safety or platform controversies, it does not count.
If no qualifying event is confirmed to have occurred between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Brand safety is a paramount concern for major corporations. If the child safety scandal escalates to the point where Roblox loses high-profile corporate partners, the direct threat to the company's monetization and public image would serve as a strong catalyst for the Board of Directors to demand new leadership. Thus, an advertiser pullout is a highly informative early indicator of David Baszucki's potential ouster.

question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt reaches the listed value this year at any point by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimate the U.S. federal budget deficit for Fiscal Year 2025 to be $1.85 trillion or greater in its September 2025 Monthly Budget Review?
subquestions.background_information:
The U.S. national debt surpassed $37 trillion in August 2025 and has been growing at a rapid pace of about $1 trillion every five months (https://apnews.com/). A key driver of this continuous debt accumulation is the federal budget deficit. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) regularly tracks government spending and revenues. In a report covering up to August 2025, the CBO estimated that the government had accumulated a $2 trillion deficit over the first 11 months of Fiscal Year 2025. However, because September typically sees an influx of quarterly corporate and individual tax receipts resulting in a monthly surplus, the CBO projected the final total deficit for the entirety of FY 2025 (which ended September 30, 2025) to settle at $1.8 trillion (https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review).

The CBO generally releases its 'Monthly Budget Review' for September—summarizing the completed fiscal year—by mid-October. This report provides an early, highly reliable estimate of the total fiscal year deficit before the Treasury Department publishes its final official year-end joint statement. If the September deficit estimate exceeds the previously projected $1.8 trillion and reaches $1.85 trillion or higher, it would signal that government spending outpaced late-year projections or revenues underperformed. This higher-than-expected borrowing requirement would be a direct indicator that the total national debt is accelerating even faster than anticipated.

Sources:
- Associated Press: https://apnews.com/
- Congressional Budget Office Monthly Budget Review: https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review
- KPVI News: https://www.kpvi.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) officially publishes its 'Monthly Budget Review' for September 2025 between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19 (inclusive), and the report estimates the total U.S. federal budget deficit for Fiscal Year 2025 to be $1.85 trillion (equivalent to $1,850 billion) or greater. 

The primary resolution source will be the official CBO Monthly Budget Review published on the CBO website (https://www.cbo.gov/topics/budget/monthly-budget-review). Resolvers must use the total deficit figure reported for 'Fiscal Year 2025' or the 12-month 'Year-to-Date' total ending in September 2025.

If the stated deficit is exactly $1.85 trillion (or 1,850 billion) or higher, the question resolves Yes. If the figure is strictly less than $1.85 trillion, the question resolves No. 

Edge Cases and Clarifications:
- If the CBO provides a range for the estimated deficit rather than a point estimate, the arithmetic midpoint of the range will be used for resolution.
- If the September 2025 Monthly Budget Review is not published between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-19, the question will resolve as Unresolvable, as the event falls outside the resolution window.
- Any subsequent modifications, errata, or revisions to the deficit figure published by the CBO or the Treasury Department after 2025-10-19 will not be considered for the resolution of this market. Only the initial figure published in the report within the specified window will be evaluated.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the total U.S. national debt will hit $38 trillion by the end of 2025. The speed at which the gross debt grows is largely dictated by the size of the federal budget deficit. By measuring the CBO's preliminary year-end deficit estimate in mid-October, forecasters get a critical, early pulse on the government's borrowing velocity. A deficit of $1.85 trillion or more would mean the government overshot its $1.8 trillion baseline projection, implying the Treasury must issue more debt than planned, making the eventuality of reaching $38 trillion by December 31 much more likely.

question: Will CME self certify a sports contract in 2025?
description:
This market resolves to “Yes” if CME Group files a self-certification under CFTC Regulation 40.2 for at least one sport-based event contract by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it resolves to “No.”

For this market, “self-certify” means CME, acting as a DCM or self-listing exchange, submits a written certification per 17 C.F.R. § 40.2 that the contract complies with the Commodity Exchange Act and CFTC regulations. The contract must explicitly reference a sporting event (e.g. game result, player performance, etc.). Announcements alone do not qualify; the filing must be made and publicly verifiable.

The resolution source will be the CFTC’s public filings, CME’s disclosures, and a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will at least one U.S. state gaming regulator (other than Ohio) issue a formal public warning or regulatory directive to sportsbooks regarding sports-based event contracts between October 9, 2025, and November 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The intersection of prediction markets and sports betting has drawn increasing regulatory scrutiny as operators bridge the gap between commodity derivatives and gambling. In August 2025, the Ohio Casino Control Commission issued a stern warning to licensed sportsbooks that offering or associating with prediction-market contracts for sporting events could jeopardize their state gaming licenses (Covers, https://www.covers.com/). This warning directly impacts operators like FanDuel, which recently partnered with CME Group to offer event contracts on non-sporting events, while other operators pursue National Futures Association (NFA) licenses (Yahoo Sports, https://sports.yahoo.com/). At the federal level, the CFTC issued a non-interventionist advisory on September 30, 2025, leaving the legality of these contracts largely subject to ongoing court battles between state sovereignty and federal preemption (JD Supra, https://www.jdsupra.com/). Given that FanDuel and similar CME partners rely heavily on their state-licensed sports betting operations, the spread of state-level regulatory threats would likely deter them—and consequently CME—from pursuing sports event contracts.

Sources:
Covers - Ohio Warns Sportsbooks Contemplating Prediction Market Services: https://www.covers.com/
Yahoo Sports - States Rights Vs. Federalism: Can Prediction Markets Be Kept At Bay?: https://sports.yahoo.com/
JD Supra - CFTC's Advisory on Exchange-Listed Sports Event Contracts: https://www.jdsupra.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08 (inclusive), any U.S. state gaming regulatory agency or commission (excluding the Ohio Casino Control Commission) publishes a formal public warning, letter, advisory, or regulatory directive explicitly stating that offering, facilitating, or associating with sports-based event contracts (or sports prediction markets) may jeopardize a state sports wagering/gaming license or violates state gambling laws. The directive must be publicly verifiable via the official website of the respective state regulator (e.g., New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement at https://www.njoag.gov/about/divisions-and-offices/division-of-gaming-enforcement/, Nevada Gaming Control Board at https://gaming.nv.gov/, or Massachusetts Gaming Commission at https://massgaming.com/) or through consensus reporting by credible industry news sources such as Covers (https://www.covers.com) or Legal Sports Report (https://www.legalsportsreport.com). The event must occur and be made public strictly between 2025-10-09 and 2025-11-08. Internal, non-public communications do not count. If a state issued such a warning prior to 2025-10-09 and merely restates it without a new formal directive, it does not qualify. If no such warning is issued by a new state by 11:59 PM ET on 2025-11-08, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: CME Group's retail strategy for event contracts is heavily reliant on partnerships with major operators like FanDuel. These sportsbooks derive their primary revenue from state-licensed sports betting. If a wave of state regulators threatens to revoke these core licenses over the offering of federally-regulated sports event contracts, sportsbooks will refuse to clear or offer them. Consequently, CME would have no retail incentive or viable partner network to self-certify a sports contract. Tracking state regulatory pushback therefore serves as a highly informative leading indicator for CME's willingness to pursue sports event contracts in 2025.

question: Will SpaceX Starship Flight Test 11 Superheavy explode?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the booster for the eleventh Starship-SuperHeavy test explodes at any point during the test from the start of fueling operations to 60 minutes after it makes contact with Earth upon landing. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An explosion is defined as a violent and catastrophic event resulting in the destruction of all or part of the vehicle, regardless of intent or context (e.g., a planned termination event would also count).

If the eleventh launch has not occurred by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

Note: The sixth Starship-SuperHeavy test flight which exploded after executing controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico would qualify for a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official video provided by SpaceX (https://www.youtube.com/c/SpaceX), as well as secondary video feeds and/or written reports if necessary.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX officially announce an attempt to catch the Super Heavy booster for Starship Flight 11 using the launch tower arms prior to October 10, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
During SpaceX's Starship Flight 10 test in late August 2025, the Super Heavy booster executed a planned, controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico and eventually exploded in a fireball (https://earthsky.org/). While this marked a significant success, SpaceX's long-term operational goal is to fly the Super Heavy booster back to the Starbase launch site and catch it mid-air using the launch tower's mechanical arms, affectionately known as 'Mechazilla' or 'chopsticks'. Attempting a launch pad catch introduces immense operational risks: if a Raptor engine fails during the final descent or if the booster loses aerodynamic control, it could crash into the tower or the ground, likely resulting in a catastrophic explosion. Conversely, a planned water splashdown keeps the booster far away from launch infrastructure, meaning any impact-related explosion would happen over the ocean. Consequently, knowing whether SpaceX intends to perform this high-risk maneuver during Flight 11 is a key crux in forecasting the likelihood of a booster explosion.

Sources:
SpaceX Official Website: https://www.spacex.com/
SpaceX Official X Account: https://twitter.com/SpaceX
SpaceX Starship Page: https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/starship/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if an official SpaceX communication explicitly announces between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive) that the mission plan for Starship Flight 11 includes an attempt to catch the Super Heavy booster using the launch tower's arms.

Qualifying sources for resolution include:
1. Updates, press releases, or mission descriptions posted on SpaceX's official website (https://www.spacex.com/launches/ or https://www.spacex.com/vehicles/starship/).
2. Public posts from the official SpaceX X/Twitter account (https://twitter.com/SpaceX).
3. Public posts from SpaceX CEO Elon Musk's official X/Twitter account (https://twitter.com/elonmusk).
4. Statements made during official SpaceX livestreams or publicized company presentations.

The announcement must specify that the tower catch attempt is planned for Flight Test 11. If the announcement states that a catch attempt is conditional (e.g., 'we will attempt a tower catch if the boostback burn is nominal'), this will still count as a 'Yes' resolution, as the attempt is part of the mission profile. If SpaceX launches Flight 11 between 2025-09-10 and 2025-10-10 and attempts a catch without a prior written announcement, the question will also resolve 'Yes'.

If no such announcement is made by 2025-10-10 at 23:59:59 UTC, or if SpaceX explicitly announces that the catch attempt will be delayed to Flight 12 or a later mission, the question resolves 'No'. If an announcement is made within the window but later retracted before the end of the window, it will still resolve 'Yes' because the plan was officially announced.
subquestions.rationale: A launch tower catch is a completely unprecedented and highly dangerous maneuver. If SpaceX decides to attempt it on Flight 11, the Super Heavy booster will need to return to the launch site and hover over solid ground and infrastructure. Any slight error in navigation, engine relight, or structural integrity during this phase will likely result in a hard crash and a massive explosion. Therefore, the presence of a catch attempt drastically increases the baseline probability that the booster will explode compared to a safe, planned splashdown in the ocean.

question: Will Atlas have a Windows app live by December 31?

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI release an iOS or Android version of the Atlas browser by November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 21, 2025, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Atlas, an AI-enabled web browser built on the Chromium engine. Atlas integrates OpenAI's ChatGPT directly into the browser interface, replacing the traditional address bar with a chat interface and offering an "agent mode" to automate web tasks. At launch, the browser was only made available globally on Apple's macOS. During the announcement, OpenAI explicitly stated that support for Windows, iOS, and Android is expected "soon" or in the "coming weeks". This subquestion evaluates whether OpenAI will launch either of the mobile versions (iOS or Android) within a month of the initial macOS rollout. A prompt release of mobile apps would signal strong momentum in their cross-platform rollout strategy, raising the likelihood that the Windows version will be deployed before the end of the year.

Sources:

Fast Company: https://www.fastcompany.com/
OpenAI News: https://openai.com/news/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if OpenAI publicly releases any version (including stable, beta, or preview) of the Atlas browser for either iOS or Android between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive). 

The application must be officially released by OpenAI and must be a dedicated browser app (branded as Atlas or clearly marketed as their new AI browser), distinct from the existing standard ChatGPT app. Availability in any regional Apple App Store (https://apps.apple.com/) or Google Play Store (https://play.google.com/store/apps) qualifies, as does an official public TestFlight or an official APK download link provided directly by OpenAI.

If no iOS or Android version of Atlas is made publicly available for download by November 22, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET, this question resolves No. Resolution will primarily be determined by official announcements from OpenAI (e.g., via https://openai.com/news or their official social media channels) and corroborated by verified public availability of the app on the respective platforms.
subquestions.rationale: OpenAI explicitly promised that Windows, iOS, and Android versions of their new Atlas browser are "forthcoming." Monitoring the rollout of the iOS or Android versions provides a clear, observable proxy for OpenAI's cross-platform engineering and deployment pace. If they successfully release mobile versions within a month of the macOS launch, it is highly likely that the Windows version is on track for a December 31 release. Conversely, if no additional platforms are launched by November 22, it suggests a slower-than-expected cross-platform development cycle, which would significantly lower the probability of the Windows app launching by the ultimate deadline.

question: Will Graham Platner drop out of Maine Senate race by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Graham Platner withdraws from or officially announces his withdrawal from the 2026 Maine U.S. Senate race, or announces the suspension of his 2026 Senate campaign, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Graham Platner or his official/legal representatives, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Senator Bernie Sanders publicly withdraw his endorsement of Graham Platner for the U.S. Senate by November 22, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Graham Platner, a Democratic candidate for the U.S. Senate in Maine, is challenging incumbent Republican Susan Collins and prominent primary rival Governor Janet Mills. Platner secured a high-profile endorsement from Senator Bernie Sanders, who backed him over the establishment-supported Mills. However, in late October 2025, Platner's campaign faced severe controversies: on October 19, his political director resigned following the unearthing of old Reddit posts containing racist and xenophobic remarks by Platner. A few days later, on October 22, Platner publicly apologized for a tattoo resembling a Nazi SS symbol, which he promised to cover or remove. Despite these scandals and calls from fellow primary contender Jordan Wood to drop out, Platner has vowed to remain in the race, and Sanders had not immediately pulled his support. Because Sanders' endorsement is the cornerstone of Platner's progressive credibility and fundraising, the retraction of this endorsement would be a crucial indicator of Platner's campaign viability. If Sanders drops his support, Platner would likely face insurmountable pressure to withdraw before December 31.

Sources:
AP News: https://apnews.com
HuffPost: https://www.huffpost.com
The Maine Wire: https://www.themainewire.com
Bernie Sanders Official Site: https://berniesanders.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-23 and 2025-11-22 (inclusive), Senator Bernie Sanders or his official representatives publicly announce the withdrawal, retraction, or suspension of his endorsement of Graham Platner for the 2026 Maine U.S. Senate race. The question will also resolve Yes if Sanders officially endorses another candidate in the Maine Democratic Senate primary (such as Janet Mills or Jordan Wood) during this window, which would effectively revoke his exclusive support for Platner.

The announcement must be verifiable via official channels, such as Sanders' Senate website (https://www.sanders.senate.gov/), his campaign website (https://berniesanders.com/), his official social media accounts (e.g., https://x.com/SenSanders or https://x.com/BernieSanders), or via on-the-record statements reported by credible national news organizations (e.g., AP News: https://apnews.com or CNN: https://www.cnn.com).

If Sanders states he is 're-evaluating' his support but does not explicitly suspend or withdraw the endorsement, it does not qualify for a Yes resolution. If Platner withdraws from the race before Sanders explicitly retracts his endorsement, this question resolves No. If the resolution window ends on 2025-11-22 at 11:59 PM ET without a qualifying retraction or alternative endorsement by Sanders, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Bernie Sanders' endorsement is the primary pillar of Platner's national legitimacy and progressive fundraising. In light of the recent severe scandals regarding racist comments and a Nazi-style tattoo, immense pressure will be placed on Sanders to distance himself from Platner. If Sanders withdraws his endorsement, Platner's campaign will lose its main source of political capital and financial momentum, making his withdrawal from the race highly probable. Conversely, if Sanders holds firm, Platner is more likely to weather the storm and stay in the race.

question: Will Consensys IPO by December 31 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ConsenSys (the parent company of MetaMask) completes an Initial Public Offering (IPO) by the listed date ET, as confirmed by official company announcements and credible news sources. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The IPO refers to the first sale of stock by the listed company to the public on any recognized stock exchange.

If ConsenSys is acquired by another company that is already public, this market will immediately resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market is a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will ConsenSys publicly file a Form S-1 or equivalent IPO registration statement with the SEC between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29?
subquestions.background_information: ConsenSys, the software developer and parent company of MetaMask, is reportedly planning an initial public offering (IPO) and has hired JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs to lead the process (Yahoo Finance, https://finance.yahoo.com). This follows favorable regulatory developments, such as the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) dropping its lawsuit against ConsenSys regarding MetaMask's staking features earlier in 2025. For a company to go public in the US, it must file a Form S-1 registration statement with the SEC. While companies can submit this confidentially at first, the SEC requires the S-1 to be filed publicly at least 15 days before the company begins its IPO roadshow. Tracking the public filing of ConsenSys's S-1 is a necessary leading indicator for whether it can execute an IPO by the end of 2025. Sources: Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com ; SEC EDGAR Company Search: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if ConsenSys (or its direct holding/parent company) publicly files a Form S-1, Form F-1, or equivalent initial public offering registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive). The resolution will be determined by searching the SEC's EDGAR database (https://www.sec.gov/edgar/searchedgar/companysearch.html). A confidential submission that has not been made publicly accessible on EDGAR does not qualify. The public filing must be visible on the SEC database before 23:59 UTC on 2025-12-29. If no such filing occurs within the specified window, the question resolves No. In the event that the SEC EDGAR database is temporarily down or inaccessible at the time of resolution, the resolution window will be extended by up to 48 hours to check for filings made before the deadline. If EDGAR is permanently decommissioned, credible reporting from major financial news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters, WSJ) confirming the public filing will be used as a fallback.
subquestions.rationale: To conduct an IPO by December 31, 2025, a company must first publicly file a registration statement with the SEC. The SEC requires this document to be public for at least 15 days before an IPO roadshow can commence. Therefore, if ConsenSys does not publicly file an S-1 by December 29, 2025, it is structurally impossible for them to complete the IPO by December 31. This subquestion acts as a decisive leading indicator for the ultimate outcome.

question: Trump declares another national emergency by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump formally declares a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) between October 1, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or the U.S. Department of the Treasury publish an official document or press release mentioning a "housing emergency" between October 2 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In September 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated that the Trump administration is considering declaring a national housing emergency in the fall to address rising housing costs (Benzinga News). As of late August, the 30-year mortgage rate was at 6.58%, exacerbating affordability issues. Furthermore, Polymarket bettors assigned a 34% probability that President Trump would declare a housing emergency in 2025, following Bessent's comments (Benzinga News). An official press release, briefing, or statement from the White House or Treasury mentioning a "housing emergency" would serve as a strong leading indicator that the administration is preparing to formally declare one under the National Emergencies Act.

Sources:
Benzinga News, Trump Administration Weighs National Housing Emergency: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/09/trump-administration-weighs-national-housing-emergency
Benzinga News, Trump Could Declare Housing Emergency In 2025?: https://www.benzinga.com/news/25/09/trump-could-declare-housing-emergency-in-2025-polymarket
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a press release, briefing transcript, official statement, or other official document containing the exact phrase "housing emergency" (case-insensitive) is published on the official White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or the U.S. Department of the Treasury website (https://home.treasury.gov) between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The publication must occur during this specific window. To determine the resolution, the official websites will be searched using their native search functions or via site-specific searches on major search engines (e.g., Google `site:whitehouse.gov "housing emergency"`). The document must be officially published by the administration; user comments, third-party content, or archived historical documents from prior administrations republished in this window do not count. The phrase may be hyphenated (e.g., "housing-emergency") but must include both words consecutively.

If no such document is published between 2025-10-02 and 2025-10-31, the question resolves No. Documents published prior to 2025-10-02 or after 2025-10-31 do not count towards a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent explicitly stated that the administration 'may declare a national housing emergency in the fall.' The publication of an official document or press release using the phrase 'housing emergency' is a highly observable intermediate step that strongly signals the administration's active preparation for a formal emergency declaration under the National Emergencies Act. If they do not start using this terminology officially in October, the likelihood of a formal declaration by the end of the year decreases significantly.

question: Will Israel strike 0 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that Israel initiates a drone, missile, or air strike between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by Israel as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, as well as strikes within the West Bank or the Gaza Strip, will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Israeli military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the Israeli government or a consensus of credible reporting.

Missiles or drones that are intercepted and surface-to-air missile strikes will not count towards the resolution of this market, regardless of whether they land on another country's territory or cause damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes directly, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Israeli ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Israel launch an aerial bomb, drone, or missile strike that impacts the territory of Yemen between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14?
subquestions.background_information:
Israel and the Houthis in Yemen have been engaged in an escalating conflict since late 2023. As of late 2025, the Houthis have launched numerous ballistic missiles and drones at Israel, and Israel has conducted multiple retaliatory airstrikes against Houthi targets in Yemen, hitting power plants, military sites, and the presidential palace (https://www.abc.net.au/news). For instance, in August 2025, Israeli airstrikes targeted Yemen's capital, Sanaa, striking an oil facility, a power plant, and a military site (https://apnews.com). The ongoing exchanges between Israel and Yemen demonstrate a high risk of continued military action. Whether Israel conducts a strike on Yemen in the final months of 2025 is a crucial indicator of ongoing military operations and directly informs the likelihood of Israel striking foreign soil in 2026.

Sources:
Australian Broadcasting Corporation - https://www.abc.net.au/news
AP News - https://apnews.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-14 and 2025-12-14 (inclusive), a consensus of credible reporting or the Israeli government officially confirms that Israeli military forces used aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) that impacted the officially acknowledged ground territory of Yemen.

Strikes where the projectile is intercepted and does not impact ground territory, or where the operation consists solely of actions such as cyberattacks, naval shelling, small arms fire, or ground incursions will not count, matching the conditions of the ultimate question.

The resolution will be determined by a consensus of credible reporting from major international news outlets, such as AP News (https://apnews.com), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), or The Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com), or official Israeli military/government statements. Delayed events or strikes that occur outside the specified resolution window (after 2025-12-14) will not count toward resolving this question as Yes.
subquestions.rationale: The ongoing retaliatory conflict between Israel and the Houthis makes Yemen a highly probable target for Israeli strikes. If Israel continues to launch strikes that impact Yemeni territory between mid-November and mid-December 2025, it strongly indicates that regional hostilities remain active and unresolved, increasing the likelihood that Israel will continue to strike foreign countries in 2026. Therefore, a 'Yes' on this subquestion would significantly lower the probability of Israel striking 0 countries in 2026.

question: 30-year mortgage rate below 6% by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the 30-Year Fixed Rate Mortgage Average in the United States falls below 6.00% at any point between September 2 and December 31, 2025. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If, for any reason, there is no data point for this market's resolution date on either of the sources listed below, information for the nearest previously available date will be used.

The primary resolution source for this market is Freddie Mac, specifically https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms. The data that will be looked at is the "30Y FRM" as indicated on the graph titled "Primary Mortgage Market Survey®". If the resolution source is unavailable, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US will be looked at instead. If both sources are unavailable, other credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the 10-Year U.S. Treasury yield fall below 3.60% at any point between September 3 and October 3, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The 30-year fixed-rate mortgage (FRM) is closely tied to the 10-Year U.S. Treasury yield. Lenders use the 10-year Treasury as a primary benchmark to price long-term fixed-rate mortgages, typically maintaining a spread of roughly 150 to 300 basis points over the Treasury yield. As of late August 2025, Freddie Mac reported the average 30-year FRM at a 10-month low of 6.56%. For the 30-year mortgage rate to eventually drop below the ultimate question's threshold of 6.00% by December 31, 2025, the 10-Year Treasury yield will likely need to compress further, approaching or breaking the 3.60% mark during the early fall. Monitoring whether the 10-Year yield falls below this threshold in September or early October provides a strong, distinct early indicator for the trajectory of mortgage rates through the rest of the year.

Sources:
Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) 10-Year Treasury Yield: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey: https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms
U.S. Department of the Treasury Yield Curve Data: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if the daily Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 10-Year Constant Maturity (quoted on an investment basis) is recorded at strictly less than 3.60% (i.e., 3.59% or lower) for any observation date between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 (inclusive). 

The primary resolution source for this market is the Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) database, specifically the 'DGS10' series, available at https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10. 

If FRED data is unavailable, the fallback resolution source will be the official Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates published directly by the U.S. Department of the Treasury at https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025. 

Resolution will be based on the first published data for the specified dates. Any subsequent ex-post revisions to the data made after October 10, 2025, will not affect the resolution of this market. If the yield never drops below 3.60% within the specified window, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Because the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage average is priced primarily at a premium over the 10-Year U.S. Treasury yield, analyzing the movement of the 10-Year Treasury is standard practice for forecasting mortgage rate trends. A drop in the Treasury yield below 3.60% in the near term would confirm significant downward momentum in long-term borrowing costs, serving as a critical crux for forecasters anticipating whether mortgage rates can clear the 6.00% hurdle by year-end.

question: Will Russia capture Bilytske by February 28, 2026?

If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. “Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine” will not qualify.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. subquestions.question: Will the ISW map show Russian control or advance at 48.354° N, 37.203° E in Rodynske by February 14, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:

Assessing whether Russia can capture a central coordinate in Rodynske (48.354° N, 37.203° E) by mid-February 2026 provides a highly informative early indicator of whether they will have the momentum and proximity to reach Bilytske by the end of February. As of January 15, 2026, the area remains under Ukrainian control.

DeepStateMap: https://deepstatemap.live/
The Straits Times - Russia says its forces advance in embattled Ukrainian city of Pokrovsk: https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/russia-says-its-forces-advance-in-embattled-ukrainian-city-of-pokrovsk
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if, at any point between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-14 (inclusive), the ISW interactive map of the Russian Offensive Campaign (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) shades the coordinate 48.354° N, 37.203° E (located in Rodynske, Donetsk Oblast) with colors indicating 'Assessed Russian Control', 'Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine', or 'Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours'.

1. The specified shading covering the coordinate must occur between 2026-01-15 and 2026-02-14 (23:59 UTC).

If the ISW map is temporarily down, resolution will be delayed until it returns. If the ISW map is rendered permanently unavailable, DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) will serve as the fallback primary source; on DeepStateMap, the coordinate must be covered by the red or dark-red shading denoting Russian control. If both maps are permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting will be used. If the location is not captured according to these criteria by the end of the day on 2026-02-14, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Rodynske lies directly on the axis of advance between the heavily contested Pokrovsk area and the ultimate target of Bilytske. If Russian forces fail to secure this intermediate waypoint by mid-February, their chances of traversing the remaining distance to capture the specific building in Bilytske by February 28 drop significantly. question: Trump enacts a de minimis crypto tax exemption before 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to establish a de minimis tax exemption on cryptocurrency transactions by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If the tax exemption only applies for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate pass a bill that includes a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions before December 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Currently, the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) treats cryptocurrency as property, meaning that every transaction triggers a taxable event for capital gains, regardless of the transaction's size. There is currently no de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions in the U.S. (Decrypt, https://decrypt.co). Over 70 cryptocurrency organizations sent a letter to President Donald Trump on November 20, 2025, urging regulatory clarity, including a de minimis tax exemption for digital asset transactions up to $600 (CoinCentral, https://coincentral.com). Concurrently, crypto industry executives launched a coordinated campaign and held a private dinner with key members of the House Ways and Means Committee to build legislative support for this exemption (TechStory, https://techstory.in). U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis has also previously proposed legislation to exempt crypto transactions under $300 from capital gains taxes (AMBCrypto, https://ambcrypto.com). Passing a bill in either chamber of Congress would be a major milestone toward enacting such a tax exemption into law.

Sources:
Decrypt: https://decrypt.co
CoinCentral: https://coincentral.com
TechStory: https://techstory.in
AMBCrypto: https://ambcrypto.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29 (inclusive), the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate passes a piece of legislation (e.g., a standalone bill or an amendment included in a broader passed bill) that contains a provision establishing a de minimis tax exemption for cryptocurrency transactions.

The legislation must stipulate that individual cryptocurrency transactions under a certain fiat value threshold (e.g., $200, $300, $600) are exempt from capital gains taxation for U.S. taxpayers. 

'Passes' means the bill must be approved by a successful floor vote in at least one full chamber of Congress (the House or the Senate). Approval by a congressional committee alone does not suffice unless the bill subsequently passes the full chamber. 

Resolution will be based on official legislative records from Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov) or the official websites of the U.S. House (https://www.house.gov) or U.S. Senate (https://www.senate.gov). A consensus of credible reporting from major news outlets (e.g., Bloomberg, Reuters) may be used to confirm the contents of the passed bill.

If neither chamber passes such a bill between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-29, the question resolves No. Delayed events extending past the resolution window will not be considered, and the question will resolve No.

question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.
