On October 8, 2025, Russian Deputy FM Sergei Ryabkov stated that the momentum for a settlement has 'run out' following a US-Russia meeting in Alaska, claiming the US is uninterested in strategic dialogue (https://apa.az/en). Concurrently, the European Parliament passed a resolution urging member states to lift restrictions on Ukraine's use of Western weapons inside Russia (https://www.europarl.europa.eu/). However, reports also suggest a potential US strategic shift, with recent restrictions on military aid to Baltic countries and statements suggesting a ceasefire might not be a prerequisite for permanent peace (https://in-cyprus.philenews.com/). An announcement of direct peace or ceasefire negotiations would represent a major policy shift and serve as a crucial early indicator for a potential buffer zone agreement by the end of 2025.

European Parliament: https://www.europarl.europa.eu/

The confirmation must come via an official statement, press release, or verified social media account from a high-ranking official (e.g., President, Foreign Minister, official spokesperson). 'Direct negotiations' means meetings (in-person or virtual) involving representatives from both governments. Third-party mediated proximity talks qualify if both Russian and Ukrainian delegations are explicitly participating in a shared negotiation framework regarding these topics.

Negotiations exclusively limited to prisoner exchanges, the return of bodies, or isolated humanitarian corridors without broader ceasefire or settlement objectives do NOT qualify.

Resolution will rely on official government websites (e.g., http://kremlin.ru, https://president.gov.ua) or reporting from credible international media outlets (e.g., Reuters: https://www.reuters.com, Associated Press: https://apnews.com). If no such announcement or confirmation is made within the specified window between 2025-10-13 and 2025-11-12, the question resolves No.

If neither Russia nor Ukraine announces formal negotiations regarding a ceasefire or peace settlement by mid-November, the timeline to negotiate, draft, and finalize a complex buffer zone agreement by December 31 becomes extremely constrained. Conversely, if negotiations are announced, it serves as a strong positive indicator for the ultimate question's affirmative resolution.

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield dip below 3.9% in 2025?

Expectations for a December 2025 rate cut have been volatile, with the probability of a 25 basis point reduction dropping to approximately 50% following inflation uncertainty and cautious remarks from Fed officials. A significant drop in the 2-year yield below 3.50% would indicate that market participants are pricing in more aggressive rate cuts by the Federal Reserve ahead of their December 17-18 FOMC meeting. Downward pressure on the short end of the yield curve is typically correlated with declines in the 10-year yield, making it a valuable leading indicator for whether the 10-year yield will approach the 3.9% threshold in 2025. Sources: U.S. Department of the Treasury Yield Curve Data (https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025), CME FedWatch Tool (https://www.cmegroup.com/markets/interest-rates/cme-fedwatch-tool.html), Federal Reserve Economic Data FRED 2-Year Treasury Constant Maturity Rate (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rate for the '2 Yr' maturity is lower than 3.50% (i.e., 3.49% or lower) for any trading date between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-17 (inclusive). Otherwise, it resolves No. The primary resolution source will be the official U.S. Department of the Treasury website, specifically the data listed under 'Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates' for the column '2 Yr' (https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025). If the Treasury website is permanently unavailable or fails to publish data for the specified window by December 31, 2025, alternative reliable financial data providers such as FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2) will be used to determine the official 2-year par yield for those dates. Delayed publication of the rates due to holidays or government shutdowns will not prevent a Yes resolution as long as the official rate assigned to a valid trading date within the window is below 3.50%.
subquestions.rationale: The 2-year Treasury yield is an effective gauge for the market's near-term monetary policy expectations, specifically regarding the Federal Reserve's path for rate cuts. If the 2-year yield breaks below 3.50% ahead of the December FOMC meeting, it demonstrates a strong shift toward pricing in lower interest rates. Because the 10-year yield and the 2-year yield are heavily correlated, tracking this shorter-duration instrument acts as an excellent early indicator for whether the broader rate environment is softening enough to push the 10-year yield below the 3.9% ultimate threshold.

subquestions.question: Will Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook commence a formal leave of absence from her duties between December 9, 2025, and January 8, 2026?

Following the attempt to remove her, the administration explicitly pressured Cook to step aside temporarily; White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett stated that Cook should 'go on leave' until the legal and factual disputes over the accusations are resolved (https://finance.yahoo.com/). Federal Reserve Press Releases: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The leave must be explicitly described as a 'leave of absence', 'administrative leave', or a complete temporary recusal from her official duties at the Federal Reserve. Routine vacations, sick leave, or exclusion from specific meetings that do not constitute a formal leave status will not qualify.

If Lisa Cook permanently resigns or is legally permanently removed during this window without first taking a leave of absence, this question resolves No, as that would trigger the ultimate question directly rather than this specific interim step. Delayed events announced to take effect after the resolution window will not qualify. The primary resolution source will be Federal Reserve press releases (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases.htm) alongside major financial news reporting (e.g., https://www.bloomberg.com/ or https://www.reuters.com/).
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question explicitly states that 'temporary absences... will not qualify' for its resolution. However, a formal leave of absence is exactly what the White House publicly pushed for as an interim step while the dispute over her attempted firing is litigated. question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Russia initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on the sovereign territory of any NATO member state or on any official embassy or consulate of a NATO member state between October 30 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by Russian military forces that impact the ground territory of a NATO member state or an official embassy/consulate of a NATO member (e.g., if a weapons depot on NATO territory is hit by a Russian missile, this market will resolve to "Yes").

Missiles or drones that are intercepted (i.e., do not impact) and surface-to-air missile launches will not be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether debris falls on NATO territory or causes damage.

Actions such as artillery fire, small arms fire, FPV or ATGM strikes conducted directly by ground operatives, ground incursions, naval shelling, cyberattacks, or other operations conducted by Russian ground operatives will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will any NATO member state officially confirm a violation of its sovereign airspace by a Russian-launched drone or missile between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Recent Russian aerial bombardments of Ukraine have increasingly approached or crossed into NATO airspace, testing the alliance's air defense readiness. On September 20, 2025, Polish and other NATO jets scrambled to intercept a large Russian strike on Ukraine. Reports indicated that Russian drones had violated the airspace of Poland and Romania, prompting NATO to intercept and shoot down several drones over Poland. The Russian military has launched massive, frequent barrages, such as over 300 drones and 37 missiles on October 17, 2025, and 705 targets on October 30, 2025. These large-scale attacks increase the risk of stray drones or missiles crossing into neighboring countries. Monitoring whether airspace violations continue provides a critical early indicator of the likelihood that a projectile might ultimately impact NATO territory, accidentally or intentionally. Sources: Euronews: Russia batters Ukraine's energy grid with drone and missile strikes - https://www.euronews.com/ Ukrainian National News Agency: Ukraine’s air defenses down 623 drones and missiles out of 705 launched - https://www.ukrinform.net/ NATO Press Releases - https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/press_releases.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the government, defense ministry, or military command of any NATO member state officially confirms that a Russian-launched drone or missile entered its sovereign airspace between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). The official statement must explicitly identify the object as an unmanned aerial vehicle (drone) or missile (including cruise or ballistic missiles, or loitering munitions) and attribute its launch to Russian forces. The airspace violation must have occurred within the specified time window (2025-10-31 to 2025-11-30). If the airspace violation occurs within this window but the official confirmation is delayed, it still counts toward a Yes resolution, provided the announcement is made before the end of the ultimate question's resolution date. If an event occurs but remains unconfirmed by official channels before the resolution window closes, it does not count. Events involving manned aircraft, helicopters, or naval vessels do not qualify. The projectile does not need to impact the ground; merely crossing into sovereign airspace (as confirmed by the state) is sufficient. If no such official confirmation is made regarding an incident occurring between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, this question resolves No. Resolution will be based on official government or military press releases, such as the Polish Armed Forces (https://www.wojsko-polskie.pl/), the Romanian Ministry of National Defence (https://english.mapn.ro/), or official NATO press releases (https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/press_releases.htm), and must be corroborated by major credible news outlets like Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) or AP News (https://apnews.com).
subquestions.rationale: Airspace violations by Russian drones or missiles are a direct precursor to potential strikes or impacts on NATO territory. The ultimate question asks whether a Russian projectile will 'impact' NATO ground. By tracking whether projectiles are crossing the border (even if intercepted or returning to Ukraine) in the preceding month, forecasters can better assess the frequency of border friction. A high rate of confirmed airspace violations suggests an elevated risk that a drone or missile will eventually crash or strike NATO territory, whereas a lack of violations indicates successful de-escalation or improved precision by Russian forces.

Launch providers typically announce a targeted launch month or specific launch date several weeks prior to liftoff to coordinate with payload customers, range authorities, and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). If no such announcement is active or made between 2025-12-12 and 2026-01-11, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: If New Glenn Flight 3 is going to launch by January 31, 2026, Blue Origin will almost certainly have announced a targeted launch date or month by January 11, 2026 (20 days prior to the ultimate question's deadline). question: Will Trump send the national guard to Boston by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump or his administration takes a formal action or makes an official announcement directing the deployment of National Guard troops to the listed city by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No.”
A qualifying announcement or action will count, regardless of if/when the deployment actually occurs, or if the deployment is delayed, suspended, or subsequently blocked by judicial or other actions.

Qualifying actions include but are not limited to:
- A Presidential action (e.g., Executive Order, Presidential Memorandum) that directs or announces National Guard deployment to the listed city.
- An official White House/DoD/National Guard Bureau press release, fact sheet, or order explicitly stating that National Guard troops will be deployed to the listed city.
- A Secretary of Defense or NGB directive/order that calls up or assigns National Guard forces to the listed city, including under Title 32 (state control with federal funding) or Title 10 (federalized).
- An official federal announcement that specific state Guard units (including the listed city National Guard or out-of-state Guard) are being sent to the listed city.

Non-qualifying actions include:
- Informal announcements/social media posts which do not constitute a formal policy announcement 
- Ambiguous remarks, “we’re considering it,” broad statements like “ready to go anywhere,” or contingent plans without a clear directive to the listed city.
- Generic posture changes (e.g., standing up quick-reaction forces “nationwide”) that do not explicitly name the listed city as a deployment location.
- A state-only activation by the listed city's state Governor without any official Trump administration action or announcement about sending the Guard to the listed city.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

Mayor Michelle Wu of Boston has already warned that her city is preparing for federal deployments (https://www.bostonglobe.com). subquestions.resolution_criteria:

- An official White House, Department of Defense (DoD), or National Guard Bureau (NGB) press release or order explicitly stating that troops will be deployed to Chicago.

- Ambiguous remarks such as "we are considering Chicago" or "ready to go anywhere."

subquestions.rationale: Chicago is explicitly mentioned as the most likely immediate target for the Trump administration's expanded National Guard deployment plans. If the administration follows through and formally deploys troops to Chicago by early November, it proves their willingness and legal capability to act on these threats against Democratic-led cities, significantly raising the probability that Boston will also see a deployment by December 31. Conversely, if no deployment occurs in Chicago, it signals a lack of momentum, strategic shift, or legal hurdles that make a subsequent deployment to Boston highly unlikely within the year.

subquestions.rationale: In a fragmented 15-candidate primary where several candidates share similar platforms and demographic bases, a major newspaper endorsement is one of the most reliable leading indicators of a candidate's mainstream appeal and organizational strength. Previous seasons have seen a sharp, consistent decline in audience ratings: Season 1 had an 88% audience score, Season 2 dropped to 54%, and Season 3 plummeted to 20%. Given the immense fan backlash to the casting change and noted departures from the source material, the audience reception is highly anticipated.

Sources:
CBR: https://www.cbr.com/witcher-season-4-rotten-tomatoes-score-henry-cavill-legacy/
ScreenRant: https://screenrant.com/witcher-season-4-rotten-tomatoes-debut-record/

If the score is 26% or higher, or if the score has not yet been established (e.g., displaying 'No Score Yet' due to insufficient reviews), the question resolves No. If the Rotten Tomatoes website is temporarily or permanently unavailable at the resolution time, the most recent archived capture on the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org/) recorded between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-25 will be used to determine the score.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks whether the Tomatometer (critics' score) will end up between 45% and 59% by the end of 2025. Currently at 40%, the score could rise or fall as more reviews come in. The audience score (Popcornmeter) provides a separate, early observable indicator of the season's overall reception. If the audience score is 25% or lower—reflecting the deep dissatisfaction seen in Season 3's 20% score and the controversy over Henry Cavill's departure—it signals universally poor reception. Such overwhelmingly negative sentiment often correlates with a stalled or falling critics' score, making it less likely that the Tomatometer will climb into the 45-59% bracket. Conversely, a higher-than-expected audience score could indicate that the season resonates well enough to eventually sway late-arriving critical reviews upwards.

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Southern Command, U.S. Coast Guard, or a consensus of credible media reporting confirms that U.S. military or Coast Guard forces have used kinetic force (e.g., missiles, gunfire) to destroy or sink at least one vessel suspected of drug smuggling or other illicit activity in the Caribbean Sea or waters near Venezuela. The strike must be carried out by U.S. military or Coast Guard forces. Vessels officially belonging to the Venezuelan military are excluded from this question (as a strike on a Venezuelan military vessel would trigger the ultimate question directly). If the vessel struck is a civilian, unidentified, or alleged cartel drug-smuggling vessel, it counts for this question. Information will be verified via official press releases from the U.S. Southern Command (https://www.southcom.mil/), the U.S. Department of Defense (https://www.defense.gov/), or major news outlets (e.g., Reuters https://www.reuters.com, AP News https://apnews.com). subquestions.rationale: The continuation of U.S. kinetic strikes on suspected drug vessels in the Caribbean is a key crux for whether a direct military engagement with Venezuela will occur. These strikes are the primary aggressive action currently being taken by U.S. forces in the theater. If the strikes continue, they maintain a high operational tempo and increase the risk of miscalculation, accidental targeting of Venezuelan assets, or a retaliatory response from Venezuela. If the strikes cease, it may indicate a U.S. policy shift toward de-escalation, significantly lowering the probability of a direct US-Venezuela military engagement.

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The 15 Executive Departments are: Agriculture, Commerce, Defense, Education, Energy, Health and Human Services, Homeland Security, Housing and Urban Development, Interior, Justice, Labor, State, Transportation, Treasury, and Veterans Affairs. 

'Leaves their position' means the individual permanently vacates the role, whether by resignation, termination, retirement, or transfer/promotion to another position. Temporary absences or administrative leaves do not count if the individual formally retains the title. Individuals serving in an 'acting' capacity do not count; the departing individual must have been formally confirmed by the Senate and actively serving in the position. 

Announcements of future departures do not trigger a 'Yes' resolution unless the effective date of the departure falls strictly within the resolution window (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01). If a departure is announced within this window but the effective date is after 2025-10-01, it will not count. If a qualifying event is delayed and occurs after the resolution window, the question resolves No.

In the absence of an official announcement, a consensus of credible reporting from major outlets (e.g., Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/), AP News (https://apnews.com/)) confirming the departure will be used.
subquestions.rationale: Tracking turnover at the Deputy Secretary level provides a reliable leading indicator of cabinet-level instability. High turnover among these immediate subordinates often precedes or reflects the same ideological purges and administrative chaos that could lead a Cabinet Secretary to resign or be fired. Since a cabinet departure is a rarer, more significant event, observing the slightly more common but highly prominent Deputy Secretary departures allows forecasters to update their probabilities on the ultimate outcome regarding Cabinet turnover.

For example, Sergio Gor's transition from the White House Presidential Personnel Office to Ambassador to India was followed by Dan Scavino taking over the role in October 2025 to oversee the administration's workforce (https://nypost.com/2025/10/12/trump-announces-dan-scavino-as-new-head-of-white-house-presidential-personnel-office/). question: Will 7-9 SpaceX Starship launches successfully reach Space in 2025?
description:

A successful launch is defined as the Starship taking off from its launchpad and reaching a minimum altitude of 62 miles above sea level. Any subsequent anomaly (e.g. an explosion) after the vehicle reaches 62 miles will have no bearing on the outcome.

The primary resolution source for this market will be SpaceX’s official video feed of the launches (e.g. via SpaceX YouTube Channel), as well as secondary video feeds or written reports if necessary. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will SpaceX fully stack a Starship vehicle on the Orbital Launch Mount at Starbase between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late August 2025, SpaceX successfully completed Starship's 10th flight, which marked the 4th test flight of 2025. To achieve the ultimate question's threshold of 7 to 9 successful space-reaching flights in 2025, SpaceX needs to execute at least 3 more successful flights in the final four months of the year (September through December). Elon Musk recently outlined an accelerated timeline, aiming for a flight cadence of once every 3 to 4 weeks. Achieving such a high cadence requires extremely rapid turnaround of the launch infrastructure. 

Before any Starship can fly or complete final pre-launch testing like a Wet Dress Rehearsal (WDR), SpaceX must "fully stack" the vehicle—mating the Starship upper stage atop the Super Heavy booster on the Orbital Launch Mount (OLM). Because Flight 10 occupied the OLM until late August, preparing the pad and stacking the next vehicle (Flight 11) is the immediate operational bottleneck. If SpaceX fails to stack a vehicle by October 1, it provides strong evidence that the 3-4 week launch cadence is slipping, making it highly unlikely they will reach the 7-flight threshold by December 31.

Sources:
Yahoo News - SpaceX Starship flight 10 coverage: https://www.yahoo.com/news
SpaceX Official Website: https://www.spacex.com
NASASpaceflight: https://www.nasaspaceflight.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if SpaceX fully stacks a Starship vehicle on the Orbital Launch Mount (OLM) at Starbase, Texas, at any time between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). 

"Fully stacks" is specifically defined as the physical placement and mating of a Starship upper stage atop a Super Heavy booster while resting on the OLM. The vehicle does not need to launch, undergo a static fire, or complete a Wet Dress Rehearsal (WDR) during this window; visual confirmation of a complete stack is sufficient. If the vehicle is fully stacked and subsequently unstacked within the time window, the condition is still met and the question resolves Yes. 

If no full stacking event occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, the question resolves No. Delayed events extending past 2025-10-01 will not count toward a Yes resolution.

Resolution will primarily rely on visual confirmation and reporting from NASASpaceflight's continuous Starbase coverage (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com) or official communications, videos, and images released by SpaceX (https://www.spacex.com or https://x.com/SpaceX). In the event of minor timeline discrepancies, the earliest publicly verifiable timestamp of the completed stacking operation will be used.
subquestions.rationale: SpaceX must maintain a launch cadence of roughly one flight per month to achieve 7-9 total successful flights in 2025. Stacking the vehicle on the launch mount is a strictly necessary precursor to any launch or final testing. If they cannot reach this milestone within one month of the previous launch, it is an early, highly informative indicator that their turnaround time is too slow to meet the end-of-year target.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce or release a standalone web browser between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?

On September 3, 2025, a federal judge ruled that Google does not have to sell Chrome to resolve its monopoly case, instead ordering data sharing with rivals. Given this ruling, Alphabet is highly unlikely to voluntarily sell its dominant browser to a major AI competitor. Consequently, OpenAI may accelerate the launch of its own proprietary browser. Tracking whether OpenAI announces its own browser provides a strong early indicator: launching an independent browser would signal a pivot away from acquiring Chrome, directly informing the ultimate question's outcome.

subquestions.rationale: If OpenAI commits to its own standalone AI browser by officially announcing or releasing it in October 2025, it strongly indicates a strategic decision to build rather than buy. question: U.S. x Russia Nuclear deal by December 31?
description:

Only agreements that are publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia will qualify. The agreement must pertain to nuclear arms control or limitation—such as a treaty, framework, or memorandum—addressing matters including (but not limited to) nuclear warheads, delivery systems, verification mechanisms, or strategic stability.

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the United States and the Russian Federation hold formal bilateral talks on nuclear arms control between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: On September 22, 2025, Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed a one-year unilateral extension of the New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (New START) until February 2026, provided the U.S. agrees to similar limits. The treaty currently caps U.S. and Russian strategic arsenals at 1,550 deployed warheads and 700 launchers. Following this, U.S. President Donald Trump indicated that the proposal sounded like a good idea. However, formalizing any such agreement or a broader arms control framework requires official bilateral negotiations. Security experts like Daryl G. Kimball of the Arms Control Association have emphasized that to finalize an extension, the Kremlin and the White House must formalize the arrangement and begin immediate negotiations. Because the ultimate question seeks a finalized agreement by December 31, 2025, tracking whether direct, formal talks actually commence in November is a critical early indicator. Sources: 1. TASS (https://tass.com) 2. Firstpost (https://www.firstpost.com) 3. Arms Control Association (https://www.armscontrol.org/factsheets/NewSTART)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if the United States and the Russian Federation hold at least one formal, bilateral, government-level meeting or negotiation session explicitly addressing nuclear arms control (including a potential extension of New START) between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive). The meeting must involve official representatives from both governments (e.g., from the U.S. State Department and the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs) and can take place either in person or virtually. Resolution will be determined by official confirmation from either the U.S. government (https://www.state.gov or https://www.whitehouse.gov) or the Russian Federation (http://en.kremlin.ru or https://mid.ru/en/) explicitly acknowledging that a bilateral meeting or negotiation on nuclear arms control took place during this window. Media reports from major credible news outlets (such as Reuters at https://www.reuters.com or AP News at https://apnews.com) confirming the meeting occurred between the specified dates can also trigger a 'Yes' resolution if official press releases are unavailable. If the event is postponed beyond the resolution window, or if no such talks are held and confirmed to have occurred between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Reaching a finalized nuclear arms agreement by December 31, 2025, practically necessitates formal diplomatic talks beforehand. If the U.S. and Russia do not engage in dedicated bilateral arms control talks by November 30, it becomes highly improbable that a finalized agreement will be signed and announced before the end of the year, making this a strong early indicator.

question: Will Russia enter Borova by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Borova (49.37457173620971, 37.62233412539868) by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the ISW map indicate Russian control or advance at coordinate 49.380, 37.695 (approximately 5km east of Borova) between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-20?
subquestions.background_information:
Borova is a strategically important settlement in the Kharkiv region, situated on the eastern bank of the Oskil river. Throughout late 2024 and 2025, Russian forces have sustained localized offensive operations along the Kupiansk-Svatove-Kreminna line, aiming to push toward the Oskil river to establish a natural defensive barrier and disrupt Ukrainian logistics. Russian tactics in this sector have heavily relied on "a thousand cuts," deploying small infantry groups of four to six soldiers to infiltrate Ukrainian lines rather than executing massive mechanized breakthroughs. The coordinate 49.380, 37.695 corresponds to a location in the settlement of Shyikivka, approximately 5.3 kilometers almost directly east of Borova's center (49.374, 37.622). To enter Borova from the main eastern axis of advance, Russian forces would necessarily have to push through or immediately bypass this area. Establishing control over this 5km marker would place Russian forces on the immediate outskirts of Borova.

Institute for the Study of War (ISW) Interactive Map - https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
CNN (Reporting on Russian incremental tactics) - https://edition.cnn.com/
DeepStateMap - https://deepstatemap.live/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any time between the start_date of 2025-11-28 and the end_date of 2025-12-20 (inclusive), the specific coordinate 49.380, 37.695 is shaded under any of the following layers on the official ISW Ukraine map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375): "Assessed Russian Control", "Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine", "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", or "Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours". 

For a change on the ISW map to qualify, the relevant shading indicating Russian control or advance over the exact coordinate must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle to rule out temporary mapping errors or glitches. Once this qualifying condition is met within the specified time window (2025-11-28 to 2025-12-20), any subsequent loss of control of the coordinate will not affect the "Yes" resolution.

If the ISW map is rendered permanently unavailable during the resolution window, DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) will be used as the fallback source. In this fallback scenario, the question resolves Yes if the coordinate 49.380, 37.695 falls under Russian control (shaded red) or the "gray zone" (contested territory) on DeepStateMap between 2025-11-28 and 2025-12-20. If neither map is available, the question will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting confirming Russian presence at the coordinate during the timeframe.
subquestions.rationale: Capturing or entering Borova by December 31, 2025, requires Russian forces to cross the remaining kilometers east of the settlement. The selected coordinate is exactly ~5 km east of Borova, serving as a direct gatekeeper. If Russian forces cannot reach this 5-kilometer threshold by December 20, their momentum and the tactical timeline strongly suggest they will lack the capacity to conquer the remaining fortified distance and enter Borova by December 31. Conversely, if they hit this milestone, an attack on Borova itself becomes highly probable, making this a perfect early-warning crux.

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will a formal ceasefire or cessation of hostilities agreement between Ukraine and the Russian Federation be publicly announced between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of late 2025, the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine has seen shifting frontlines and renewed diplomatic pressure for a resolution. Reports indicate that Ukraine's Western allies have been discussing peace plans that might involve freezing the conflict along current battle lines, effectively leaving Russia with de facto control of occupied territories like Crimea, Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia (https://www.dw.com). However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has consistently maintained that Ukraine will not formally cede territory it currently holds, though international mediators have suggested negotiations could lead to de facto recognition of Russian control over certain areas (https://www.firstpost.com). Any comprehensive peace agreement in 2025 that includes formal or de facto territorial concessions by Ukraine would likely necessitate an immediate cessation of hostilities to allow for final diplomatic negotiations and border demarcations. A formal ceasefire is a standard precursor to such treaties. If a ceasefire is not reached by the end of October 2025, the timeline to negotiate and finalize a complex territorial agreement by the end of the year becomes exceedingly tight.

Sources:
Deutsche Welle: https://www.dw.com
Firstpost: https://www.firstpost.com
Daily Sabah: https://www.dailysabah.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a mutual agreement for a ceasefire, armistice, or generalized cessation of hostilities between the armed forces of Ukraine and the Russian Federation is officially and publicly announced between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The agreement must apply to the majority of the active frontline between the two nations. Localized truces (e.g., temporary humanitarian corridors, localized pauses for prisoner swaps, or holiday truces lasting less than 7 days) do not count.

The public announcement must occur within the resolution window (between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31), regardless of when the ceasefire is actually scheduled to take effect on the battlefield.

A unilateral ceasefire declaration by one party that is not explicitly accepted or adhered to by the other does not qualify.

Resolution will be based on official announcements from the Office of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en) or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation (https://mid.ru/en/). In the absence of direct official statements, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting from major international news agencies (e.g., Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com)) confirming that a mutual ceasefire agreement has been reached will suffice for a Yes resolution. If no such agreement is announced by 23:59 UTC on 2025-10-31, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A deal involving the cession of currently held territory requires significant diplomatic negotiation, which historically occurs after or alongside a formal ceasefire. If a ceasefire is established by late October, it strongly indicates that serious, substantive negotiations (which could include territorial concessions) are underway, significantly raising the probability of a final agreement by December 31, 2025. Conversely, if fighting continues uninterrupted through October, the remaining two months of the year are highly unlikely to be sufficient to negotiate and conclude a major territorial concession agreement.

question: Will 2025 be the second hottest year on record?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the data for the Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index for 2025 shows the second greatest increase of any previously recorded year when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

An anomaly which is the second greatest of any previously recorded year for 2025 is necessary and sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes" immediately once the data becomes available, regardless of whether the figure for 2024 and/or 2025 is later revised.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the figure found in the table titled "Land-Ocean Temperature Index (C)" under the column "No_Smoothing" in the row "2025" (https://data.giss.nasa.gov/gistemp/graphs/graph_data/Global_Mean_Estimates_based_on_Land_and_Ocean_Data/graph.txt). If NASA's "Global Temperature Index" is rendered permanently unavailable, other information from NASA may be used. If no information for 2025 is provided by NASA by March 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) officially report that 2025 was the second-warmest year on record globally by January 11, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) tracks global surface air temperatures using the ERA5 dataset. According to news reports in December 2025, C3S indicated that the global average temperature anomaly for January to November 2025 tied with 2023 as the second-warmest on record, making 2025 virtually certain to finish as either the second- or third-hottest year globally, behind 2024. C3S typically releases its annual Global Climate Highlights report detailing the full year's rankings in the first or second week of January (often around January 8-10). Because NASA's GISTEMP dataset (the resolution source for the ultimate question) and the C3S dataset usually closely agree on global temperature rankings, the C3S announcement serves as a highly informative early indicator for the NASA record.

Sources:
Copernicus Press Releases: https://climate.copernicus.eu/news-and-media/press-releases
Copernicus Climate Bulletins: https://climate.copernicus.eu/climate-bulletins
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) officially publishes its annual global climate summary for 2025 (such as the "Global Climate Highlights 2025" or an equivalent press release) between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11 (inclusive), and the publication explicitly states that the entire year 2025 was the second-warmest (or second-hottest) year on record globally, or tied for second-warmest.

This question resolves "No" if C3S publishes the aforementioned summary between 2025-12-30 and 2026-01-11 and explicitly ranks 2025 as the third-warmest year on record globally, or any other rank (e.g., first, fourth) other than second (or tied for second). It also resolves "No" if C3S does not publish its annual summary for 2025 by 2026-01-11 at 23:59 UTC.

The primary resolution source will be the official announcements, press releases, and reports published on the Copernicus Climate Change Service website (https://climate.copernicus.eu/news-and-media/press-releases).
subquestions.rationale: C3S typically publishes its annual global temperature report a few days before NASA releases the GISTEMP dataset. Since both datasets track the same global climate phenomena closely, knowing whether C3S ranks 2025 as the second-warmest year serves as a highly accurate and timely crux to forecast the outcome of the ultimate question.

question: Will Trump talk to Nicolás Maduro by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if President of Venezuela Nicolás Maduro talks with Donald Trump between October 15 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

A talk is defined as any interaction between the listed individual and Donald Trump, occurring either in person or through verbal communication by phone or video call.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. or Venezuelan government officially confirm direct diplomatic talks between the two nations between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-01?
subquestions.background_information:
Tensions between the United States and Venezuela have escalated, with the U.S. launching military strikes in the Caribbean against alleged drug-smuggling vessels linked to Venezuelan criminal networks. During an October 17, 2025, press conference, U.S. President Donald Trump claimed that Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro 'has offered everything' to avoid conflict, hinting at possible backchannel communications and significant economic concessions (https://www.thedailybeast.com/). Despite this, official diplomatic channels remain minimal, and Venezuelan Vice President Delcy Rodríguez has previously denied reports of internal negotiations (https://www.skynews.com.au/). Meanwhile, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has expressed concern over the military operations and offered his diplomatic engagement to prevent conflict in the region (https://apnews.com/). An official confirmation of lower-level diplomatic talks would be a strong indicator that a direct conversation between Trump and Maduro is being organized to formalize these concessions or reach a truce.

Sources:
The Daily Beast: https://www.thedailybeast.com/
Sky News Australia: https://www.skynews.com.au/
AP News: https://apnews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-01 at 11:59 PM ET (inclusive), either the United States government (e.g., the White House, U.S. Department of State) or the Venezuelan government (e.g., the Presidency, Ministry of Foreign Affairs) officially announces or confirms that direct diplomatic talks, negotiations, or official meetings have occurred, are occurring, or are scheduled between representatives of the two governments.

To count toward resolution, the confirmation must be made through an official government press release, a public statement by a cabinet-level official, or via verified official social media accounts. The talks must involve direct interaction between U.S. and Venezuelan officials. 

Resolution will be based on official government sources such as the U.S. State Department press releases (https://www.state.gov/press-releases/) or the White House briefing room (https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/), as well as credible media reporting (e.g., AP News (https://apnews.com/), Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/)) verifying the official confirmation. If no such official confirmation occurs within the specified window between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: If Trump and Maduro are to speak directly by the end of the year, it is highly likely that their administrations will first publicly acknowledge lower-level diplomatic talks or negotiations to set the stage and conditions for the leaders' call. Confirming these preliminary discussions serves as a strong leading indicator for the ultimate question.

question: Trump invokes War Powers against Iran by March 31, 2026?
description:

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The market will resolve based on the listed date of the report. This market may stay open until 10 days after the listed date (ET) to allow for a qualifying report to be published.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be the White House, the Congressional Record, and the NYU Law War Powers Resolution Reporting Project; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Senate hold a roll call vote on a War Powers Resolution regarding Iran between February 13, 2026, and February 28, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
In early 2026, the U.S. Senate narrowly failed to pass a War Powers Resolution aimed at limiting President Trump's military actions in Venezuela. Following this, Democrats signaled their intent to introduce a series of similar resolutions targeting other countries where the President has threatened military action, including Iran. A bipartisan Iran War Powers Resolution sponsored by Senators Tim Kaine and Rand Paul has been highlighted by advocacy groups as a priority. Concurrently, reports indicate the Trump administration has weighed military strikes against Iran, with U.S. naval assets moving toward the region, although immediate action was reportedly delayed. A Senate vote on an Iran-focused resolution would reflect escalating congressional concern over imminent hostilities.

Sources:
Washington Examiner - Democrats ready war powers blitz to exploit a Trump 'vulnerability': https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/campaigns/democrats-ready-war-powers-blitz-to-exploit-a-trump-vulnerability
People's World - RAPID RESPONSE: No war with Iran!: https://www.peoplesworld.org/article/rapid-response-no-war-with-iran/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Senate holds a roll call vote on a joint or concurrent resolution specifically addressing U.S. military action, hostilities, or the deployment of armed forces involving Iran (e.g., a resolution introduced under the War Powers Resolution of 1973 framework) between 2026-02-13 and 2026-02-28 (inclusive).

The vote can be on the passage of the resolution, a cloture motion, or a procedural motion (such as a motion to table the resolution), as long as the underlying legislation explicitly targets military action or war powers regarding Iran.

Resolution will be determined by official U.S. Senate Roll Call Vote records, available at https://www.senate.gov/legislative/votes_new.htm, and legislative text available on https://www.congress.gov/. If no such roll call vote occurs between 2026-02-13 and 2026-02-28, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: A Senate vote on an Iran War Powers Resolution would serve as a key early indicator of the perceived imminence of military action against Iran. If Congress is forcing a vote, it demonstrates credible intelligence, significant political momentum, or public evidence anticipating that the Trump administration may introduce U.S. armed forces into hostilities with Iran, which would subsequently trigger the 48-hour War Powers report requirement of the ultimate question.

question: OpenAI social app in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a social iOS app owned by OpenAI is available for installation on the US iOS app store by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Pre-Order does not satisfy the market conditions.

A "social app" refers to an iOS application whose primary function is facilitating social interaction between users, such as messaging, content sharing, or community engagement.

The primary resolution source will be the US iOS app store, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will OpenAI officially announce the development or release of a standalone social application by September 27, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Rumors have been circulating that OpenAI is developing a social network to compete with platforms like Elon Musk's X and a forthcoming standalone AI app from Meta. According to a reported leak accessed by The Verge in April 2025, OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman sought external feedback on a concept that integrates ChatGPT's capabilities into a social feed (https://medium.com). The ultimate question asks whether a social iOS app owned by OpenAI will be available on the US iOS App Store by the end of 2025. Given typical software rollout schedules, an official public announcement or beta launch of a social application by late September would be a strong leading indicator for a full App Store release later in the year.

Sources:
OpenAI takes the fight to Musk and Zuckerberg: https://medium.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if OpenAI publicly and officially announces the development, upcoming launch, beta release, or public launch of a standalone software application whose primary function is facilitating social interaction between users (such as messaging, user-to-user content sharing, or community engagement) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-27 (inclusive).

The announcement must be made via an official OpenAI channel, which includes but is not limited to:
- The official OpenAI Blog (https://openai.com/blog) or OpenAI News page (https://openai.com/news)
- OpenAI's official X (formerly Twitter) account (https://x.com/OpenAI)
- A verified press release issued directly by OpenAI or its executives (e.g., CEO Sam Altman) speaking in an official capacity at a public event.

Rumors, unauthorized leaks, or third-party reporting of internal developments without explicit and official confirmation from OpenAI do not count towards a Yes resolution. The announced application does not need to be exclusively for iOS to trigger a Yes, so long as it is a standalone social platform, network, or app (distinct from the standard ChatGPT interface or enterprise API tools). If no such official announcement occurs within the resolution window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Major consumer software releases, especially in the competitive social media market, are almost always preceded by official announcements, waitlists, or beta tests weeks or months in advance to build user bases and hype. An official announcement by OpenAI regarding a social platform in September strongly increases the probability of an iOS app store debut by December 2025.

question: Will Google Gemini 3 score at least 40% on Humanity’s Last Exam by January 31?

subquestions.question: Will any AI model achieve a score of at least 37.0% on the official Humanity's Last Exam leaderboard between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05?
subquestions.background_information:
Humanity's Last Exam (HLE) is a rigorous benchmark designed to test the frontier of AI capabilities. As of August 2025, Google's Gemini 2.5 Deep Think reasoning model reached a state-of-the-art score of 34.8% on this benchmark, outperforming other top models like Grok 4 and OpenAI's o3 (https://www.extremetech.com/computing). Around the same time, reports suggested an early version of Gemini 3.0 scored 32.4% on HLE (https://medium.com/ai-news). For the upcoming Gemini 3 to cross the ambitious 40% threshold by January 2026, we should expect the industry-wide state-of-the-art (SOTA) on HLE to continue steadily increasing in the months prior. This subquestion asks whether any AI model (from any developer) will be listed with a score of at least 37.0% on the official HLE leaderboard by December 5, 2025, acting as an early indicator of AI progress toward the ultimate 40% mark.

Sources:
ExtremeTech: https://www.extremetech.com/computing
Medium: https://medium.com/ai-news
Official Leaderboard: https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the official Humanity's Last Exam leaderboard (https://scale.com/leaderboard/humanitys_last_exam) lists any AI model (from any developer) with an overall score of 37.0% or higher at any point between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05 (inclusive). 

The resolution will be based strictly on the publicly visible scores on the provided official leaderboard URL during the specified window. If a score of 37.0% or higher is listed on the leaderboard at any time between 2025-11-05 and 2025-12-05, the question resolves Yes. If the highest score remains strictly below 37.0% throughout this entire time window, the question resolves No. Claims made by companies in technical reports, press releases, or blog posts do not count toward resolution unless the score is officially verified and published on the HLE leaderboard by the end date. If the official leaderboard is permanently taken down or continuously inaccessible during the entire resolution window, the question resolves as unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: To assess whether Gemini 3 can achieve 40% on Humanity's Last Exam by late January 2026, it is useful to track the general state-of-the-art progress on the benchmark. If any model achieves a score of 37.0% or higher by early December, it signals that the industry is progressing at a rate that makes a 40% score by Gemini 3 a month later highly plausible. Conversely, if no model can break 37% by December, the 40% target may be too difficult to reach by late January.

question: Ukraine agrees not to join NATO in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Ukraine publicly agrees not to join NATO by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An official pledge by Ukraine not to join NATO will qualify for a “Yes” resolution whether as a unilateral announcement or part of an agreement with the Russian Federation. 

Any agreement or pledge made before the resolution date of this market will qualify, regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

An agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO for any amount of time will count (e.g. If Ukraine not to join NATO for 10 years this will qualify).

An agreement by Ukraine not to join NATO as a precondition of a more comprehensive peace process or deal will qualify, even if the agreement is not finalized or part of a formalized peace deal. The September 8, 1995 “Agreed Basic Principles” between Bosnia and Yugoslavia which recognized the borders and sovereignty of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and was later formalized through the Dayton Peace Agreement is an example of a qualifying agreement. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by the Ukraine, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming a qualifying agreement has been reached will also count.

subquestions.question: Will Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump hold an in-person meeting between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-20?
subquestions.background_information:
Recent reports from late November 2025 indicate that Ukraine, the United States, and Russia are in the process of finalizing a peace plan to end the ongoing war. A pivotal component of this 28-point framework, backed by the Trump administration, requires Ukraine to formally abandon its bid for NATO membership in exchange for US security guarantees that mirror NATO's Article 5. According to reports covering the negotiations in Geneva, "The final agreement is expected to be finalized in a meeting between Zelenskiy and Trump" (https://www.bne.eu). Ukrainian officials also expressed optimism that Zelenskyy would travel to the US (possibly Mar-a-Lago) to cement the deal (https://www.cbsnews.com). Since finalizing the agreement hinges heavily on this highly anticipated leader-to-leader interaction, tracking whether this meeting occurs is a vital early indicator of whether Ukraine will ultimately agree to the NATO concessions embedded in the peace plan.

Sources:
CBS News - Ukraine agrees to peace proposal, with only "minor details" to settle: https://www.cbsnews.com
bne IntelliNews - EU leaders meet with US officials in Geneva to soften 28-point peace plan: https://www.bne.eu
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US President Donald Trump hold an in-person meeting between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-20 at 23:59:59 UTC. 

An "in-person meeting" is defined as both leaders being physically present in the same room or immediate geographic vicinity for the purpose of a discussion. Video conferences, phone calls, or exchanges through intermediaries do not qualify. 

The primary sources for resolution will be official press releases, schedules, or statements published by the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov) or the Office of the President of Ukraine (https://www.president.gov.ua/en). In the absence of direct government press releases, a clear consensus of credible reporting from major news agencies—such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Associated Press (https://apnews.com), or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com)—confirming that the meeting took place within the specified time window will be sufficient for a "Yes" resolution. 

If no qualifying in-person meeting between the two leaders takes place between the specified start date and end date, the question will resolve "No".
subquestions.rationale: The broader peace framework—which mandates Ukraine not joining NATO—is reportedly awaiting finalization at an upcoming meeting between Zelenskyy and Trump. If this in-person meeting happens, it strongly signals that the terms of the peace deal are agreeable to both sides and nearing formal adoption. If the meeting is delayed or canceled, it indicates a breakdown or stall in negotiations, significantly lowering the likelihood that Ukraine publicly pledges not to join NATO by the end of 2025.

question: Will a new country join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

Countries already part of the Abraham Accords as of June 26, 2025—including the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan—will not count.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the United States, Israel, or any prospective member country publicly announce active negotiations for a new country to join the Abraham Accords between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The Abraham Accords, initially signed in 2020, established formal diplomatic relations between Israel and several Arab states, including the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/). On October 17, 2025, former U.S. President Donald Trump indicated he expects an expansion of the accords soon, hoping Saudi Arabia will join, while other reports have mentioned potential expansion to Azerbaijan or Central Asian nations (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/). However, expansion efforts currently face significant hurdles due to the ongoing conflicts in the region, along with widespread negative public sentiment in Arab nations. Saudi Arabia has continually maintained that the establishment of a Palestinian state is a strict precondition for normalization. If a new country is to formally join the Accords by December 31, 2025, it is highly likely that formal negotiations will be publicly acknowledged or a framework agreement announced in the preceding months. Sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), an official representative (head of state, head of government, foreign minister, or their official spokespersons) of the United States, Israel, or any country not currently in the Abraham Accords publicly confirms that active negotiations are taking place or have concluded for a new country to join the Abraham Accords or establish formal diplomatic relations with Israel. The confirmation must be published in an official government press release (e.g., US State Department at https://www.state.gov or Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs at https://www.gov.il) or quoted directly by major, credible international news organizations (e.g., Reuters at https://www.reuters.com or AP News at https://apnews.com). Statements expressing mere 'hope' or 'desire' for a country to join do not qualify; the statement must explicitly acknowledge active, formal bilateral or mediated negotiations, or a completed agreement framework. If no such announcement occurs between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: To formally sign a normalization agreement and join the Abraham Accords by the end of 2025, significant diplomatic groundwork must be laid, which typically involves a period of publicly acknowledged negotiation or an imminent pre-signing announcement. Given the current geopolitical climate and the lack of confirmed imminent candidates as of late October 2025, an official announcement of negotiations by late November serves as a crucial leading indicator. If this subquestion resolves No, the probability of a sudden signing by December 31 drops dramatically, making it an excellent crux for forecasting the ultimate outcome.

question: Another France debt downgrade by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if France's long-term sovereign credit letter rating is downgraded by any of the three major credit rating agencies (S&P, Moody's, Fitch) at any point between September 12, 6:15 PM ET, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. subquestions.question: Will the daily closing yield of the France 10-Year Government Bond be 3.60% or higher on any trading day between September 13, 2025, and October 13, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 12, 2025, Fitch downgraded France's sovereign credit rating from 'AA-' to 'A+', citing political instability and strained public finances following the resignation of former Prime Minister Francois Bayrou. The downgrade and associated political turbulence pushed the French 10-year bond yield to 3.47%, a level close to Italy's, reflecting increased market anxiety over France's debt trajectory and governance (https://www.barrons.com/news/fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow-01682718000). With both Moody's and S&P Global scheduled to update their ratings later in the fall, market pricing on sovereign bonds will act as a real-time gauge of downgrade risk. If investors anticipate that the new Prime Minister, Sebastien Lecornu, will fail to enact a credible deficit consolidation plan, sovereign bond yields will likely face continued upward pressure. A crossing of the 3.60% threshold would signal severe distress and align with expectations of a further downgrade by the remaining major rating agencies.

Sources:
- Barron's: https://www.barrons.com/news/fitch-downgrades-france-s-credit-rating-in-new-debt-blow-01682718000
- Investing.com France 10-Year Bond Yield: https://www.investing.com/rates-bonds/france-10-year
- MarketWatch France 10-Year Yield: https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/bond/tmbmkfr-10y?countrycode=bx
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the daily closing yield of the France 10-Year Government Bond reaches or exceeds 3.60% on any trading day between 2025-09-13 and 2025-10-13 (inclusive). Resolution will be determined using the 'Price' column (which denotes the closing yield percentage) for the relevant dates on the historical data page for the France 10-Year Bond Yield on Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/rates-bonds/france-10-year-bond-yield-historical-data). If Investing.com is unavailable or its data is demonstrably erroneous, equivalent daily closing yield data from MarketWatch (https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/bond/tmbmkfr-10y?countrycode=bx) or Bloomberg (https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/rates-bonds/government-bonds/france) will be used as a fallback. Intraday yields that spike at or above 3.60% but close below 3.60% do not count toward a Yes resolution. If the yield does not close at or above 3.60% during the specified window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: Sovereign bond yields are a direct market proxy for a nation's creditworthiness. Because credit rating agencies (Moody's and S&P) use similar macroeconomic indicators and market realities as bond investors, a significant spike in the 10-year yield (rising from the recent 3.47% up to 3.60% or higher) serves as a strong, market-driven early indicator that conditions are worsening. This makes an official agency downgrade highly probable by the end of the year without just asking the ultimate question with an earlier date.

question: Will Donald Trump visit North Korea in 2025?

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will U.S. President Donald Trump physically enter South Korea between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
