question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla release Full Self-Driving (FSD) version 13 or 14 to non-employee customers by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Tesla is currently developing its Full Self-Driving (FSD) software, which operates as a Level 2 driver assistance system requiring continuous human supervision. Recent reports indicate that Tesla has launched a ride-hailing service in the San Francisco Bay Area, but with human drivers monitoring the vehicles, as the company lacks autonomous vehicle deployment permits in California (Electrek, 2025). In an effort to advance the technology, CEO Elon Musk has teased a major upcoming FSD update, indicating that the next major version (referred to as V14) could roll out as early as September 2025. Musk claims this update features a '10x increase in parameters' and will be two to three times safer than human drivers (Tesla North, August 2025). Tracking whether Tesla meets its short-term development milestones, such as releasing this major software version to the public, serves as a crucial leading indicator for the company's ability to launch a fully unsupervised system by June 2026.

Sources:
Electrek: https://electrek.co/
Tesla North: https://teslanorth.com/
Digital Trends: https://www.digitaltrends.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), Tesla officially releases a major Full Self-Driving (FSD) software update designated as version 13 (e.g., v13.x.x), version 14 (e.g., v14.x.x), or a newly branded major version that succeeds the v12 branch, to at least one non-employee customer vehicle.

To resolve Yes, the rollout must be explicitly verified by one or more of the following authoritative sources occurring between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01:
1. Third-party Tesla software tracking sites such as TeslaFi (https://www.teslafi.com/firmware.php) or Not a Tesla App (https://www.notateslaapp.com/software-updates/) documenting the firmware as installed on at least one customer vehicle.
2. Official announcements, release notes, or confirmations published by Tesla (https://www.tesla.com) or posted by Elon Musk on X (https://x.com/elonmusk) indicating that the public or early-access rollout to non-employees has begun.

If the software update is exclusively deployed to internal Tesla employee vehicles, or if the major version number remains in the v12 branch (e.g., v12.5.x, v12.6.x) throughout the entire resolution window, this question resolves No. If the release of the next major FSD version is delayed and postponed beyond the resolution window (i.e., occurs after 2025-10-01 23:59:59 UTC), the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: The successful launch of an unsupervised FSD system by mid-2026 relies on rapid, scheduled iterative improvements to the current software architecture. Elon Musk has explicitly targeted September 2025 for the next major release (V14), claiming significant structural upgrades. If Tesla fails to deliver this update to public testers within the promised September timeframe, it is a strong indicator that their software development timeline is slipping, which lowers the probability of achieving regulatory-approved, unsupervised autonomy by June 2026.

question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. officially announce an agreed framework or draft for a bilateral military security guarantee with Ukraine between October 31, 2025, and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In late August 2025, U.S. and Ukrainian officials met to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, with a draft project planned to be finalized as a framework version shortly thereafter. Furthermore, a coalition of Western leaders met in Paris on September 4, 2025, to discuss military-support frameworks, emphasizing that any European military role would require U.S. security guarantees as a 'back-stop.' Because negotiating a formal, binding treaty or executive agreement takes considerable time, a formal commitment by the U.S. before the end of 2025 would highly likely be preceded by the announcement of an agreed framework, draft text, or agreement-in-principle. Tracking whether the U.S. government officially confirms a draft framework in November acts as a strong leading indicator for a finalized, binding security guarantee in December.

Sources:
Українська правда: US secretary of state and chief of Zelenskyy's office discuss security guarantees, draft expected next week - https://www.google.com/search?q=US+secretary+of+state+and+chief+of+Zelenskyy%27s+office+discuss+security+guarantees
CBC News: Ukraine's allies discuss security guarantees, but say U.S. must help enforce any peace deal - https://www.google.com/search?q=Ukraine%27s+allies+discuss+security+guarantees%2C+but+say+U.S.+must+help+enforce+any+peace+deal
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30 (inclusive), the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or the U.S. Department of State (https://www.state.gov/) publishes a press release, official statement, or official briefing transcript explicitly announcing that the United States and Ukraine have reached an agreed framework, draft agreement, or agreed-in-principle text for a bilateral security guarantee.

To qualify, the announced framework or draft must explicitly include a proposed U.S. commitment to a military defense obligation, a military 'backstop,' or a direct military response mechanism in the event of an attack on Ukraine (similar in character to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment). Announcements of purely financial aid, weapons transfers without a defense guarantee, or cooperative/consultative mechanisms that do not obligate military defense will not qualify.

The qualifying announcement must occur strictly within the resolution window: starting on 2025-10-31 and ending on 2025-11-30. If no such official announcement is published on the specified official U.S. government websites by the end of 2025-11-30, the question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: A formalized, legally binding mutual defense commitment takes time to draft, finalize, and sign. By asking whether an official framework or draft agreement is announced in November, we are measuring a necessary precursor event. A 'Yes' resolution would strongly indicate that the parties have aligned on the core military commitments, making the finalization of the ultimate binding agreement by December 31, 2025, highly probable.

question: Somalians who defrauded government to fund terrorists deported?
description:
On September 18, 2025, Acting U.S. Attorney Joseph H. Thompson announced that eight Minneapolis defendants were indicted for defrauding Minnesota’s housing stabilization program. It is rumored that some of these funds were used to fund the Somalian terrorist group Al-Shabaab. You can read more about that here: https://www.city-journal.org/article/minnesota-welfare-fraud-somalia-al-shabaab?.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if any of the Minnesota defendants who were indicted for fraud in this case are officially deported from the United States by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

Deportation is defined as the formal removal of any of the indicted persons from the US by government authorities due to legal or administrative reasons. Voluntary departure, extradition, or relocation without an official deportation order will not count.

The resolution source will be credible reporting from major news outlets or official government statements.

subquestions.question: Will any of the eight defendants indicted on September 18, 2025, for Minnesota Housing Stabilization Services fraud enter a guilty plea or have their federal charges dismissed between 2025-12-22 and 2026-01-21?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 18, 2025, Acting U.S. Attorney Joseph H. Thompson announced the federal indictment of eight defendants in Minnesota for allegedly defrauding the Medicaid Housing Stabilization Services program (https://www.city-journal.org/article/minnesota-welfare-fraud-somalia-al-shabaab). The Trump administration has recently linked these welfare fraud schemes to potential terrorist financing for al-Shabaab and has deployed Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to Minneapolis to conduct mass deportations of Somali nationals (https://www.dailywire.com/news/trump-admin-sends-ice-to-minneapolis-to-nab-hundreds-of-somali-illegal-immigrants). However, under U.S. law, individuals facing active federal criminal charges are typically not deported until their criminal proceedings conclude. For any of these eight defendants to be officially deported by the ultimate question's deadline of February 28, 2026, their criminal cases would likely need to be resolved very quickly—either via a guilty plea with an agreement for immediate removal, or by the Department of Justice dismissing the charges to clear the way for ICE deportation. Tracking the federal court docket for plea agreements or dismissals provides a strong, early legal indicator of whether rapid deportation is feasible.

Sources:
City Journal: https://www.city-journal.org/article/minnesota-welfare-fraud-somalia-al-shabaab
The Daily Wire: https://www.dailywire.com/news/trump-admin-sends-ice-to-minneapolis-to-nab-hundreds-of-somali-illegal-immigrants
U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Minnesota: https://www.justice.gov/usao-mn
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if, between 2025-12-22 and 2026-01-21 (inclusive), official U.S. court records (such as PACER, https://pacer.uscourts.gov/) or credible reporting from major news outlets or the U.S. Department of Justice (specifically the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Minnesota at https://www.justice.gov/usao-mn) confirm that at least one of the eight defendants indicted on September 18, 2025, for Housing Stabilization Services fraud has either:
1. Formally entered a guilty plea in federal court, OR
2. Had their federal criminal charges officially dismissed by the prosecution or judge.

The qualifying event (the formal entry of the plea or the dismissal of the charges) must occur and be publicly verifiable between 2025-12-22 and 2026-01-21. If neither a plea nor a dismissal occurs for any of the eight defendants by January 21, 2026, at 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves "No".
subquestions.rationale: For a defendant to be deported while facing federal criminal charges, the ongoing criminal proceedings must generally be resolved first. This typically happens through a conviction (like an expedited guilty plea) followed by time served, or by prosecutors dismissing the charges to allow ICE to assume custody. If none of the eight defendants have their charges dismissed or enter a guilty plea by late January 2026, it is highly improbable that they will conclude their criminal process and be physically deported by the ultimate deadline of February 28, 2026. Therefore, a "No" resolution to this subquestion strongly indicates a "No" for the ultimate question.

question: Isar Aerospace successful orbital launch in 2025?

"Reaching stable orbit" is defined as the successful insertion of a payload into a sustained low Earth orbit (LEO) or higher, where the payload completes at least one full revolution around Earth.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Isar Aerospace publicly announce or officially reaffirm a target launch window for the second flight of the Spectrum rocket to occur in 2025, between October 31 and November 30, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Isar Aerospace, a well-funded European space tech startup, is developing the Spectrum rocket to provide launch services for small to medium-sized satellites. The company conducted its maiden flight from the Andøya Spaceport in Norway in March 2025. Although the rocket crashed shortly after takeoff, the company considered the test a "great success" for data-gathering purposes, noting that Spectrum launch vehicles 2 and 3 were already in production. 

To conduct a second orbital launch attempt by the end of 2025, Isar Aerospace would typically need to confirm a launch window several weeks in advance. This lead time is necessary to coordinate range safety, secure final regulatory approvals, and finalize logistics with payload customers—such as those confirmed under the European Space Agency's Flight Ticket Initiative. If a 2025 launch date is not publicly targeted or reaffirmed by late November, it strongly indicates that the launch will slip into 2026.

SpaceDaily: https://www.spacedaily.com/

subquestions.resolution_criteria:

Qualifying announcements must be published by an official Isar Aerospace channel, such as their official press releases (https://www.isaraerospace.com/news), their official X/Twitter account (https://x.com/isaraerospace), or statements explicitly attributed to company executives in credible aerospace reporting (e.g., https://spacenews.com/). 

If no such announcement is made between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-30, or if an announcement sets the launch window exclusively in 2026 or later, the question resolves No. If an announcement made prior to October 31, 2025, is not actively reaffirmed during the resolution window via official channels, it does not count toward a Yes resolution. Delayed announcements or events occurring after November 30, 2025, will not be considered.
subquestions.rationale: An orbital launch requires significant logistical and regulatory coordination. Aerospace companies typically announce or confirm a targeted launch window roughly a month before liftoff. Checking whether Isar Aerospace commits to a 2025 date during November serves as a highly informative leading indicator for the ultimate question of whether a successful launch will occur before the end of 2025.

question: Will US GDP growth in Q4 2025 be between 2.0% and 2.5%?
description:
This market will resolve according to the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP "Advance Estimate" release for Q4 of 2025, scheduled for January 29, 2026.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

The GDP release will be made available here: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

Note: data in the first available GDP report is labelled by the BEA as an "Advance Estimate". The data found in the advance estimate will be used to resolve this market. Data may be revised during the following quarter or as a part of the next estimate's publication, however any revisions to GDP report data made after the release of the advance estimate will not be considered for this market's resolution.

subquestions.question: Will the initial US Employment Situation report show an increase of 100,000 or more nonfarm payroll jobs for December 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
According to recent economic data, the US economy expanded at a robust 4.3% annualized rate in Q3 2025, driven largely by consumer spending. However, intermediate indicators showed labor market conditions cooling toward the end of the year. In November 2025, the economy added only 64,000 jobs, and the unemployment rate unexpectedly rose to 4.6% (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm). Since consumer spending is a primary driver of US GDP—accounting for more than two-thirds of economic activity—labor market health is deeply intertwined with GDP growth. The December 2025 nonfarm payrolls report will be the final major employment data point for Q4. A rebound in job creation to 100,000 or more would suggest sustained economic momentum, whereas another weak print would indicate softening conditions that could drag Q4 GDP growth down closer to the 2.0% - 2.5% range.

Sources:
US Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) GDP Data: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product
US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Employment Situation: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the initial "Employment Situation" report released by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that total nonfarm payroll employment (seasonally adjusted) increased by 100,000 or more for December 2025. The qualifying event must occur between the start_date of 2025-12-29 and the end_date of 2026-01-28 (inclusive).

Resolution will be based solely on the headline nonfarm payroll change figure for December 2025 found in the first release of the BLS Employment Situation report for that month, which is officially published on the BLS website (https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm or its archives at https://www.bls.gov/bls/newsrels.htm). Any subsequent revisions to the December 2025 figure made in later months will not be considered. If the reported figure is exactly 100,000, the question resolves Yes.

If the BLS report for December 2025 is delayed and not published between 2025-12-29 and 2026-01-28, this question will be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: December's nonfarm payroll data acts as a crucial proxy for household income and consumer spending in the final month of the quarter. Given the reported slowdown to 64k jobs in November, knowing whether job growth recovered to >= 100k or remained weak in December will significantly update forecasters on whether Q4 GDP has lost enough momentum to decelerate from 4.3% down to the narrower 2.0%–2.5% bracket.

question: Foreign intervention in Gaza in 2025?
description:

The foreign personnel must physically enter the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip to qualify. Entering the maritime territory, as occurred during the US’s attempt to construct a floating pier in 2024, or entering the airspace will not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the United Nations Security Council adopt a resolution authorizing the deployment of a multinational military, security, or peacekeeping force to the Gaza Strip before November 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
A ceasefire between Israel and Hamas went into effect on October 10, 2025, initiating the first phase of a peace plan mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump. While the U.S. has deployed 200 Central Command troops to Israel to coordinate aid and monitor the truce, these forces are prohibited from physically entering Gaza (Fortune, https://fortune.com/). To manage security and govern Gaza post-conflict, discussions are underway to deploy an International Stabilization Force (ISF) or a joint Arab-international force. However, international and regional stakeholders, including Egypt, have emphasized that any foreign force deployment requires a legal framework, specifically a United Nations Security Council (UNSC) resolution with a clear mandate (Middle East Monitor, https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/). On October 14, 2025, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced that talks had begun with permanent UNSC members, including Russia and China, to secure a resolution authorizing the ISF's deployment (Anadolu Ajansı, https://www.aa.com.tr/en/). 

Sources:
Fortune: https://fortune.com/
Middle East Monitor: https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/
Anadolu Ajansı: https://www.aa.com.tr/en/
UN Security Council: https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) officially adopts a resolution between 2025-10-16 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive) that explicitly mandates, authorizes, or establishes the deployment of a multinational military, security, police, or peacekeeping force to the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. 

The resolution must be officially adopted by the UNSC within this timeframe; proposed drafts or resolutions vetoed by permanent members will not count. The authorization must clearly permit the force to physically enter the terrestrial territory of Gaza for an operational role (e.g., stabilization, peacekeeping, border security inside Gaza, or enforcement). Resolutions that strictly limit the force to operating exclusively on the Egyptian side of the border or solely in maritime territory do not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be the official text published on the UN Security Council Resolutions page (https://www.un.org/securitycouncil/content/resolutions-0) or official UN press releases (https://press.un.org/en/content/security-council). If the UN site is unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting from major international news organizations (e.g., Reuters, AP News, BBC) confirming the resolution's adoption and mandate will be used.
subquestions.rationale: For a foreign military or peacekeeping force to legitimately deploy to Gaza, establishing international legal backing via a UN Security Council resolution is widely considered a prerequisite. Current diplomatic efforts are actively pursuing this authorization. If a UNSC resolution is adopted within this one-month window, it indicates that major geopolitical roadblocks have been cleared, significantly raising the probability of troops physically entering Gaza by the end of 2025. Conversely, if no resolution is reached due to vetoes or diplomatic stalling, a formal foreign deployment becomes much less likely.

If no such meeting is announced, the likelihood of resolving the complex legal and diplomatic hurdles necessary to recognize Crimea by year-end drops significantly.

question: Will EJ Antoni be confirmed as BLS Commissioner in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if E.J. Antoni is confirmed as Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The Senate must confirm this nominee for this market to resolve to "Yes". Recess appointments without Senate confirmation will not count toward a "Yes" resolution.

The resolution source for this market is information from the U.S. Senate (see: https://www.senate.gov/legislative/NominationsRejectedorWithdrawn.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will any sitting Republican U.S. Senator publicly announce their opposition to the confirmation of E.J. Antoni as BLS Commissioner between September 1, 2025 and September 28, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: In August 2025, President Donald Trump nominated conservative economist E.J. Antoni to be the Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) after firing the previous commissioner. The nomination has been highly controversial, with Antoni suggesting the suspension of monthly jobs reports. Democratic lawmakers have fiercely opposed the nomination. To be confirmed, Antoni requires a majority vote in the U.S. Senate, where Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority. Given this slim margin, Antoni can only afford to lose three Republican votes. Early public opposition from any Republican senator would serve as a strong indicator that his confirmation is in jeopardy. Sources: [1] Newsday - Trump's firing of data chief prompts questions: https://www.newsday.com [2] The Hill - Trump stuns Wall Street: https://thehill.com [3] MyBasin - BLS nominee E.J. Antoni suggests suspending monthly jobs reports: https://mybasin.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to 'Yes' if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-28 (inclusive), any sitting Republican U.S. Senator publicly states that they will vote against, oppose, or not support the confirmation of E.J. Antoni as the Commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). The statement of opposition must be made publicly either through the senator's official communication channels (e.g., official website, press release, verified social media accounts) or reported directly by a credible news organization. 'Publicly states' means the senator or their official spokesperson explicitly communicates their intent to oppose or vote against the nomination. General expressions of concern, statements that they are 'undecided,' or remarks that they 'need to review the nominee's record' do not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution. If no sitting Republican U.S. Senator makes such a public statement between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-28, the question will resolve to 'No'. Data sources to be used for resolution include the official press releases of U.S. Senators (accessible via https://www.senate.gov/senators/), and consensus reporting from major news outlets (e.g., https://apnews.com/, https://www.reuters.com/).
subquestions.rationale: Because the Republicans have a narrow 53-47 majority in the Senate, the loss of even a few Republican votes would sink Antoni's nomination. Public opposition from a Republican senator early in the process would be a major signal that his confirmation is in trouble, making it a critical crux for forecasting the ultimate question.

question: TikTok sale announced in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if ByteDance announces their intention to sell TikTok by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to “No”.

A public announcement of the intention to sell TikTok will qualify even if a sale has not been finalized. This includes any formal declaration made by ByteDance or its authorized representatives regarding their plans to sell or transfer ownership of TikTok.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from ByteDance. However, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will TikTok be removed from the U.S. Apple App Store or Google Play Store between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Under U.S. law, ByteDance has been ordered to divest its U.S. operations of TikTok to address national security concerns. The deadline for this divestiture has been extended multiple times by President Donald Trump, with the current deadline set for September 17, 2025 (https://invezz.com/news/trump-grants-bytedance-another-90-day-extension-to-sell-tiktok). President Trump has stated that a group of 'very wealthy people' is prepared to buy the platform, but the transaction still requires explicit approval from the Chinese government (https://gizmodo.com/trump-says-very-wealthy-people-are-ready-to-buy-tiktok). If ByteDance does not divest TikTok by the deadline and no further extension is granted by the U.S. administration, the app is expected to face a nationwide ban, which includes being removed from U.S. app stores. The outcome of the September 17 deadline is a critical indicator for any potential sale: a ban would strongly signal that a sale will not occur (likely due to Beijing's refusal to approve it), while an extension or avoidance of a ban keeps the possibility of a sale announcement alive for the remainder of 2025.

Sources:
Trump grants ByteDance another 90-day extension to sell TikTok - https://invezz.com/news/trump-grants-bytedance-another-90-day-extension-to-sell-tiktok
Trump Says 'Very Wealthy People' Are Ready to Buy TikTok - https://gizmodo.com/trump-says-very-wealthy-people-are-ready-to-buy-tiktok
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if, at any point between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive), the TikTok application is removed and becomes unavailable for download by new users on either the iOS Apple App Store (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tiktok/id835599320) or the Google Play Store (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.zhiliaoapp.musically) in the United States for a continuous period of at least 24 hours. 

To qualify for a "Yes" resolution, the removal must be explicitly attributed to U.S. government action, enforcement of the U.S. divestment law, or compliance with a U.S. federal ban. 

Removal due to routine technical glitches, voluntary temporary removal by ByteDance for maintenance, or standard developer policy violations (e.g., an app store guideline violation unrelated to the divestment mandate) will not trigger a "Yes" resolution. If the September 17, 2025 deadline passes and the app remains available continuously through the end date, or if it is removed but restored within 24 hours, the question resolves "No".

Primary sources for resolution will be credible media reporting from major technology and news outlets (e.g., https://www.reuters.com, https://www.bloomberg.com, https://techcrunch.com) explicitly confirming the app's removal from the U.S. storefronts in compliance with the U.S. government mandate.
subquestions.rationale: The current divestment deadline is September 17, 2025. Tracking whether TikTok is actually removed from U.S. app stores shortly after this deadline provides an unambiguous, observable crux. If a ban is enacted, it likely means negotiations failed or the Chinese government blocked the sale, drastically reducing the odds of a sale announcement by the end of 2025. Conversely, if no ban occurs, it implies either a sale is imminent or another extension was secured, making a later sale announcement much more probable.

question: Trump meets Xi, Putin, and Kim by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Kim Jong Un all meet with Donald Trump between October 24, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both the listed individual and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will North Korean leader Kim Jong Un physically attend the APEC summit in Gyeongju, South Korea between October 25, 2025 and November 5, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
US President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit South Korea for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Gyeongju, which will run from October 31 to November 1, 2025. During his Asia trip, Trump is expected to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Speculation is also high regarding a potential meeting between Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has suggested the APEC summit as a platform for a possible Trump-Kim meeting, and South Korea's reunification minister noted a 'considerable' chance of such a meeting occurring during the regional summit. However, it remains uncertain whether Kim Jong Un will travel to Gyeongju to attend the APEC summit. If Kim makes the trip to attend the summit, it would act as a highly informative indicator that an in-person meeting with Trump is imminent.

Sources:
The Indian Express: https://indianexpress.com/
AFP: https://www.afp.com/
India TV News: https://www.indiatvnews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if a consensus of credible reporting confirms that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un physically attended any official event, session, or sidelines gathering associated with the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, between 2025-10-25 and 2025-11-05 (inclusive).

'Attending' is defined as Kim Jong Un being physically present in Gyeongju and participating in the summit or holding official bilateral or multilateral meetings at or directly adjacent to the summit venue. If Kim Jong Un travels to South Korea but does not attend any APEC-associated events (for example, if he only meets leaders at the DMZ or in Seoul), this question resolves No. If the APEC summit is cancelled or postponed beyond the resolution window, the question resolves No.

The resolution will be based on major global news agencies. Resolvers should check the following sources to determine the outcome:
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/
AP News: https://apnews.com/
Bloomberg: https://www.bloomberg.com/
subquestions.rationale: For the ultimate question to resolve Yes, Trump must meet Xi, Putin, and Kim by December 31, 2025. With Trump already visiting South Korea for the APEC summit to meet Xi, a meeting with Kim Jong Un is a critical missing piece. Kim's physical attendance at the APEC summit in Gyeongju is a distinct observable event that serves as a massive crux: if Kim attends, the probability of him meeting Trump jumps significantly, pointing to a higher likelihood for the ultimate question. If he skips the summit, the timeframe and venues for a potential meeting become much more constrained.

question: EU sanctions on Israel by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the European Union officially imposes new sanctions of any form against Israel between September 2 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Sanctions could include measures like tariffs, trade restrictions, financial penalties, diplomatic expulsions, travel bans, restrictions on specific individuals, or any other actions that are commonly recognized as sanctions.

Sanctions against Israeli citizens or entities which do not directly target the Israeli state or members of the Israeli government will not qualify.

The passage of an official act authorizing sanctions on Israel within this market's timeframe will count toward a "Yes" resolution, regardless of if/when the sanctions come into effect.

Only the imposition of sanctions on Israel by the EU as an entity will qualify; if individual member states of the EU apply sanctions against Israel (e.g., France imposes novel trade restrictions on Israel unilaterally), it will not be sufficient to resolve this market to "Yes".

The primary resolution source will be official information from the European Union; however, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission or the EU High Representative formally propose new sanctions, tariffs, or trade restrictions against the Israeli state or its government by October 3, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The European Union has faced mounting internal and external pressure to impose punitive measures on Israel in response to the humanitarian situation in Gaza. In July 2025, the European External Action Service (EEAS) prepared a list of potential options, including suspending the EU-Israel Association Agreement, imposing an arms embargo, and enacting targeted sanctions on Israeli government ministers. However, EU sanctions typically require the unanimous agreement of all 27 member states, a threshold that has proven difficult to reach due to strong opposition from countries like Germany and Hungary (https://www.rt.com/).

During an informal meeting of EU foreign ministers in Copenhagen on August 30, 2025, divisions remained apparent. Nonetheless, EU High Representative Kaja Kallas stated that concrete measures would be proposed "next week." Additionally, Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen noted that while an import ban might be politically impossible, the EU could potentially impose heavy tariffs on imports from Israel, an action that might only require a qualified majority rather than unanimity (https://www.euronews.com/). Before the Council of the EU can vote on adopting any such sanctions or tariffs, a formal proposal must first be drafted and submitted by the European Commission or the High Representative. Tracking whether this official proposal is submitted is a critical leading indicator for whether actual sanctions will materialize later in the year.

Sources:
RT: EU to propose sanctions on Israel - media - https://www.rt.com/
Euronews: EU Member States divided over Gaza at their Copenhagen meeting - https://www.euronews.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the European Commission or the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy officially submits or presents a formal proposal for new sanctions, tariffs, or trade restrictions directly targeting the State of Israel, its government ministers, or its military to the Council of the European Union between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03 (inclusive).

To qualify, the proposed measures must target the Israeli state, its government, or its military apparatus. Proposals that exclusively target non-governmental Israeli citizens or private entities (such as individual settlers) without directly targeting the Israeli state or government will not trigger a Yes resolution.

The proposal does not need to be adopted, voted on, or enacted by the Council within this timeframe; the formal submission or official presentation of the proposal is sufficient for a Yes resolution. If the proposal is submitted confidentially, it will count toward resolution if its submission is subsequently confirmed by official EU statements or a strong consensus of credible reporting by major international news outlets (e.g., Reuters, Bloomberg, AFP).

If no such qualifying proposal is submitted between 2025-09-03 and 2025-10-03, this question resolves No. Any proposals submitted after October 3, 2025, will not be considered, and the question will be resolved as No.

Primary resolution sources will be official press releases, session minutes, or statements from the EU:
- Council of the EU Press Releases (https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/)
- European Commission Press Corner (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/home/en)
- European External Action Service (EEAS) (https://www.eeas.europa.eu/eeas/press-material_en)
subquestions.rationale: Before the EU can enact new sanctions or tariffs against Israel, an official proposal must be submitted by the European Commission or the High Representative. Given the EU's highly bureaucratic and often slow legislative process, if no formal proposal is even tabled by early October, it becomes highly improbable that the EU will achieve the necessary political consensus to actually impose sanctions by the end of December. Monitoring this procedural milestone provides a strong, early signal for the ultimate outcome.

question: Trump eliminates capital gains tax on crypto in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump signs a bill into law or performs any executive action changing US tax law to eliminate capital gains tax on any cryptocurrency assets by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Such a bill must apply to US taxpaying persons in general; if a law applies only to specific companies or institutions, it will not qualify toward a "Yes" resolution to this market.

If capital gains is eliminated only for specific types or classes of crypto assets (e.g., only Bitcoin or Ethereum, only American issued cryptocurrencies, or only NFTs), it will still count toward a "Yes" resolution for this market.

If the bill is signed into law, or executive action is instituted before the resolution date, it will suffice to resolve this market to "Yes" regardless of when it takes effect.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US federal government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate pass any bill that includes a provision eliminating or creating a de minimis exemption for capital gains tax on cryptocurrency before the end of October 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The Trump administration has been actively pushing pro-crypto policies, aiming to position the U.S. as a global leader in digital assets. Recent actions include the signing of the GENIUS Act to regulate stablecoins and an executive order allowing cryptocurrencies in 401(k) retirement accounts (https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/07/crypto-policy-under-the-trump-administration-could-enhance-adoption-of-digital-assets-analysis/, https://decrypt.co/2025/08/08/morning-minute-crypto-in-your-401ks-is-finally-happening). Earlier in the year, there were reports of a 'Hail Mary' push to include a crypto capital gains tax exemption in a major legislative package referred to as the 'One Big Beautiful Bill' (OBBB) (https://decrypt.co/2025/06/30/trumps-big-beautiful-bill-may-get-a-hail-mary-bitcoin-tax-exemption). The proposed de minimis tax exemption would allow American crypto users to avoid reporting smaller transactions for capital gains purposes. For President Trump to eliminate the capital gains tax on crypto via the legislative route by the end of 2025, significant congressional progress must be made. Tracking whether such a provision can pass at least one chamber of Congress provides a strong leading indicator for the ultimate resolution of comprehensive tax policy changes by year-end.

Sources:
Decrypt: https://decrypt.co/2025/06/30/trumps-big-beautiful-bill-may-get-a-hail-mary-bitcoin-tax-exemption
Crowdfund Insider: https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2025/07/crypto-policy-under-the-trump-administration-could-enhance-adoption-of-digital-assets-analysis/
Decrypt: https://decrypt.co/2025/08/08/morning-minute-crypto-in-your-401ks-is-finally-happening
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if official congressional records show that either the U.S. House of Representatives or the U.S. Senate has successfully passed a bill or joint resolution containing a provision that eliminates capital gains tax, or creates a de minimis tax exemption for capital gains, on any cryptocurrency assets, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 11:59 PM ET (inclusive).

The legislation must pass a floor vote in at least one chamber. The provision must apply to U.S. taxpaying persons in general; bills that solely apply to specific companies or institutions will not count. If the provision only applies to specific types of crypto assets (e.g., Bitcoin), it will still qualify for a 'Yes' resolution. 

The primary resolution source will be the official U.S. legislative tracker (https://www.congress.gov/). If no such bill successfully passes either chamber between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, the question resolves 'No'. Delayed votes or events occurring after the resolution window are excluded.
subquestions.rationale: To achieve a legislative repeal or exemption of the capital gains tax on cryptocurrency by December 2025, a bill would likely need to pass at least one chamber of Congress by late October. If a chamber passes such a bill, it signals strong momentum and makes the ultimate outcome highly probable. If no chamber manages to pass relevant legislation by October 31, the likelihood of a bill becoming law by year-end drops significantly, leaving unilateral executive action as the only viable—and potentially more legally complex—pathway.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly launches a fully driverless taxi service by December 31, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

Any service that allows a member of the general public to summon and ride in a Tesla vehicle operating without any human—onboard or remote—actively controlling the vehicle will count. A human may be present in the vehicle or monitoring remotely for emergency intervention, but they must not be physically positioned to take control (for example, no safety driver in the driver’s seat) and must not actively steer, brake, accelerate, or otherwise drive the car under normal operation.

A program that is restricted to Tesla employees, invite-only testers, closed-beta participants, factory self-delivery features, or the mere release of Full Self-Driving software for private owner-drivers will not qualify. Regulatory permits or approvals, press demonstrations, and prototype unveilings without live public ridership likewise will not count toward resolution.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla be publicly confirmed to have applied for a driverless autonomous vehicle permit in Texas between September 1 and September 8, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
In June 2025, Tesla launched a limited 'Robotaxi' trial in Austin, Texas, using a fleet of Model Y vehicles. Contrary to CEO Elon Musk's previous claims of fully unsupervised rides, the trial vehicles operate with a human 'safety monitor' in the passenger seat. This cautious rollout occurred as Texas lawmakers requested Tesla to delay fully driverless operations until a new autonomous vehicle law took effect. Signed by Governor Greg Abbott, the law requires firms to obtain a permit from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) before operating self-driving vehicles on public streets without a human driver, and this law officially comes into effect on September 1, 2025. Since Texas is currently Tesla's primary testing ground for its Robotaxi pilot, securing this driverless permit is a critical regulatory milestone. Whether Tesla files for this permit immediately after the application window opens will serve as a strong indicator of its readiness and timeline to remove human safety monitors and launch a fully driverless service by the end of 2025.

Sources:
Popular Mechanics: https://www.popularmechanics.com/
The Express Tribune: https://tribune.com.pk/
CNA: https://www.channelnewsasia.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-08 (inclusive), credible reporting from major media outlets (such as https://www.reuters.com/ or https://techcrunch.com/) or an official statement/record from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (https://www.txdmv.gov/) publicly confirms that Tesla has formally submitted an application—or has an active application pending—for a permit to operate autonomous vehicles without a human driver on public roads in Texas. The application must explicitly be for fully driverless operation, without any onboard safety driver or monitor, to comply with the Texas law that became effective on September 1, 2025. If no such application is publicly confirmed by 11:59 PM ET on 2025-09-08, the question resolves No. If an application is submitted but kept completely secret and not publicly reported during the resolution window, it will not count towards a Yes resolution. Announcements of mere intent to apply without actual confirmed submission will not qualify.
subquestions.rationale: For Tesla to launch a fully driverless Robotaxi service in 2025, it must secure regulatory approval in the states where it intends to operate. Texas is currently Tesla's primary testbed for its robotaxi fleet. With a new Texas law requiring driverless autonomous vehicle permits going into effect on September 1, 2025, Tesla must secure this permit to transition its monitor-supervised trial to a fully driverless service. If Tesla immediately applies for this permit upon the law's enactment (between September 1 and September 8), it strongly signals readiness to launch a public, fully driverless service before the 2025 year-end deadline of the ultimate question. A failure to apply during this initial window suggests technical or regulatory delays that make a 2025 driverless launch highly unlikely.

question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. House of Representatives pass an appropriations bill funding the Departments of Commerce and Justice by January 20, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
Congress faces a January 30, 2026, deadline to pass remaining fiscal 2026 spending measures to avert a government shutdown. On January 6, 2026, lawmakers unveiled a $174 billion bipartisan "minibus" spending package covering the Departments of Commerce, Justice, Energy, and Interior, as well as the EPA and federal science initiatives. The package includes $78 billion for the Commerce and Justice Departments (funding agencies like the FBI, NASA, and the U.S. Marshals Service). A final House vote on the package was expected around January 9, 2026, though it requires navigating a narrow Republican majority and potential procedural hurdles. Passing this package is critical for averting a shutdown and demonstrating the Republican Party's ability to govern ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

Sources:
House Clerk Votes: https://clerk.house.gov/Votes
Congress.gov: https://www.congress.gov/
CBS News (Context): https://www.cbsnews.com/news/government-shutdown-deadline-congress/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the U.S. House of Representatives passes an appropriations bill providing full-year fiscal 2026 funding for the Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-20 (inclusive).

The resolution will be based on official roll call vote results published on the website of the Clerk of the U.S. House of Representatives (https://clerk.house.gov/Votes) and/or official legislative tracking on Congress.gov (https://www.congress.gov/). 

To qualify, the passed legislation must be a full-year appropriations package (such as the proposed "minibus"); a stopgap funding measure or Continuing Resolution (CR) that temporarily extends funding without full-year appropriations does not qualify. If the House passes the bill within the resolution window, it resolves Yes, regardless of whether the Senate subsequently passes it or the President signs it by the end date. If no such full-year funding bill for these departments is passed by the House by 11:59 PM ET on 2026-01-20, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question is a combination of avoiding a government shutdown by January 31, 2026, and the Republican Party retaining control of the House in November 2026. Passing the $174 billion minibus package in the House is a significant early hurdle. If the House passes this bill by January 20, the likelihood of a January 30 shutdown drops significantly because major agencies will be funded. Furthermore, the successful passage of a complex appropriations package demonstrates that House Republicans can overcome internal divisions to govern effectively, acting as a proxy indicator for their electability and chances of retaining the House majority in the 2026 elections.

question: Negative GDP growth in Q4 2025?
description:
"This market will resolve to 'Yes' if the seasonally adjusted and annualized GDP 'Advance Estimate' for Q4 2025, scheduled for release by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on January 29, 2026, reports a growth rate below 0. Otherwise, this market will resolve to 'No'.

The GDP release will be available at: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product.

Only the first available GDP report labeled as the 'Advance Estimate' will be used for resolution. Any subsequent revisions or updates to the data will not be considered."

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) report that total nonfarm payroll employment increased by fewer than 100,000 jobs in October 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The U.S. economic landscape in 2025 has shown significant volatility. While Q2 2025 GDP rebounded to a strong 3.3% annualized growth rate driven by AI investments and consumer spending, Q1 experienced a 0.5% decline (Yahoo Finance, https://finance.yahoo.com). Furthermore, economists have warned that recent tariff implementations might drag on future quarters, potentially slowing annual growth. Observations of the labor market suggest it remains in a 'no-hire, no-fire' holding pattern. To forecast whether Q4 2025 GDP will turn negative, forecasters need early signals of economic contraction in the final quarter. The October 2025 jobs report (Nonfarm Payrolls) is the first major concurrent indicator for Q4 performance. A reading below 100,000 jobs typically signals significant cooling in the labor market, strongly correlating with broader economic downturns and lower GDP. Sources: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics: https://www.bls.gov/ces/ | Yahoo Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reports that total nonfarm payroll employment changed by fewer than +100,000 jobs (which includes any increase of 99,000 or less, as well as any decrease or negative number) for the month of October 2025. The qualifying event must occur between the start date of 2025-10-30 and the end date of 2025-11-20 (inclusive). Only the initially reported ('advance' or first estimate) figure for October 2025 will be used for resolution. Any subsequent revisions or updates in later months will not be considered. If the report is delayed and not published by the end date, the question resolves as unresolvable. The official resolution source is the 'Employment Situation' news release published by the BLS, available at: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm.
subquestions.rationale: Total nonfarm payrolls serve as one of the most reliable and immediate indicators of current economic activity. Because October is the first month of the fourth quarter, significant weakness in October job growth (falling below the 100,000 threshold) would be a strong early indicator that Q4 GDP could be at risk of turning negative, effectively acting as a crux for forecasters.

question: Will Russia capture Pokrovsk train station by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the Pokrovsk train station (48.284816377539386, 37.180016843748454) by October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

The train station will be considered captured if any part of the train station icon is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

subquestions.question: Will DeepStateMap show Russian control within 5 kilometers of the Pokrovsk train station at any point between October 1 and October 21, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Throughout the summer and early fall of 2025, Russian forces have maintained a persistent offensive in the Donetsk region, heavily targeting the logistics hub of Pokrovsk. While Russian forces have made localized gains, such as advancing near Novoekonomichnoye and the village of Lysovka (Charter 97), their progress has been slow and costly, and they have faced significant Ukrainian counter-attacks. Pokrovsk remains one of the most intense battle zones along the frontline (Al Jazeera Online). The Pokrovsk train station is centrally located within the city. For Russian forces to capture the train station by October 31, they must first penetrate the immediate outskirts and defensive lines of the city. A 5-kilometer radius around the train station covers the eastern approaches to Pokrovsk. Monitoring whether Russian-controlled territory breaches this 5 km threshold by October 21 serves as a highly measurable and reliable early indicator of Russia's ability to reach the train station by the end of the month.

Sources:
Charter 97 - https://charter97.org/
Al Jazeera Online - https://www.aljazeera.com/
DeepStateMap - https://deepstatemap.live/
ISW Interactive Map - https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, at any point between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-21 11:59 PM UTC (inclusive), the DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) shades any area within a 5.00-kilometer radius of the Pokrovsk train station (coordinates: 48.284816, 37.180016) in red, indicating Russian control.

To verify this, resolvers should use the measurement tool on DeepStateMap (or a standard Haversine geodesic distance calculation) to measure the distance from the station's exact coordinates to the nearest edge of the Russian-controlled (red) zone. If the minimum distance is 5.00 km or less during the resolution window, the criteria are met.

Once the 5 km threshold is breached and recorded, any subsequent loss of control by Russian forces will not reverse the Yes resolution.

Fallback criteria: If DeepStateMap is permanently rendered unavailable or stops updating during the resolution window, the primary ISW interactive map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) will be used to make the identical 5 km distance measurement. If both maps are permanently unavailable, resolution will be based on a consensus of credible open-source intelligence (OSINT) and major news reporting explicitly stating that Russian forces have advanced within 5 km of the Pokrovsk train station. If no such event occurs by 2025-10-21 11:59 PM UTC, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: If Russia is to capture the Pokrovsk train station by October 31, their forces must exhibit the momentum to reach the city's immediate perimeter beforehand. Tracking a 5-kilometer radius around the train station provides a concrete geographical crux. A failure to breach this radius by October 21 strongly suggests that Russian forces lack the necessary pace to secure the station by the ultimate deadline.

question: Brazil unemployment below 6.3% for Q4 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Brazil's unemployment rate for Q4 2025 is below 6.3% when it is released. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve according to IBGE's (https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego) public release of the Q4 2025 figure unemployment, expected in January 2026. If the publication of this figure is delayed beyond February 28, 2026 ET, this market will resolve according to the last published figure. 

Because this market's resolution source reports quarterly unemployment to one decimal point (e.g. 4.5%), this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

subquestions.question: Will the first official IBGE unemployment rate published between October 1 and October 31, 2025, be 5.5% or lower?
subquestions.background_information:
Brazil's labor market has seen a sustained tightening throughout 2025, with unemployment dropping to historic lows. In the moving quarter ending July 2025, the unemployment rate fell to 5.6%, down from 6.2% in May, and formal employment hit record highs. The release of this July data was delayed by 18 days due to technical issues at the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE), shifting the typical publication schedule into mid-September. Economists, such as Bruno Imaizumi from 4intelligence, projected the rate to reach a new historic low of 5.5% for the August moving quarter. The IBGE tracks this via the PNAD Contínua survey. This subquestion measures whether the labor market will meet or exceed these optimistic projections in the upcoming data release. A sustained drop or stabilization at 5.5% would strongly suggest that the ultimate Q4 2025 figure will easily remain below 6.3%, especially since the fourth quarter typically benefits from seasonal holiday hiring.

Sources:
IBGE Unemployment Indicators: https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego
IBGE News Agency: https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/en/agencia-news
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the first headline unemployment rate (taxa de desocupação, PNAD Contínua) published by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE) occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), and the published rate is 5.5% or lower.

Resolution will be based exclusively on the official IBGE indicators page (https://www.ibge.gov.br/en/indicators#desemprego) or official IBGE press releases (https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/en/agencia-news).

- The rate is evaluated to one decimal place, matching IBGE's reporting standard. A published rate of exactly 5.5% resolves Yes, while 5.6% resolves No.
- The specific reference period of the data (e.g., the moving quarter ending in August or September) does not matter, as long as it is the very first newly released figure published within the specified resolution window.
- If the IBGE revises the figure after publication, the first published figure within the window will be used for resolution, unless a correction is explicitly issued within 24 hours of the release due to an acknowledged clerical error.
- Delayed event contingency: If IBGE fails to publish any new unemployment rate between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, this question should be considered unresolvable and canceled.
subquestions.rationale: The trend in the near-term moving quarter (August/September) will act as a strong leading indicator for the Q4 2025 outcome. If unemployment falls to 5.5% or lower in October's release, it confirms the structural tightening of the labor market and validates expert projections. This would add high confidence that Q4 unemployment (which typically drops further due to holiday seasonality) will remain safely below the 6.3% threshold.

question: Will Trump pardon Sam Bankman-Fried in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed individual receives a presidential pardon, commutation, or reprieve from Donald Trump by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for whether the individual is pardoned or not will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump post or repost a message mentioning Sam Bankman-Fried on his official X or Truth Social account between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Sam Bankman-Fried, the former CEO of the cryptocurrency exchange FTX, was sentenced to 25 years in prison in March 2024 for fraud and conspiracy. His legal team is preparing for oral arguments in his appeal scheduled for November 4, 2025. Speculation has arisen that Bankman-Fried, supported by his parents, is actively seeking a presidential pardon from President Donald Trump, who returned to office in January 2025 and has already granted pardons to several figures in the crypto industry, such as Ross Ulbricht. Trump's public statements on social media often precede or reflect his pardon decisions; for instance, he recently posted on Truth Social regarding his pardon of Sheriff Scott Jenkins. Monitoring Trump's social media for mentions of Bankman-Fried provides an early indicator of whether the administration is publicly considering a pardon before the end of the year.

Sources:
The Crypto Basic: https://thecryptobasic.com/2025/09/12/sam-bankman-fried-appeal-hearing/
Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/2025/05/28/trump-makes-news-with-more-pardons/
TechStory: https://techstory.in/sam-bankman-fried-to-challenge-his-conviction/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Donald Trump makes at least one post, repost (retweet), or 'Re-Truth' on his official X account (https://x.com/realDonaldTrump) or his official Truth Social account (https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump) that explicitly contains the exact text 'Bankman-Fried', 'Sam Bankman', or 'SBF' (case-insensitive) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time, inclusive. The qualifying text must appear in the text body of the post or be explicitly written in text natively embedded within the post's image or quote-tweet. Spoken audio or video content alone where the name is spoken but not written in the post's text does not count. If a post is made during the resolution window and subsequently deleted, it will still count toward a Yes resolution provided there is credible proof (such as archived versions from the Wayback Machine at https://archive.org/web/ or reporting by credible mainstream news outlets) that the post was made by the official account within the specified time window.
subquestions.rationale: President Trump frequently uses his social media platforms to telegraph his political actions, including his decisions on pardons and commutations (as he did for Sheriff Jenkins). A public mention of Sam Bankman-Fried by Trump shortly before SBF's November 4 appeal hearing would strongly indicate that Trump is actively monitoring the case and is sympathetic to, or weighing, a potential pardon. This would significantly update the probability of the ultimate pardon outcome.

question: Will Claude 5 be released by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Anthropic's Claude 5 model is made available to the general public by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For this market to resolve to "Yes," Claude 5 must be launched and publicly accessible, including via open beta or open rolling waitlist signups. A closed beta or any form of private access will not suffice. The release must be clearly defined and publicly announced by Anthropic as being accessible to the general public.

Claude 5 refers to a product explicitly named Claude 5 (e.g. Claude 5.0 would count), or one that is recognized as a successor to Claude 4, similar to the progression from Claude 2 to Claude 3. Products labeled as Claude 4.5 or similar will not count for this market's resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from Anthropic, with additional verification from a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Anthropic officially announce or release a "Claude Opus 4.5" model by October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 29, 2025, Anthropic officially released Claude Sonnet 4.5, an upgraded AI model touting major improvements in coding and agentic capabilities, particularly on benchmarks like SWE-bench and OSWorld (https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/29/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-4-5-its-best-ai-model-for-coding/). This rapid launch occurred less than two months after the release of Claude Opus 4.1 in August 2025. The debut of the Sonnet 4.5 model introduces a new mid-cycle generation. 

The ultimate question asks whether a completely new major version, Claude 5, will be released by the end of 2025. Tracking whether Anthropic intends to complete the "4.5" model family by announcing "Claude Opus 4.5" serves as a highly informative crux. Historically, Anthropic staggers the releases of its model tiers (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus). If the company utilizes October to roll out or preview the Opus version of the 4.5 generation, the short remaining time window in the year makes a subsequent full Claude 5 release before 2026 highly improbable.

Sources:
TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/2025/09/29/anthropic-launches-claude-sonnet-4-5-its-best-ai-model-for-coding/
Anthropic Official News: https://www.anthropic.com/news
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if Anthropic officially announces or publicly releases an AI model explicitly named "Opus 4.5", "Claude 4.5 Opus", or "Claude Opus 4.5" between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive).

The announcement or release must be verifiable via Anthropic's official blog (https://www.anthropic.com/news) or their official X/Twitter account (https://x.com/AnthropicAI).

"Announces" is defined as a clear, official public statement from Anthropic confirming that they are developing, training, or planning to release the Opus 4.5 model. A formal release to the Claude API, a limited beta program, or an early access preview explicitly bearing the Opus 4.5 name also qualifies for a "Yes" resolution.

Leaks, rumors, or unofficial statements from third parties do not count. If the model is announced under a completely different naming convention (e.g., they skip directly to Claude 5 Opus), this does not satisfy the criteria.

If no qualifying announcement or release occurs between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 at 11:59 PM PT, this question resolves "No".
subquestions.rationale: If Anthropic officially commits to or launches an 'Opus 4.5' model in October, it firmly establishes that their product cycle remains focused on the 4.x generation. Given the typical months-long gap between major version updates required to maximize marketing impact and allow enterprise users to adapt, dedicating October to Opus 4.5 makes a Claude 5 release by December 31, 2025, extremely unlikely. Conversely, skipping the rest of the 4.5 tier could signal an accelerated jump straight to Claude 5, making this a strong crux for the ultimate question.

question: Will Russia capture Huliaipole by December 31?
description:

The intersection station will be considered captured if any part of the intersection is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by the specified date, the market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.
