subquestions.question: Will Russia capture the settlement of Zelenyi Hai (Zaporizhzhia Oblast) by December 20, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Recent reporting indicates Russian forces are advancing in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Oblast and creating a strategic corridor from the north towards Huliaipole. According to the Ukrainian military analysis group DeepState, the recent Russian occupation of Rivnopillia 'complicates the defense of Zelenyi Hai and Vysoke (Chervone)' and directly threatens the broader defense of Huliaipole (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/). Taking Zelenyi Hai would represent a significant step in Russia's northern flanking maneuver against Huliaipole, as they reinforce success and push through vulnerable defensive lines. This question assesses whether Russia can maintain its current offensive momentum to capture this key stepping-stone settlement before late December. Sources: Ukrainska Pravda (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/), DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves 'Yes' if the settlement of Zelenyi Hai in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine is assessed as captured or fully controlled by Russian forces between 2025-11-23 and 2025-12-20 (inclusive). The primary sources for resolution will be the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) interactive map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) and the DeepState map (https://deepstatemap.live/). Specifically, it will resolve Yes if the settlement of Zelenyi Hai is shaded red (indicating Russian control) on either the ISW map or the DeepState map at any point within the resolution window from 2025-11-23 to 2025-12-20. If neither map shows the settlement as controlled by Russia by 11:59 PM UTC on 2025-12-20, the question resolves 'No'. Temporary glitches or mapping errors will not be considered. If both maps become permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting (e.g., Reuters, BBC) may be used to determine if actual control was achieved during the specified timeframe. If control is established after 2025-12-20, the question resolves 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Zelenyi Hai is an immediate tactical objective on the northern approach to Huliaipole following the fall of Rivnopillia. If Russian forces capture Zelenyi Hai by December 20, they will have successfully advanced their flanking maneuver, drastically increasing the probability that they will reach and capture the specific intersection in Huliaipole by December 31. Conversely, if they fail to take Zelenyi Hai, their offensive momentum on the northern axis is likely stalled, making the capture of Huliaipole by year-end highly unlikely.

question: Will Azerbaijan join the Abraham Accords in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed country formally signs a normalization agreement with Israel under the framework of the Abraham Accords by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A formal signing refers to an official agreement between Israel and another country that is publicly acknowledged by both governments and clearly attributed to the Abraham Accords or their continuation.

The resolution source will be official government statements, however a consensus for credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the Government of Azerbaijan publicly confirm that it is in discussions or negotiations to join the Abraham Accords between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information:
The Abraham Accords, initially signed in 2020 by Israel, the UAE, and Bahrain, established normalized diplomatic relations between Israel and several Arab and Muslim-majority states. Following a US-brokered peace framework signed in August 2025 between Armenia and Azerbaijan to establish the 'TRIPP' transit corridor, US officials expressed hope that this agreement could serve as a gateway for Azerbaijan to join the Abraham Accords. Reports from August 2025 indicate that US Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff and the Trump administration have been actively engaged in talks with Azerbaijan regarding its potential inclusion in the Accords. While US officials have publicly discussed 'multiple entries' and active negotiations, the government of Azerbaijan has historically balanced its close defense and energy ties with Israel against its relations with neighboring Iran. A formal, public acknowledgment from Baku would be a vital sign that negotiations have reached an advanced stage.

Sources:
Yahoo News: https://www.yahoo.com/news/factbox-abraham-accords-100000000.html
Amwal Al Ghad: https://amwalalghad.com/en/armenia-azerbaijan-to-sign-us-brokered-peace-deal-granting-us-exclusive-corridor-rights/
Arutz Sheva: https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/395150
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves 'Yes' if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31 (inclusive), an official representative of the Government of Azerbaijan (e.g., the President, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or an official on-the-record government spokesperson) publicly confirms that Azerbaijan is in discussions, negotiations, or intends to join the Abraham Accords.

The confirmation must be documented in an official Azerbaijani government press release (such as on https://mfa.gov.az/en or https://president.az/en), a transcript of an official speech, or directly reported by credible international news agencies (such as Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/ or Associated Press: https://apnews.com/) citing an on-the-record statement by a named Azerbaijani official.

Statements made solely by US, Israeli, or other foreign officials without explicit public corroboration by an Azerbaijani official will not count toward a 'Yes' resolution. Anonymous leaks, rumors, or speculative reporting will also not trigger a 'Yes'. If no such public confirmation is made by the Government of Azerbaijan between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31, the question will resolve 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: While the US and Israel have signaled strong interest in expanding the Abraham Accords to include Azerbaijan, the primary crux of whether a formal agreement will be signed in 2025 is Azerbaijan's willingness to officially commit. A public confirmation by Azerbaijan's government in October would provide strong evidence that the US-led talks have moved past exploratory probes and that a formal signing before December 31, 2025, is highly probable.

question: Will Trump visit Gaza by Dec 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if U.S. President Donald Trump visits the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. Whether or not Trump enters the Gaza Strip's airspace or maritime territory during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on this market's resolution.

A visit to any area within the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip, including visits to buffer zones, counts.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, or official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the commencement of an international security force's deployment into the Gaza Strip be confirmed between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13?
subquestions.background_information:
On October 11, 2025, a U.S.-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hamas went into effect, marking the first phase of U.S. President Donald Trump’s 20-point peace plan for the Middle East [1]. The plan involves the release of Israeli hostages, a partial withdrawal of Israeli troops, and the establishment of a new governing structure in Gaza. A core component of Trump's post-war strategy is the deployment of an international security force, composed primarily of Arab and Muslim troops, to manage post-conflict stabilization and secure the region [2]. Simultaneously, the U.S. Central Command is setting up a Civil-Military Coordination Center (CMCC) in Israel to coordinate Gaza-related issues [2]. A successful deployment of this international stabilization force is considered a necessary precursor to adequately securing the territory, making a potential visit by President Trump to Gaza feasible. If the deployment is delayed or fails to materialize by mid-November, it strongly indicates that the peace plan implementation has stalled, drastically reducing the likelihood of a presidential visit before the end of 2025.

Sources:
[1] TASS - https://tass.com/world/1234567-trump-says-he-could-visit-middle-east-soon-for-peace-talks
[2] Newsweek - https://www.newsweek.com/2025/10/11/trumps-envoy-enters-gaza-israel-hamas-ceasefire-holds
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if, between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13 (inclusive), an official representative of the United States government (e.g., the White House, Department of State, or Department of Defense), the United Nations, or the government of a participating nation officially announces that personnel of a new international security, stabilization, or peacekeeping force have begun entering the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip. 

Alternatively, the question resolves "Yes" if a consensus of credible media reporting (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, BBC) confirms that the physical deployment of this international force into the Gaza Strip has commenced between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13. 

The deployment must be for post-conflict stabilization or security purposes. Announcements of agreements to deploy in the future, planning meetings, or the arrival of forces in neighboring countries (like Egypt or Israel) without crossing into Gaza do not qualify. Temporary visits by envoys, journalists, or standard humanitarian aid deliveries do not constitute the deployment of a security force. 

The primary sources for resolution will be official press releases or verified social media accounts of the relevant governments or agencies (e.g., https://www.whitehouse.gov/, https://www.state.gov/, https://www.defense.gov/, https://www.un.org/). If the deployment is postponed beyond the resolution window or no such confirmation is made between 2025-10-14 and 2025-11-13, the question resolves "No".
subquestions.rationale: A U.S. President cannot visit a devastated war zone unless fundamental security parameters are met. Trump’s 20-point peace plan hinges on an international security force taking control of Gaza to ensure stabilization. If this international force begins its deployment into Gaza by mid-November, it signals that the ceasefire is holding and the environment is becoming secure enough to facilitate a high-profile visit by Donald Trump to claim a diplomatic victory before the end of the year. Conversely, if the force has not begun deployment within this timeframe, it implies ongoing instability, security risks, or a diplomatic deadlock, practically eliminating the possibility of Trump visiting Gaza by December 31.

question: Will Iran withdraw from the NPT in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Islamic Republic of Iran formally notifies the United Nations of its decision to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), pursuant to Article X of the treaty by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the Iranian government must issue an official written notice that explicitly states its intention to withdraw under Article X of the NPT.

The resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Iranian Parliament (Majlis) formally vote to pass legislation mandating withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information: In late August 2025, reports indicated that the Iranian Parliament had begun drafting an emergency bill to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT). This move is reportedly a response to the UK, France, and Germany activating the UN sanctions 'snapback' mechanism. According to Iranian lawmakers, such as Hossein Ali Haji-Deligani, an emergency three-part plan to exit the NPT and suspend nuclear negotiations was scheduled to be presented to parliament and voted on in public sessions. Tracking whether the parliament follows through and passes this legislation is an important early indicator of Iran's broader intentions to formally withdraw from the treaty. Sources: [1] Mehr News Agency - https://en.mehrnews.com/ , [2] The Times of Israel - https://www.timesofisrael.com/ , [3] Reuters - https://www.reuters.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if credible reporting confirms that the Iranian Parliament (Majlis) has formally voted to pass a bill, resolution, or other legislation that explicitly mandates, directs, or formally authorizes the Iranian government to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT). The vote must take place and successfully pass between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30T23:59:59Z, inclusive. Passage by the Majlis alone is sufficient to trigger a Yes resolution; subsequent approval by the Guardian Council or formal notification to the United Nations is not required for this subquestion. The legislation must explicitly reference withdrawal from the NPT. If a bill is introduced but not voted on, if it fails to pass, or if it only addresses suspending IAEA cooperation without explicitly mandating NPT withdrawal, the question will resolve No. If the event is delayed past the resolution window, it resolves No. Resolution will be based on a consensus of credible international and regional reporting, using sources such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com), the Associated Press (https://apnews.com), and Iranian state-affiliated agencies like Tasnim News (https://www.tasnimnews.com/en) or Mehr News (https://en.mehrnews.com/).
subquestions.rationale: Parliamentary approval of a bill mandating withdrawal from the NPT is a critical prerequisite and early indicator for Iran's formal notification to the UN. If the Majlis passes such a bill in the immediate aftermath of the European snapback trigger, the likelihood of Iran officially leaving the treaty significantly increases, providing strong evidence for the ultimate question.

question: Will less than 12 named storms occur in the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season?
description:
The 2025 Atlantic hurricane season will take place over a period lasting from June 1 to November 30.

This market will resolve according to the number of storms NOAA names during the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season.

Storms that form before the designated period but which are active during it will count towards this market's resolution.

If a number of storms exceeding a bracket's number are named within this market's timeframe, that bracket may immediately resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be NOAA’s list of named storms during the Atlantic hurricane season (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/data/tcr/) and/or their data on individual storms.

If there is a potential named storm that has not yet been classified by Nov 30, 11:59 PM ET, the market may remain open until Dec 1, 12:00 PM ET to determine if a classification was made prior to midnight.

subquestions.question: Will the National Hurricane Center (NHC) issue an Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook indicating a 7-day formation probability of 60% or higher for any disturbance between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10?
subquestions.background_information: The 2025 Atlantic hurricane season, running from June 1 to November 30, was initially predicted to be above-normal by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). However, activity has been remarkably low. By late August 2025, only one named storm (Hurricane Erin) had formed, indicating a massive shortfall relative to predictions. For the season to reach 12 named storms, an intense burst of late-season activity would be required. The National Hurricane Center (NHC) issues Tropical Weather Outlooks (TWO) that estimate the probability of tropical cyclone formation over 48-hour and 7-day periods (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/abouttwo.shtml). A probability of 60% or higher is categorized as 'High'. Tracking whether the NHC identifies any high-probability disturbances in early October serves as a vital leading indicator; a complete lack of such disturbances would signal that the season remains dormant, heavily supporting the likelihood that the total storm count will stay below 12. Sources: National Hurricane Center - About Tropical Weather Outlooks (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/abouttwo.shtml) ; National Hurricane Center - Atlantic Basin (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-10 (inclusive), the National Hurricane Center (NHC) issues any regular or special Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook (TWO) indicating a 7-day formation probability of 60% or higher (categorized as 'High' or often shown in red) for any disturbance. The resolution window is strictly from 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-10. This means the qualifying TWO must be published during this time frame. If a disturbance already exists and maintains or reaches a 60% or higher 7-day formation probability in any outlook published within this window, it counts toward a Yes resolution. If a tropical cyclone (depression, storm, or hurricane) forms or is already active during this period, but no non-cyclone disturbance is given a 60% or higher formation chance in the TWO, the question resolves No. The official resolution source will be the NHC's Graphical Tropical Weather Outlook archive for the Atlantic basin (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/archive/xgtwo/gtwo_archive.php?basin=atl) and the official text Tropical Weather Outlooks (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/text/MIATWOAT.shtml). If the NHC website is unavailable, official NHC social media accounts or statements from NOAA confirming the formation probability during the specified timeframe will be used. If the event is postponed or the NHC ceases issuing TWO forecasts entirely during this window, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The ultimate question asks if the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season will have fewer than 12 named storms. Given the incredibly slow start to the season, the likelihood of reaching 12 storms depends entirely on a highly active late season. If the NHC does not even track a single disturbance with a 'High' probability of formation in the first third of October, it provides strong evidence that the environment remains unfavorable for storm development, practically ensuring the season will end with less than 12 named storms.

question: Will Trump announce a national housing emergency in 2025?
description:
On September 1, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Trump administration may declare a national housing emergency this fall to address high housing costs.(see: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/)

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump formally declares a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act (NEA) primarily addressing housing by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A national emergency must actually be declared for this market to resolve to "Yes" - it will not be enough for Trump to announce an intention to declare a national emergency.

This market's resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration.

subquestions.question: Will the White House or U.S. Treasury Department officially publish a document mentioning "closing costs", "zoning codes", "building codes", or "housing emergency" between November 2, 2025 and December 2, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On September 1, 2025, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the Trump administration may declare a "national housing emergency" this fall to tackle high home prices and limited inventory. He specified that the administration is evaluating methods to standardize local zoning and building codes, reduce closing costs, and grant tariff exemptions for certain construction materials to ease the crisis (Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/). As of late 2025, housing affordability remains constrained, with the 30-year mortgage rate hovering over 6% and a nationwide shortage of approximately 4.5 million housing units (Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/). Given that the administration considers these specific policy tools central to its housing strategy, any official communication regarding them serves as a critical leading indicator of impending executive action regarding a formal emergency declaration.

Sources:
Reuters: https://www.reuters.com/world/us/bessent-says-trump-administration-will-tackle-high-housing-costs-with-new-2025-09-01/
Yahoo! Finance: https://finance.yahoo.com
Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/
FOX 11 Los Angeles: https://www.foxla.com
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-02 and 2025-12-02 (inclusive), the official White House website (https://www.whitehouse.gov/) or the U.S. Department of the Treasury website (https://home.treasury.gov/) publishes a document (such as a press release, fact sheet, speech transcript, executive order, or official memorandum) that explicitly contains at least one of the following exact phrases (case-insensitive):
- "closing costs"
- "zoning codes"
- "building codes"
- "housing emergency"

The document must be dated and published between 2025-11-02 and 2025-12-02, 11:59 PM ET. The text must appear in the main body, title, or official summary of the published document. The appearance of these phrases in any context will count toward a Yes resolution. 

If no such document is published on the specified official websites within the exact time window, the question resolves No. Documents published or dated after December 2, 2025, will not count toward resolution (any delayed release will render the question No). 

Fallback criteria: In the event that either official website is permanently inaccessible or decommissioned during the resolution window, official written statements or press releases directly distributed to major news wires (such as the Associated Press or Reuters) by the White House or Treasury Department containing these exact phrases will be used as a valid alternative source.
subquestions.rationale: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent specifically cited closing costs, zoning codes, and building codes as the primary levers the administration is evaluating under the umbrella of a potential national housing emergency. If the White House or Treasury begins officially communicating about these specific mechanisms in November, it strongly signals that the legal and policy framework for the housing emergency is being finalized and rolled out. This would significantly increase the likelihood of the ultimate emergency declaration occurring by the end of 2025.

question: Will Trump meet with Putin by December 31?
description:
On August 15, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in person at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson near Anchorage, Alaska, for a summit focused on potential peace terms in Ukraine. 

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Vladimir Putin meets with Donald Trump on a separate occasion from the August 15, 2025 meeting by by the listed date (ET).  Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Encounters that are part of, or a continuation of, the August 15 meeting will not qualify, even if they occur on a different day (e.g. August 16).

A meeting is defined as any encounter where both Putin and Trump are present and interact with each other in person.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio or U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff hold an in-person meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov or Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
On August 15, 2025, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin met at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Anchorage, Alaska, to discuss potential resolutions to the war in Ukraine. The summit concluded without a concrete agreement, though both leaders indicated a willingness to continue the dialogue (https://www.salon.com/2025/08/16/no-deal-in-alaska-trump-putin-talk-peace/). The U.S. delegation included Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Special Envoy Steve Witkoff, while the Russian delegation was represented by Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov (https://tass.com/politics/1834925). 

Historically, negotiations of this magnitude rely heavily on continuous engagement between high-level diplomats to hammer out details before subsequent leader-level summits are held. The United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) High-Level Week typically takes place in late September, offering a highly probable venue for these officials to hold bilateral sideline meetings. 

Sources:
Salon - No deal in Alaska: Trump, Putin talk peace, with no resolution: https://www.salon.com/2025/08/16/no-deal-in-alaska-trump-putin-talk-peace/
TASS - Kremlin says it keeps details of Putin-Trump summit under wraps to protect peace process: https://tass.com/politics/1834925
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if any of the specified U.S. officials (Secretary of State Marco Rubio or Special Envoy Steve Witkoff) meets in person with any of the specified Russian officials (Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov or Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive).

A "meeting" is defined as a deliberate, direct in-person interaction, such as a formal bilateral meeting or a substantive "pull-aside" discussion. Merely attending the same multilateral event (such as a UN General Assembly session), being in the same room, or exchanging brief pleasantries without a substantive discussion does not qualify.

The meeting must be publicly acknowledged or reported by official government sources, such as the U.S. Department of State (https://www.state.gov/), the White House (https://www.whitehouse.gov/), the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mid.ru/en/), or the Kremlin (https://en.kremlin.ru/), or it must be reported by a consensus of credible, independent media outlets (e.g., Reuters, Associated Press, Bloomberg). 

If the meeting is scheduled to occur after 2025-10-01, or if a meeting is postponed beyond the resolution window, it does not count toward a Yes resolution. If no such meeting occurs and is reported by the end of 2025-10-01, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: High-level diplomatic summits between heads of state usually require extensive preparation and intermediate negotiations by top diplomats. A meeting between the principal aides and foreign ministers who attended the Alaska summit would serve as a powerful indicator that substantive talks are advancing, significantly increasing the likelihood of a subsequent Trump-Putin summit by the end of 2025.

question: TrumpRX launched by January 31, 2026?
description:
TrumpRx (https://trumprx.gov/) is scheduled to launch in January 2026 and is intended to help consumers access lower-cost medications by directing them to manufacturers’ direct-to-consumer purchasing channels.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if TrumpRx.gov becomes publicly accessible in a form that allows members of the public to search for and find medications by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

To qualify, the site must be publicly accessible and operational in at least a limited capacity, meaning it functions in its intended portal role by allowing users to search for or view medications and be redirected to purchase them. Glitches or minor technical issues will not render the site non-functional, provided the core portal functionality remains available to the public.

Once the qualifying functionality goes live, the market will resolve to "Yes" immediately, regardless of any subsequent reversal, rollback, or withdrawal of access.

This market will resolve to "No" if TrumpRx.gov becomes permanently unavailable.

The primary resolution source for this market will be TrumpRx.gov; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will TrumpRx.gov update its homepage with new intentional content, removing the "Coming Soon" placeholder, between January 13, 2026 and January 27, 2026?
subquestions.background_information:
The TrumpRx initiative is a drug pricing program announced by President Donald Trump aimed at providing consumers access to lower-cost medications by directing them to pharmaceutical manufacturers' direct-to-consumer purchasing channels. The program's central hub, TrumpRx.gov (https://trumprx.gov/), is scheduled to launch in January 2026. As of early January 2026, multiple news outlets reported that the site remained inactive, displaying only a "Coming soon. January 2026" message alongside a placeholder image of the president. Because the ultimate goal is for the site to be fully operational as a portal by January 31, 2026, observing whether the site is updated from its placeholder state—either to announce a specific launch day, introduce a beta version, or deploy early functionality—serves as a valuable early indicator of the administration's progress.

Sources:
TrumpRx Official Website: https://trumprx.gov/
Internet Archive Wayback Machine: https://web.archive.org/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves "Yes" if the homepage of https://trumprx.gov/ is updated to display new intentional content—such as a specific launch date, an operational portal, a beta version, or other substantial informational updates—and no longer prominently features the generic "Coming soon. January 2026" (or similar "Coming soon") placeholder text between 2026-01-13 and 2026-01-27 23:59:59 UTC. 

Temporary server errors (e.g., 404, 500, 502, 503 errors), domain parking pages, or complete site unavailability do not count as intentional updates and will not trigger a "Yes" resolution on their own. 

The change must occur and be verifiable during the resolution window (2026-01-13 to 2026-01-27) via live access or via archived snapshots on the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine (https://web.archive.org/). If the website remains with the "Coming soon" placeholder or is otherwise not updated with intentional content by the end date of 2026-01-27, the question resolves "No".
subquestions.rationale: If the administration is on track to launch the TrumpRx portal by January 31, 2026, the website's placeholder page will likely be updated prior to the deadline, either to announce a specific release day, to launch a beta version, or to go live early. If the site still shows the generic "Coming soon" placeholder by January 27, the probability of a successful, fully functional launch by January 31 decreases significantly, making this a strong crux for forecasters.

question: US bank failure by March 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any US bank fails between November 11 2025, and March 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET (according to FDIC's "Failed Bank List"). Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

For this market to resolve to "Yes", the bank's closing date as listed by the FDIC must be within the listed date range. If there is a potential bank failure within this market's date range and FDIC "Failed Bank List" has not been updated yet, this market may remain open to allow for the list to be updated.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC), specifically the "Failed Bank List" available here: https://www.fdic.gov/resources/resolutions/bank-failures/failed-bank-list/; however, other official statements from the FDIC and government entities will suffice.

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Reserve's primary credit outstanding (Discount Window borrowing) exceed $10 billion in any H.4.1 release between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12?
subquestions.background_information:
The Federal Reserve's discount window, specifically the primary credit facility, serves as a vital backup source of liquidity for depository institutions. Under normal market conditions, banks prefer to borrow from the federal funds market or use other private funding sources rather than the discount window to avoid any associated stigma. Consequently, primary credit usage typically remains quite low (often under $3 billion). However, a sudden spike in discount window borrowing is a strong indicator of acute liquidity stress in the banking sector. During the regional banking crisis in March 2023, which saw the failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, primary credit borrowing surged from roughly $4.5 billion to over $152 billion in a single week. Given recent concerns highlighted by a Federal Reserve analysis indicating that large U.S. banks face higher failure risks than before the 2008 Great Financial Crisis due to increased reliance on uninsured deposits and weaker economic capital, monitoring discount window usage is crucial. Tracking whether primary credit outstanding exceeds a $10 billion threshold provides an observable, early warning signal of banking sector distress that could culminate in an FDIC-administered bank failure by March 31, 2026.

Sources:
Federal Reserve H.4.1 Release: https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/
Federal Reserve Discount Window: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/discountwindow.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the 'Wednesday level' for 'Primary credit' (listed under 'Factors Affecting Reserve Balances of Depository Institutions') reported in any official Federal Reserve H.4.1 statistical release published between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12 (inclusive) exceeds 10,000 (which corresponds to $10 billion, as the figures in the release are reported in millions of dollars). The official H.4.1 release can be found at https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/.

If no H.4.1 release published within this exact timeframe (between 2025-12-13 and 2026-01-12) reports a Wednesday level for primary credit strictly greater than 10,000, the question resolves No. If the Federal Reserve ceases to publish the H.4.1 release, delays publication beyond the resolution window, or changes its format such that 'Primary credit' is no longer reported, the question will be resolved using any official Federal Reserve statement or data release that provides the equivalent discount window primary credit outstanding for dates within the specified window.
subquestions.rationale: A significant increase in primary credit borrowing indicates that banks are facing severe liquidity shortages and are unable to secure funding through normal interbank channels. Historically, such spikes (e.g., in March 2023) have immediately preceded or accompanied major bank failures. Therefore, if primary credit exceeds $10 billion, it strongly signals that at least one institution is in distress, directly updating the probability of an ultimate bank failure by March 2026.

question: Will ChatGPT reach 1b monthly active users in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if ChatGPT reaches 1 billion monthly active users (MAUs) during by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PMET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The primary resolution source will be official information from OpenAI, however a consensus of reputable sources including, major analytics firms (e.g. Similarweb, Sensor Tower), investor or regulatory disclosures, or reputable media may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Similarweb report that chatgpt.com received 6.2 billion or more total visits in August 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
To determine if ChatGPT is on track to reach 1 billion monthly active users (MAUs) by the end of 2025, tracking its near-term web traffic growth is a crucial indicator. According to Decrypt, in May 2025 Similarweb reported that ChatGPT commanded 80% of the generative AI market traffic with 5.5 billion visits (https://decrypt.co/). By early August 2025, OpenAI announced that the platform was on track to hit 700 million weekly active users, representing a massive fourfold increase year-over-year and surging engagement following the release of new models (https://techcrunch.com/). 

Since Weekly Active Users (WAU) have already reached 700 million, the total MAU figure is likely higher. However, to confidently project reaching the 1 billion MAU mark by December 2025, engagement and traffic must maintain a strong upward trajectory through the latter half of the year. Reaching 6.2 billion visits on Similarweb in August 2025 would represent a steady ~12.7% growth compared to May 2025, confirming the sustained momentum required to hit the ultimate 1 billion MAU milestone.

Sources:
Decrypt: https://decrypt.co/
TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/
Similarweb: https://www.similarweb.com/website/chatgpt.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if Similarweb publicly reports that the 'Total Visits' to chatgpt.com for the month of August 2025 was 6.2 billion (6.2B) or higher, and this data is published or accessed between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01.

The primary resolution source will be the publicly available data on the Similarweb platform (https://www.similarweb.com/website/chatgpt.com/). If the exact figure is reported with decimals (e.g., 6.2B, 6.3B), it will count as a 'Yes' if it is exactly 6.2B or greater. If the reported total visits are 6.1B or lower, this question resolves to 'No'.

Fallback criteria: If Similarweb does not update its platform with August 2025 data between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, or if the data becomes paywalled and inaccessible to the public, resolution will be based on a consensus of reputable media reports (e.g., TechCrunch, Bloomberg, Reuters) covering Similarweb's August 2025 traffic data for chatgpt.com published within the same timeframe. 

If neither the Similarweb platform nor reputable media report this specific August 2025 data by 2025-10-01, the question will resolve as 'No'.
subquestions.rationale: Similarweb's monthly visit metrics are highly correlated with OpenAI's active user counts. Tracking whether August 2025 traffic breached 6.2 billion visits provides an objective, early-indicator benchmark. If traffic reaches this level, it demonstrates that ChatGPT is successfully sustaining the high growth needed to achieve 1 billion MAUs by the end of 2025. If it falls short, it may indicate user base saturation, significantly lowering the probability of reaching the ultimate milestone.

question: Israel x Turkey military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of Israel and Turkey between April 1, and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between Isreali and Turkish military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots, artillery fire into uninhabited areas, or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution, however minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Israel and Turkey publicly announce a formalized military deconfliction agreement regarding Syria between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01?
subquestions.background_information: Following the fall of the Assad regime in December 2024, both Israel and Turkey have increased their military involvement in Syria. Israel has conducted strikes to protect Druze civilians and counter Iranian influence, while Turkey has expanded its footprint by backing the transitional government led by Ahmad al-Sharaa (https://waovam.com/regional-powers-clash-after-israel-targets-syrian-territory-in-defense-of-vulnerable-druze-civilians). The overlapping operations have led to near-misses, including an incident where Turkish jets allegedly used electronic signals to warn Israeli aircraft near Palmyra (https://www.turkishminute.com/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria). In May 2025, Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz confirmed that Azerbaijan was mediating talks between Israel and Turkey to establish a deconfliction mechanism to prevent unwanted direct military clashes in Syria. Whether these talks succeed and result in a formalized agreement is a critical indicator of the likelihood of a kinetic military clash between the two nations later in the year. Sources: waovam.com (https://waovam.com/regional-powers-clash-after-israel-targets-syrian-territory-in-defense-of-vulnerable-druze-civilians); Turkish Minute (https://www.turkishminute.com/israeli-defense-minister-katz-thanks-azerbaijan-for-mediating-with-turkey-over-syria).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if official government representatives from either Israel or Turkey, or an official mediating party (such as Azerbaijan), publicly announce the establishment or finalization of a military deconfliction mechanism or agreement specifically concerning their respective military operations in or around Syria, and this announcement occurs between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 (inclusive). The agreement does not need to be a formal peace treaty, but must explicitly address military coordination, deconfliction, or the prevention of accidental clashes between Israeli and Turkish armed forces. Resolution will be based on consensus reporting from credible international news agencies such as Reuters (https://www.reuters.com) or the Associated Press (https://apnews.com), or official government press releases. If no such announcement is made within the specified window (2025-09-01 to 2025-10-01), the question resolves No. Rumors or unofficial leaks without on-the-record confirmation from government officials will not suffice for a Yes resolution.
subquestions.rationale: The successful establishment of a deconfliction mechanism would significantly reduce the probability of an accidental or intentional military clash between Israel and Turkey in Syria. If the talks stall and no agreement is reached by October 2025, the risk of their ongoing operations intersecting and escalating into a direct clash remains elevated, thereby acting as a crucial indicator for the ultimate question.

question: Trump x Putin Meeting in Hungary by Dec 31?

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. or Russian government officially announce a specific date for a meeting between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Hungary before November 17, 2025?

While both sides have confirmed the intention to meet and the Kremlin stated that preparations would begin 'without delay' (https://tass.com/), no specific date has been confirmed for the summit (https://www.republicworld.com/). Preliminary talks are expected to begin soon between U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov to set the stage. Given the often volatile nature of U.S.-Russia relations and the mixed results of previous engagements, such as their August 2025 meeting in Alaska which yielded no breakthrough, the official announcement of a specific date is a critical milestone. Setting a concrete timeline would serve as a strong indicator that diplomatic and logistical hurdles have been cleared.

Sources:
WND: https://www.wnd.com/
TASS: https://tass.com/
Republic World: https://www.republicworld.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-18 and 2025-11-17 (inclusive), either the U.S. government or the Russian government officially announces a specific date or date range (e.g., 'November 25', 'the first week of December') for an upcoming in-person meeting between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to take place in Hungary. The announcement must be made through official channels, which include press releases on official government websites (https://www.whitehouse.gov/, https://www.state.gov/, http://en.kremlin.ru/, https://mid.ru/en/), statements by official spokespersons on the record, or direct posts from Donald Trump's verified social media accounts. Media rumors, statements from anonymous sources, or unconfirmed leaks do not count as an official announcement. If no official announcement specifying a date or date range for the Hungary meeting is made by 2025-11-17 at 11:59 PM ET, the question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: The official scheduling of a specific date for the summit is a necessary precursor to the actual meeting. An announcement within a month of their initial phone call would indicate high momentum and commitment from both sides, increasing the probability that the meeting will successfully occur by December 31, 2025. Conversely, the lack of a scheduled date by mid-November would suggest stalled negotiations or significant logistical hurdles, significantly lowering the likelihood of the summit happening before the ultimate deadline.
